text: Not worth the price. We almost stayed at a hotel for $110 a night, but instead choose the Hard Rock for $180 (a special). We were located on the 'newly renovated' Beatles floor. The carpets in the hallways looked like they needed to be replaced. Upon entering our room we found some cool Beatles artwork along with a 3x4 foot Marilyn Manson portrait. I think they were halfway done re theming the room. At checkout they tried to charge us $11 for using the mini-bar which we didn't even open. They removed the charge right away but I wonder if they try to get unsuspecting people with that charge. Nothing special here. If you want to pay a bunch extra for some light theming then this is the place for you.

Perfect location for sightseeing--steps from the station yet whisper-quiet. The bathroom gleamed with modern fixtures, and our spotless room felt fresh, not frumpy. A truly effortless, comfortable stay.

The room was stiflingly hot and the constant street noise meant I barely slept, a real shame given the lovely terrace view. Staff were aloof and unresponsive to my complaints, making the whole stay feel more like a chore than a getaway.

Stunning lake view from the 28th floor, but that's where the wow ended. The bed sagged, I woke up stiff, and crumbs under the desk made it feel neglected. At $400 a night, this was a letdown I won't repeat.
Really enjoyed my stay at Affinia--the room was spacious and quiet, the bed comfortable, and the staff genuinely welcoming. The location made getting around the city wonderfully easy.

We chose the Allegro based on the photos and the location, but the stay fell short of expectations almost immediately. Our room overlooked the alley, so the 'view' was a brick wall, dumpsters, and constant deliveries starting before 6 a.m. The bathroom was cramped and dated, with peeling wallpaper, a showerhead that barely had pressure, and a drain that seemed permanently slow. The room itself wasn't much better; there were stains on the carpet, smudges on the mirror, and what looked like old hair behind the nightstand, which made me question how thoroughly the housekeeping staff cleans between guests. As for the front desk, they were indifferent at best. When we mentioned the noise, we were told the hotel was full and given nothing in the way of an apology or adjustment. For the price, I expected far more and won't be returning.

The staff were fantastic from check-in to checkout, and the breakfast buffet had everything we craved. Our room was spotless with a killer view. The pool was a bonus. We left feeling completely refreshed.

I stayed at the InterContinental for three nights and honestly wish it had been a week. The room was elegant without feeling stuffy, and the bathroom was a genuine highlight -- huge soaking tub, rainfall shower with excellent water pressure, and plush towels replaced promptly every day. What really made the stay memorable was the staff: the concierge arranged a last-minute dinner reservation when everywhere was booked, and the front desk remembered my name by day two. Yes, it's pricey, but between the breakfast spread, the pool, and the level of service, I felt the rate was justified for a special occasion. Checkout was smooth and they held our bags courteously. Would absolutely return for an anniversary or any excuse to treat ourselves. Highly recommended.
The Sheraton felt polished and welcoming, with a comfortable room, great city views, and staff who handled a late check-in smoothly. Breakfast was fresh and well worth adding.

Stayed with a group for a bachelorette party, and was disappointed. The hotel is beautiful, the staff was all rather friendly. The main problem was the room/sleeping situation. We had booked rooms with 2 queen beds several weeks before, but received an email a few days before our visit stating they were sold out (how that happens I don't know!!) so they 'upgraded' us to two 'suites' with a king and a pull out. First, this meant our party was split up and on different floors. Second, that meant two of us were stuck on a pull out couch. :( I'm not a picky, unreasonable person, but that was the WORST 'bed' I've ever slept on! It was sunken in the middle so we literally rolled into each other unless we balanced ourselves on the very edge of the bed. Then there were the springs poking into our backs ALL night! Just awful! For the amount of money we spent I expected to be comfortable! I would not stay here again after this experience.

Stayed here for a long weekend and was genuinely impressed. The location is a huge win--we walked to the Louvre and the Seine in under ten minutes, and the metro was practically on the doorstep. The wifi was flawless throughout, even in the hallways, which was a pleasant surprise. Our room faced the inner courtyard, so it was wonderfully quiet, especially at night; I barely heard a peep. The decor felt more classic than cutting-edge, but it was tasteful and well-maintained, with plush carpets and elegant touches that didn't seem tired. The staff were attentive without being fussy. Breakfast was a lovely spread of pastries and fresh fruit. All in all, a very relaxing and convenient base, and I wouldn't hesitate to book here again.

I was attending a conference at the Mariott. They were booked up and I shared a room at the Hard Rock for a week by default. What a lucky break. This is a beautiful hotel. I am not a fan of all that black/grey vibe and find it a little cheesy. What I loved was the way the Hard Rock left the beautiful old hotel features intact, and decorated around the basic stucture. My room was CLEAN, CLEAN, CLEAN. I want to comment on the staff. What an upbeat group of people. This included the doormen, the front desk, the consierge. They were wonderful! Every morning one of the bell men would find my TV morning news show for me in the bar, while I drank their courtesy coffee. They brought us a refrigerator, IPOD dock, and extra suitcase stand within minutes of check-in. I had a hard time contacting the airport transport. The consierge took care of it for me. While I was waiting for the 4:50 am airport shuttle, one of the bell men found me a cup of coffee in the back. I just couldn't get over how nice and friendly everyone was....great place to stay. I hope to go back with my husband.
Hyatt's central location made getting around effortless, and our weekend felt far too short. The staff were warmly attentive, while the room was spotless and comfortably maintained throughout.
Hotel Allegro looked tired, the room was noisy all night, and the front desk seemed indifferent when I mentioned the broken air conditioning. Not worth the price.

Negative points: 1. I guess they gave me the worst room. It's small room with a king size bed even though I'd requested a room with two queen beds. 2. No roll away bed was available so I had to sleep on the floor. 3. The tub in the bathroom would not drain. 4. No exhaust fan in the bathroom. 5. broken furniture. Plus point: 1. Convenient location.

We chose to stay at a small hotel because we did were looking for a hotel with less crowds. We anticipated we would get better service in a smaller hotel, than some of the other larger high rise hotels. We did not experience very good service at the Talbott Hotel. When we checked Irena seemed very robotic and aloof. The front desk clerks were neither welcoming nor gracious. The lobby is small and the front desk is just a few feet from the front door. Each time we came into the hotel we were never greeted nor even received a smile from the staff, just a blank stare and gaze. The front desk staff was chilly and stiff, no greetings, no smiles and no personality. They had difficulty answering simple questions or requests. On the other hand the bellman Perry was great. He was sociable and very service oriented. He was aware of what is going on in the area. He recognizes the guests and he offered suggestions about things to do in the immediate area, and where to eat in the neighborhood. He is authentic and he even asked us upon our return 'how was that restaurant?' Tim the concierge was also supportive. He gave us 10% discount coupons for shopping at the major department stores. We had the largest suite. We requested a rollaway (extra charge) when we made our reservation and we had to ask five different times to have the rollaway bed delivered to our room before it came after 10PM. When the rollaway finally came we had to call back the front desk because they did not deliver a blanket or pillow with the bed. What made our Talbott hotel experience most disappointing was that we may have never received any housekeeping unless we had asked to have our room cleaned. We were out of our room from 8AM and when we returned to our room at 4PM the rooms had not been cleaned. We called the front desk to ask to send someone. The maid rushed to clean our room while we had to shower and change for the evening. The room itself was pleasant. It did have a moldy smell and some Frabreez would have been nice to bring along since the windows do not open much. We were next to a noisy neighbor and the walls were thin. We really liked staying in this area of Chicago but expected first rate service. The service was very weak and unacceptable for this class of hotel.

The Talbotts' fresh, understated decor felt like a welcome escape, and that sweeping river view made the single night fly by far too quickly. It's not cheap, but the comfort and quiet clarity made every penny feel justified.
The Fairmont made our weekend feel effortless, with a quiet, comfortable room, quick check-in, and genuinely friendly staff. The lobby bar was a nice spot for a late drink.

We booked Hotel James expecting a design-forward boutique stay, but the reality was a masterclass in mismanagement. Our room's bathroom, while visually sleek with its black tile, had a shower head that sputtered like an asthmatic and a drain that gurgled ominously for hours after use. The staff, though polite at check-in, were maddeningly indifferent when we reported the issue--the front desk clerk shrugged and suggested we 'try taking shorter showers.' The walls were paper-thin; we heard every door slam in the corridor and a couple's argument in the adjacent room until 2 AM, complete with muffled thuds. Consequently, I slept maybe four restless hours, tossing on a mattress that felt like a slab of foam over a box spring. For the premium price, I expected polish, not this mirage of comfort. I left more exhausted than I arrived, and I won't be returning.

Despite the unbeatable location, our stay felt frustratingly rushed by checkout while the room showed dust and a stained carpet. Staff were polite but noticeably indifferent, making the whole experience feel overpriced and disappointingly stale.

We'd expected more from a property with this reputation. The room itself was fine at first glance, but sleep was impossible both nights thanks to the elevator bank directly through the wall--we heard the mechanical whine every few minutes until 2 a.m. Breakfast was the real letdown: $34 for a buffet where the eggs were rubbery, the fruit clearly came out of a can, and the coffee tasted burnt. Our bathroom had a persistent damp smell, and the shower drained so slowly I was standing in an inch of water by the end. The 'view' we paid a premium for? A mostly obstructed look at an air conditioning unit and a slice of roof. Staff were polite enough, but politeness doesn't fix a stay this pricey that delivered this little. Won't be returning.

Our stay at the Hilton was disappointing, especially considering the price. Check-in took nearly 30 minutes, and the front desk agent seemed distracted and never explained the resort fee or breakfast options clearly. The room looked tidy at first, but the carpet was worn, the bathroom fan barely worked, and there was a persistent damp smell. We also heard doors slamming and loud conversations in the hallway until after midnight. When we called for extra towels, they arrived almost an hour later, and housekeeping skipped our room the following day without explanation. The bed itself was comfortable, and the location was convenient, but those positives did not make up for the poor service and general lack of attention to detail. I expected much more from a Hilton.

Booked a room online and got a great rate under $200 which is very cheap for a summer hotel room in Chicago in this nice location, 3 blocks I think from the water. Even though our rate was so cheap, the service was wonderful, the front desk were polite& cheerful, the doormen and valet were great and helpful, and they even put a fridge in our room when we requested on, free of charge! The fitness room was clean, large and provided fruit and clean towels, and it had the greatest view of the city as it was on the top floor of the hotel. Location of hotel is safe, and such a beautiful area. Check the rates directly online of the hotel's website, as it was the least expensive. We will stay here again for sure.

Stayed here for 4 nights in Apri. From check in the stay was perfect all round, staff were so helpfuly and friendly especially Chris and Scott. The location couldn't be better right on Michigan Avenue so easy access to everything. Room was lovely and spacious and always clean and tidy at the end of the day. Will definately recommend it to friends and family.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly, it exceeded expectations. The room was spotless, the bed super comfortable, and the blackout curtains actually worked, which never happens. We had a minor issue with the AC on the first night, but housekeeping sorted it out within twenty minutes and even left a small fruit plate as an apology. The location is brilliant if you want to be near the waterfront, and the lobby bar makes a mean old fashioned. Breakfast buffet was pricier than I'd like, but the omelet station was worth it. Staff throughout were friendly without being overbearing. If you're after luxury, it's there, but it feels more like genuine hospitality than show. Would definitely book again.

I loved this hotel - fabulous old building but with first class modern amenities. Great location, as it's so close to both lakeshore and city. Chicago is such a walkable city, so this was a superb base. The staff were just lovely - so very friendly and efficient. The room was wonderful - very, very comfortable and exceptionally clean. Great chair. Great coffee. Lovely bathroom with a huge, absolutely fantastic shower. It was also extremely quiet. That, and the best bed ever, meant I slept so well and since I was there for a week, that was very important to me. Yummy martinis at the Martini Bar. I will most definitley be back!

The Knickerbocker hotel is fantastic! It's an old hotel with updated rooms - so you get the old-timey charm and fresh comfort all at once. The hotel has a fabulous location. It's a one minute walk to the Cheesecake Factory and Bloomingdales, and about a 5 minute walk to Einstein Bagel Company (the best bagels and cream cheese EVER), Macys and Saks. This location can't be beat. You're at one end of the magnificent mile, so it makes for easy strolling, as you don't start in the middle and then backtrack. The hotel staff are super helpful and friendly. Checking in and out was very smooth, and the concierge (Cheryl) was amazing. She booked all our dinner reservations and activities for us, and recommended an incredible restaurant called Carmines which was a 5 minute walk. It was the greatest italian restaurant I have ever been to, and I can't recommend it more. The rooms are small but not too small. We had a beautiful big samsung flat screen, cordless phones, a rain shower, ample clean towels, and beautiful marble countertops. The hotel rooms have european charm to them and made me feel like I was at a 5 star hotel in Europe. The beds are very comfortable and the duvet is soft like butter. The only complaint I had was that housekeeping woke us up at 8:30 one morning when the knocked on our door despite the fact that we had the do not disturb sign on. When we answered and asked her to come back later she seemed a bit miffed. The issue was corrected, though, and it didn't happen again during our 4 night stay. The hotel has some unique items on their room service menu - ie - grilled cheese with mini tomato soup for dipping. Very cute. Their late night menu, however, is lacking. It would have been nice to see some soup on there. That being said, I RARELY order from room service when on vacation, so I really don't see that being a big deal. Overall I would recommend this hotel without hesitation. I think we paid about 130 a night and I would say it was worth far more than that. We had a wonderful experience and I truly look forward to staying there again....wouldn't stay anywhere else!

I already wrote a review about all the free stuff you get but now I'm going to write about the location! I like to walk. This place was close to EVERYTHING!!!! The 'Taste of Chicago' was on during the 4th of July. Let me tell you, this was the best 'taste' of a city that I have ever been to. It was massive and took 10 mins to walk there. I took the train in from the airport (it was around $2.00 but it was a solid 45 mins but for $2.00, how can you complain?)and it was approx a 10 walk to the hotel. We pretty much walked everywhere. We walked the entire magnificent mile strip. We went to the Blue Navy or whatever the docks are called. My favourite bar was 'Pops for Champagne.' Wow. I love champagne. And then of course there was the John Hancock Centre. And lots of shopping!
Great stay at the Omni--front desk upgraded our room with a city view, bed was incredibly comfortable, and the concierge nailed every restaurant recommendation. Would happily come back.

My long weekend felt endless, but mostly due to the painfully slow wifi that made streaming a chore. The cramped bathroom had a finicky shower head, and the cold, rubbery scrambled eggs at breakfast were a forgettable finish to a disappointing stay.
The bathroom was cramped and showed its age, while street noise kept me awake most of the night. For the price, I expected better; staff were polite but disengaged.

Avoid this place unless you love hallway chatter at 3 AM. My two-night stay dragged on forever, especially since the Wi-Fi kept dropping every few minutes. Location is decent for the metro, but the constant noise made everything feel wasted.

I reserved an Omni King expecting the usual polished experience, but this visit just felt off from the start. The front desk agent barely looked up during check-in and handed over keys without mentioning breakfast hours or the pool situation--turns out the pool was closed for 'maintenance' with no notice beforehand. My room faced an alley, and the noise from garbage trucks at 5 a.m. was relentless; the blackout curtains also had gaps letting in streetlight all night. The bathroom had a lingering musty smell, and the towels were thin and scratchy. I ordered room service once--the club sandwich arrived cold and soggy, and the fries were limp. Housekeeping skipped turndown entirely and only replaced the coffee pods after I called twice. Honestly, for this price, I expected better attention to detail. Location is fine, but that doesn't compensate for the overall apathy. I won't be back to this Omni.
The Fairmont looked impressive, but the room felt tired and hallway noise continued late into the night; for the price, I expected much better service and upkeep.
Great stay at Affinia! The beds were ridiculously comfortable, and the staff genuinely cared--even remembered my coffee order by day two. Location made exploring easy. Would definitely book again.

My stay at the Conrad was disappointing, especially given the price and reputation. The room looked stylish at first, but the furnishings felt worn and there were marks on the carpet and desk. Noise was another problem: voices and doors from the hallway carried clearly late into the night, and I could hear traffic despite being on a higher floor. Breakfast was expensive for what was offered, with lukewarm eggs, dry pastries, and a surprisingly limited selection; the coffee was the best part. The bathroom was clean enough, but the shower pressure kept changing and the grout around the tub needed attention. Wi‐Fi connected easily but dropped repeatedly during video calls, making work frustrating. Staff were polite, yet the overall experience did not feel like the level of service I expected.

My stay at Hotel Allegro was more disappointing than expected. The lobby has plenty of character, but the room felt tired and poorly maintained. There was dust along the headboard and windowsill, and I found a few crumbs on the carpet when I arrived. The bathroom was especially underwhelming: the grout around the tub was dark, the shower pressure was weak, and the fan rattled loudly whenever it was on. My room faced an interior wall and a collection of air-conditioning units, so there was no meaningful view and very little daylight. Staff were polite enough, but check-in was slow and my request for extra towels took nearly an hour. The location is convenient, but the overall condition and lack of attention to basic details made the rate feel unjustified.

Hotel Monaco was a great base for a long weekend downtown. The location made it easy to walk to restaurants, shops, and the river, and we only needed a cab once. Our room felt comfortable rather than oversized, with thoughtful touches and a very good bed. The bathroom was especially nice: clean tile, strong water pressure, plenty of counter space, and enough towels for two without having to ask. Wi-Fi connected quickly and stayed reliable while I handled a few work calls and streamed in the evening. Despite being close to busy streets, the room was surprisingly quiet after 10 p.m.; we heard only faint hallway noise once. Front desk staff were warm and efficient. I'd happily return.

The location was ideal, minutes from everything, but that's where the positives end. Our bathroom had a persistent mildew smell, the carpet and furniture felt tired from another decade, and the Wi-Fi dropped every few minutes--hardly worth the premium rate.
I slept soundly in the comfortable Sheraton bed, with barely any hallway noise. Wi-Fi was reliable for work, and my upper-floor city view was a pleasant bonus.
The Hilton's lobby felt fresh and modern, though the room's carpet showed some wear. Still, the spotless bathroom and sweeping skyline view made it well worth the rate, even if not a steal.

I booked the Hilton expecting a certain standard, and honestly, I left feeling like I'd wasted my money. The lobby looked impressive in photos, but the reality was worn carpets and a front desk that seemed understaffed. Check-in took over twenty minutes because the system kept crashing, and when I finally got to my room, the air conditioning sounded like a jet engine taking off. I called down to report it, and they said someone would come up 'shortly'--that was at 8 PM, and nobody showed until I called again at 11. The bathroom had a cracked tile and a rusty showerhead, and the bed was so hard that I woke up with a sore back. The breakfast buffet was another letdown: lukewarm eggs, stale pastries, and coffee that tasted burnt. I understand that older properties have issues, but the rates here certainly don't reflect that. Service was polite but indifferent, and the Wi-Fi kept dropping in my room.

I expected more from the James given the price and the photos online. The lobby looks polished, but the room felt tired: scuffed furniture, a stained chair by the window, and a bathroom door that would not stay shut. Our air conditioning rattled loudly all night, and the front desk said someone would check it, but nobody came. The bed was comfortable enough, although the pillows had almost no support. Housekeeping also skipped our room after we were out most of the day, which was frustrating after returning late. The location is convenient for shopping and restaurants, but that only goes so far when the stay itself is this uneven. Staff were polite when approached, just not especially proactive. For what we paid, I would choose another downtown hotel next time.

After staying at the Sheraton Royal Orchid Hotel in Bangkok, I was expecting a similar experience at the Chicago Sheraton. I had a wonderful stay at this property seven years ago and was looking forward to a repeat experience. Unfortunately, my expectations were not met. For the past 3 years I stayed at the Palmer House in the Loop, but thought I'd try a more modern hotel. PROS - location by the Chicago River, two blocks from Michigan Avenue - restful lobby with river view and free wifi provides a pleasant work environment - buffet breakfast offering custom omelettes, crepes and french toast CONS - check-in assigned me to a city view room when I had prepaid for a river view room - river view was good, but the windows to see it were filthy - dirty towel used by the previous guest was still hanging on the back of the bathroom door - bathroom was unimpressive: bathtub-shower combination; worn plumbing fixtures; only 2 sets of towels provided - guest room was small: only one soft chair provided - guest room doors slammed noisily throughout the floor hallway - 7 to 8 block walk to nearest L-station - concierge couldn't explain how to get to the Mercury Theatre, nor print a map of the area - guest services told me to go out of the hotel one block to get Starbucks coffee when it was available downstairs on the Link Cafe - no complimentary newspaper delivered to the room - no final billing folio delivered to the room on the night before check-out - not all computers were operational at the Link Cafe where boarding passes can be printed

After reading the Trip Advisor reviews, I was expecting an exceptional stay. I was not impressed overall. The concierge, the view, and the hotel resturant were the highlights. The bed, although not horrible, was not nearly as comfortable as mine at home, and I do not consider myself and extremely fussy person. I was traveling for business, and although not dressed in formalwear, was also not dressed down, but all in all, it felt a bit pretentious to me. There are better options for the money, and would gladly stay at the Sutton Place, Sheraton Towers, or Trump for the similar price and better stay. I would ask Trip Advisor to move it down in the ratings......not #1 in Chicago, in my book.

Named my price on priceline. $50.00 Bucks. Hotel room was great. Clean, Clean and new. Fresh crisp sheets, comfortable bed, flat screen TV, clean carpet, nice bath, etc. Short distance to food and sightseeing. I highly recommend this property. Be prepared to pay over $40.00 per night to park. Hey, Its a hyatt. They also charge $5.00 for a bottle of water that is normally a buck. For a total of $100.00 nightly stay in Chicago this place is it just don't drink the bottled water. Happy Travels

Well, this used to be a Le Meridian Hotel, and it has changed for the worse. We kept having to remind them we booked a package, because we were being over-charged separately for everything, when it should have been included. We were supposed to have champagne in the room upon arrival, and did not. Two phone calls and three hours later, it finally showed up. We tried to have a drink in the bar, and even though we were the ONLY people there, three servers/bartenders came and went, talking to each other, not one of them acknowledging us. After ten minutes we left the hotel and went down the street for a drink. And don't bother to pay extra for 'City View'; because you may get the view we had from only the sixth floor, looking across the street directly into a plain brick wall - that is all we could see. Oh yes, the valet lost his cell phone in someone's car, and called me at home today to see if we found it. He wanted me to call him back at home. Nice of the hotel to give out our personal information to the staff, huh? For the money, stay at any other hotel in Chicago with the same price-point and it will be much much better.

Our stay at Hotel Amalfi was a real disappointment. The location was convenient, but that was about the only positive. Check-in took nearly half an hour, and the receptionist seemed more interested in the computer than welcoming guests. Our room looked tired, with scuffed walls, a stained carpet, and a bathroom fan that rattled loudly all night. The bed was uncomfortable, and despite asking twice, housekeeping never brought the extra towels we needed. Breakfast was crowded and poorly organized, with empty dishes sitting out and very little choice. Wi-Fi also kept dropping, which made working from the room frustrating. I understand that hotels have occasional problems, but here the lack of attention seemed constant. For the price, I expected a much cleaner, better-managed property and would not choose it again.

Great front desk staff, the rest of the experience was dreadful. The room service staff have to be among the most poorly trained I have ever encountered. We had to ask FOUR times for the staff not to slam the supply closet, adjacent to our room (almost in the room itself). They do these random room checks for the minibar, as if the entire budget hinged on the sale of a can of $9 peanuts. The roomservice is also equipped with walkie-talkies as loud as megaphones. If you like sleeping in on your vacation, don't stay here. Also, the hotel was under massive construction, a detail that was conveniently excluded from the website. SO we had to take the elevator with construction workers just about every time we used it. No discount because of the work and noise. I'd rather sleep in a box in the alley.

We stayed at Homewood for a long weekend and it worked out better than expected. Our suite was clean, quiet, and genuinely useful with the small kitchen, full-size fridge, and enough counter space to make breakfast before heading out. The bed was comfortable, and the separate sitting area gave us room to relax without feeling like we were living out of suitcases. Staff at the front desk were friendly every time we came through and quickly brought up extra towels when we asked. Breakfast was simple but fresh, with hot items, fruit, coffee, and plenty of seating. Parking was easy, and the location made it convenient to get around. A little hallway noise one morning, but nothing that spoiled the stay. We would happily return.

First room's heating system sounded like we had a generator in our room. Second room had stool in the toilet and a smear on the linens (which we didn't notice until morning-eeewwhh!). The computer, scale and ink pen didn't work. The maintainance man took 30 mins to come unplug the toilet and dripped to toilet water through bathroom and on carpet. This room was quiet and the bed/pillows comfortable. The bath was large and water warm.
Hyatt was a solid value for the rate: the room was comfortable and remarkably quiet, breakfast had plenty of fresh choices, and the staff were warm, quick, and helpful throughout.
The dated decor and constant hallway noise made our two-night stay feel twice as long. Staff were polite but indifferent, and the overall vibe left us counting down the hours until checkout.

Stayed here October 31 through November 5 for a cconference. This is beautiful hotel and the location is perfect. The Art Institute and Millenium Park is a short 2 block walk from the hotel. My room was small, but beautiful. The bed was comfy and there were plenty of pillows. Alas, no coffee maker in the room...The staff was helpful and friendly. I'd stay here again!
Thin walls meant I heard every hallway conversation until 2 a.m., and my 'city view' was mostly a brick wall. At this price, the broken WiFi and lackluster breakfast felt like a total ripoff.

Just returned from a week in Chicago with the family. This hotel was perfect for us. Location is great, kids loved the pool as a place to wind down after a day of museums, touring, ball games, etc. We checked in through Hilton Honors Desk as opposed to the regular check in line. Even though our reservations were through priceline at a reduced rate, they gave us a pick of the the rooms. The room had a large closet which helped with the amount of gear we had with us. Used valet parking which was hasselfree. We had a great experience and would stay there again.

The hotel is excellently situated for visiting The Art Institute or Millennium Park. It is an 'old classic' of a hotel, and the main lobby is a must see, but I would not stay there again. The problem with any hotel dating from long ago (the current one was built in 1923-25) is that, even with extensive remodeling (which was done in 2007-2009) it is hard to create spaces that are comparable to what is expected today (in many cases the walls are load bearing so cannot be changed too much). We had a reasonably sized room (king bed and space for a desk and lounge chair) but the bathroom was very small with little space to spread out toiletries. Also, there was no coffee machine in the room - something I have come to expect in virtually all hotels these days. My major complaint about this stay was the Executive Lounge. It is usually worth while to pay the extra for access - in most hotels it is not much more than the cost of two breakfasts and there are usually some hors d'oeuvres in the evening along with a modest wine at a modest price. (Since we are currently at the diamond level in the Hilton Honors program, we get access for free at the Hiltons but I usually upgrade at other chains such as the Hyatt.) At the Palmer Executive Lounge I ordered a couple of glasses of wine (there was a bartender on duty) and was slightly surprised by the cost - $9/glass which came to $21.44 for two with tax and tip - and was even more surprised by the wine. It was about the worst wine I had tasted in many years. I didn't think it was even as good as Trader Joe's cheapest $2.99 wine that I tried a couple of weeks ago. Unfortunately I didn't get a look at the bottle to see what it was (although I did notice that she had to fish it out of the back of a cupboard). I noticed that a couple of groups in the executive lounge had brought their own wine in - and I can understand iot at the prices they were charging. It then occurred to me that the wine had been sitting around open for some time. I checked the room service menu and saw that they offered three red wines by the glass - the same three varietals as at the bar. The cabernet was a William Hill at $10.50/glass from room service. I presume that what I had had at some time been a William Hill that had been left to turn to vinegar. It was slightly more expensive from room service, but I hope that it was in a lot better condition.

I wanted to like Hotel Monaco, especially because the location is convenient and the lobby has a fun, colorful design, but the stay was more frustrating than enjoyable. Check-in took nearly 30 minutes even though I arrived well after the posted check-in time, and the desk agent seemed overwhelmed. Our room looked worn, with scuffed furniture, stained carpet, and a bathroom fan that rattled loudly whenever the light was on. The bed was comfortable enough, but the walls were thin; we heard hallway conversations and doors slamming until after midnight. Housekeeping also skipped our room one day, despite us leaving the sign out correctly. The staff apologized, but no real solution was offered. For the price, I expected a much better-maintained room and smoother service.

Stayed here for three nights and honestly, it exceeded expectations. The location was perfect--steps from a metro stop and a short stroll to some great local eateries, which made exploring effortless without being in the tourist chaos. Our room faced the inner courtyard, so it was remarkably peaceful; the only sounds were distant morning chatter from the staff, but never disruptive. I was worried about noise given the central spot, but the windows did their job brilliantly. Breakfast was a pleasant surprise, with fresh pastries, made-to-order eggs, and proper coffee rather than the watery stuff you often get. Considering the quality of the bedding, the spotless bathroom, and the genuinely helpful concierge, I felt it was worth every penny--not cheap, but fair for what you receive. I would happily return next time and will recommend it to friends visiting the city.

Lovely stay at the Sofitel. Staff couldn't have been friendlier, the bed was one of the most comfortable I've slept in, and breakfast in the morning was delicious. Would happily come back next time I'm in town.

We had a fantastic stay at Hard Rock. The room was spotless, modern, and surprisingly quiet considering how lively the property felt downstairs. Our balcony view was a nice bonus, especially at sunset. Staff at check-in were friendly and gave us helpful recommendations for nearby restaurants and shows without being pushy. The pool area had a great atmosphere, with good music and plenty of loungers when we went in the morning. Breakfast was a little pricey, but the portions were generous and service was quick. I also appreciated the comfortable bed and blackout curtains after a long day out. A few elevators were busy around checkout, but that was a minor inconvenience. Would happily stay here again.

The Sofitel was a quiet escape in the middle of the city--the bed was heavenly and the blackout curtains worked wonders. Service felt genuine, not forced, and the bathroom's rainfall shower was a small luxury I didn't want to leave.
The Hotel Allegro looked charming online, but my room was cramped, noisy, and overdue for a refresh. Check-in dragged on, and the shower barely had any water pressure.

The Conrad Hotel is a beautiful hotel. Our room was perfect and beautiful in every way. I was very impressed (and I am hard to please and have high standards). It was so clean, aesthetically pleasing, up to date, just gorgeous! I would definitely stay there again. I loved it. The location is superb too, attached to Nordstrom and Northbridge mall. Can't wait to go back!

The air conditioning barely worked and the hallways smelled like stale cigarettes. Staff were polite but painfully slow to respond when our sink clogged. Definitely not worth the premium price for such a worn-down room.

This was one of the best hotels I've stayed at in Chicago. I've also tried Amalfi and a number of larger chain hotels downtown. This one was the best. Great service, beautiful room, roomy bathroom, top-notch amenities.

We paid $75 a night through Priceline, which is excellent for June. Our room had a fantastic view of the Hancock Building and the river. The room was large, clean and had a couch, easy chair and desk chair. The bedding was the newer 'non-bedspread' style, the bed was comfortable, the bathroom was large and, well, we were pleased with the room and the Hyatt in every way. We ate at the lobby restaurant, which is attractively decorated and was bustling with activity when we were there. We only got Cobb Salads, so I don't know if the food, in general, is good or not. The Cobb was so-so. Our only complaint was the $48 fee to park your car over-night and the $13 daily fee for the internet. Many places are offering free internet these days and I wish the Hyatt would hop on board with this concept. We hated to leave!

The lobby's fresh, modern decor was a pleasant surprise, and our room's skyline view was stunning at dusk. Breakfast had solid pastries and decent coffee, though nothing fancy, and the wifi never dropped during work calls.

I had a very comfortable three-night stay at Swissotel. The location was convenient for getting around, with restaurants, shops, and public transport all within an easy walk. My room was bright, quiet, and surprisingly spacious, with a really comfortable bed and plenty of storage for a longer visit. I also appreciated the practical desk area and the large windows, even though the view was mostly city buildings. Everything was spotless when I arrived, and housekeeping was discreet and consistent. The front desk team handled check-in quickly and were happy to arrange a taxi and suggest a few nearby places for dinner. Breakfast had a good variety, including fresh fruit and made-to-order eggs. It is not the cheapest option, but the service and overall comfort made it feel worthwhile.
The Hyatt's dated decor and hallway noise made the room feel less relaxing than expected. Even a short overnight stay felt too long, and I barely slept.

I expected more from a Hilton at this price point. The room was superficially clean, but there were crumbs along the edge of the carpet, dust on the lampshade, and a hair in the bathroom sink. The decor also felt tired, with scratched furniture, faded curtains, and an old-fashioned beige color scheme that made the space seem dim. Sleep was difficult because I could hear hallway conversations, doors slamming, and traffic well past midnight. The bed was reasonably comfortable, but that did not make up for the overall lack of care. For the rate charged, including the extra parking fee, it simply did not feel like good value.
Disappointing stay at the Sheraton: the price felt far too high for a tired room, unreliable Wi-Fi, and a bleak city view. Two nights felt much too long.

I booked the Fairmont expecting a landmark stay, but left feeling I'd overpaid for a faded name. The bed was decent, but the air conditioning cycled loudly all night, and I woke up more tired than when I arrived. At nearly $400 a night, that alone stung. The lobby has grand bones, yet the hallways and our room feel stuck in the early 2000s--scuffed baseboards, worn carpet, and furniture that looks like it survived a decade of conferences. Breakfast was the low point: a lukewarm buffet with watery scrambled eggs and stale pastries, all for $32 a head. Service was polite but stretched thin, especially at check-in. Honestly, the location is prime, but so is the competition. For this price, I expected polish, not a lesson in managing disappointment. I won't be back.

The room was so noisy my neighbor's phone conversation kept me up half the night. Staff seemed annoyed when I asked for towels, and the AC barely worked, making it stuffy. Beautiful lobby, but that's where it ends. Not worth it.

The $400+ price tag felt absurd once I saw the uninspired skyline view and endured the sad, lukewarm breakfast buffet. WiFi dropped constantly in the room, so I gave up and read. Definitely not worth the hype.

Excellent location, feels like a boutique hotel. Right next to Neiman Marcus (V.expensive dept store) and 2 mins walk to John Hancock tower. As most American ,medium to high end, hotels service was excellent from the bellhop to reception. Upgrade to a suite if you are staying longer than a couple of days as walking around the windy city can be tiring and a suite feels like a small apartment. The pub in the basement is good for a sandwich and a Beer. They will be refurbing so take adavantage of lower rates now as I feel they will be going for very high end clients after the remodelling

I've used Priceline for every trip I've made back to Chicago and I've been fortunate to have stayed in some excellent hotels downtown. This was my first and last stay at the Ambassador East. Its conveniently located near the Clark/Division stop on the El's red line. That is the best part of our experience. When we checked in we were charged additional for upgrading from a king bed to two queens. I've never had that issue at any other hotel I've stayed at. The room's decor was outdated and the TV was tiny. The hotel charges for usage of Internet. You could hear people in the hallway and when you're in the hallway you could easily hear people in the rooms. We weren't in Chicago to stay in the hotel however, for people that might want a romantic weekend this definitely isn't the place. ...read more
Disappointing stay at Homewood: the room looked clean, but hallway noise continued past midnight. Breakfast was bland and picked over, and I barely slept.

I had a very comfortable three-night stay at the Omni. The location was ideal for getting around downtown, with shops, restaurants, and several attractions just a short walk away. My room was larger than expected and thoughtfully laid out, with a sitting area that made it easy to relax without feeling like I was on top of my luggage. Everything was clean, quiet, and in good condition, and the bed was especially comfortable after long days exploring the city. Check-in was quick, and every staff member I dealt with was friendly without being overbearing. I also appreciated the well-equipped fitness room and the easy-to-use Wi-Fi. Prices at the hotel restaurant felt a little high, but the service and food were good. I would happily stay here again.

My stay at the Conrad was far more disappointing than I expected for the price. The lobby looks impressive, but the service never matched it. Check-in took nearly 25 minutes, and the front desk seemed overwhelmed even though there were only a few guests waiting. Our room was attractive and had a great city view, but it was noticeably dusty, with fingerprints on the windows and a bathroom door that would not close properly. Housekeeping also forgot towels one day and did not replace the coffee supplies. The restaurant was convenient but overpriced, and breakfast arrived lukewarm after a long wait. Staff were polite when approached, yet no one seemed particularly attentive. I may have caught the hotel on an off week, but overall it felt more polished in appearance than in actual execution.
Breakfast was fresh with good coffee and pastries, the staff were warm and attentive, and our room's river view was lovely. For the location and comfort, it felt well worth the price.

We loved our stay at the Talbott. We were in Chicago to attend the theater show Dirty Dancing. We booked our room through Orbitz and received a nice discount. When we arrived at the hotel everyone from the doorman to the front desk to the maids were highly professional and courtesy. We were upgraded to a King bed suite. The suite was well decorated and spacious. My wife particularily enjoyed the heat that could be directed at the marble floor in the bathroom. We loved the hotel and will definitely stay at the Talbott on our next trip to Chicago. Highly recommended.
The fresh, modern decor and skyline view made our stay feel special. Staff were warm and efficient, and despite the premium rate, the experience felt worth every dollar.

I found this wonderful Hotel ! The location is awesome, just minutes away from all the shopping, Restaurants and Bars you could possibly want . I was in town for an interview, so I was really nervous . I ended up suggesting the Hotel Restaurant for my interview and they took such a good care of us, they made me feel so comfortable that I was hardly nervous at all. And the place was pack! The room was superb! Really cool design . I had a room they call an apartment, and it was fantastic! The natural light you get in this room is awesome, and I am very sensitive to dark places. They have a full bar in the room , which I was able to use to entertain my friends that night. I went to the gym for a little bit of exercise and I have to say I have never seen such a extensive facility in a hotel. All the staff made me feel like I was family. They were available to me at any time, and so friendly ! I will definitely be back for another stay.

I took the wife and kids to Chicago for one last fling before school started back up. When I checked in, the staff was very attentive, I showed a little consideration for the friendly attitude (small tip) and was upgraded to a huge upper floor room complete with a bar! I didn't get the 'Priceline' glare and it paid off for all involved. The air and water show was underway on the lake front, and we had planes flying over our room. The kids thought it was great. That night we had a great view of the fireworks at Navy Pier. The Sunday morning breakfast buffet at the hotel was very good and the price was not out of reason. The conceirge was very knowledgeable and very friendly. It was one of the best times we ever had in Chicago.

We stayed at the Hotel Amalfi for four nights and honestly couldn't have asked for a smoother getaway. The location is ideal--just enough off the main strip to avoid the racket, but a two-minute stroll gets you to the beach and all the little trattorias. What really stood out was the staff; they remembered our names by day two and went out of their way to book a last-minute boat trip when the tour we wanted was sold out. Our room had a small balcony overlooking the lemon groves, and the scent drifting in each morning was pure bliss. The breakfast spread was generous, with fresh pastries and excellent espresso. Sure, the decor leans a bit traditional, but it's spotless and comfortable. We left feeling genuinely rested and a little sad to go--that says it all. Would absolutely return.

We stayed at this hotel for 4 nights in August. We waited a while to check in even though there were quite a few desks open, this was a little annoying as the receptionists seemed to work in two's. Our room had a great view of Navy Pier and was a good size. The bed was very comfortable and the room was spotlessly clean. The location of the hotel is the best, we walked to Navy Pier and Michigan Ave. The breakfast buffet was great although a little pricey and the bar very relaxing for a nightcap or two. Would certainly recommend this hotel and would stay here again.

Ideal location right in the heart of the Near North side but good grief, they need more than two elevators. You can wait 10 minutes for an elevator and if you happen to be on the first floor (registration desk on 6th floor), you can face a long line just to catch one. Rooms are from the same cookie cutter as all Homewood Suites - very utilitarian; unlike many locations however, this one does not include a DVD player in the rooms. The pool is OK but there's no jacuzzi. Oh, and housekeeping is deficient when it comes to keeping the towels stocked in the pool area. Front desk service is pretty good.
The city view from my room was lovely, and the bed was quiet and comfortable enough for a great night's sleep. Breakfast was fresh and varied, making the stay feel well worth the price.

I was lucky enough to get a '4 star' hotel off of Priceline for $70 - I was luckier that I got the Knickerbocker! From check in to check out the hotel staff was extremely helpful and friendly. The rooms are small but cozy. After reading the reviews from other guests I was somewhat scared of what I would find - they must have stayed at a different hotel. I am a very frequent traveler and felt that the rooms and the hotel met the '4 star' rating. Yes, the rooms and bathrooms were small, but what historic hotel in a big city isn't? The decor and quality met my expectations. The lobby and bar were very inviting. Overall, I would stay here again and again.

Despite the bustling heart of Amalfi just below, our room was wonderfully soundproofed--I slept like a log. The wifi didn't miss a beat for late-night planning, and waking to that pastel coastline and glittering sea was absolutely worth it.

The Omni was a pleasant surprise--check-in was quick, the room was spotless with a comfy bed, and the location made exploring easy. Staff were friendly without hovering. I'd gladly book here again for a hassle-free stay.

I expected much more from a Fairmont stay, especially at this price point. The lobby has some classic charm, but the room decor felt dated rather than elegant, with worn carpeting and heavy furniture that made the space seem gloomy. The bathroom was cramped and disappointing: chipped tile, weak water pressure, and a shower curtain that looked like it had seen better days. Housekeeping also missed replenishing towels. Staff at check-in were polite but noticeably rushed, and when I mentioned the bathroom issues, the response was a vague promise to 'look into it' with no follow-up. The location was convenient, but the overall experience felt overpriced and far below the level of comfort and service I expected.
The InterContinental made our weekend feel special--spotless room, incredibly comfortable bed, and staff who remembered our breakfast coffee order. The location was perfect for walking everywhere.
Hotel Monaco was a comfortable base for our weekend downtown. The room was quiet and charming, and everyone at the front desk was genuinely helpful when we needed dinner suggestions.

I had a very pleasant two-night stay at Hotel Allegro. The lobby has a lively, theatrical feel, and that colorful style carries into the guest room without making it seem overdone. The decor is a little eclectic rather than ultra-modern, but everything felt fresh and well cared for. My room was spotless when I arrived, including the bathroom and the corners that are often overlooked in older hotels. The bed was genuinely comfortable, and despite being in a busy part of downtown, I slept well both nights with very little street noise. WiFi connected quickly and stayed reliable for video calls and streaming. Staff at the desk were friendly, especially when I needed directions and a late checkout. It was an easy, comfortable stay, and I would happily return.

Booked the Knickerbocker specifically for its location near Times Square, and honestly, that's the only thing it has going for it. The lobby feels chaotic, more like a train station than a four-star hotel, with nowhere to sit while you wait for check-in. Our room wasn't ready until almost 4 PM, which was already annoying, but when we finally got up there, the view was of a brick wall and the air conditioning sounded like a lawnmower. The bed was okay, but the pillows were flat as pancakes. We ate at the rooftop bar one night--overpriced drinks and service that clearly didn't care. The hallway smelled like old carpet and the elevator took forever. For what they charge, it's just not worth it. I'd skip this one and stay somewhere with actual soundproofing and staff who respond to requests. Won't be back.

Breakfast was a satisfying spread of fresh pastries and made-to-order eggs, and the staff's genuine warmth set a great tone each morning. Perched steps from DuPont Circle, the view over the rooftops was lovely, making every errand an easy stroll.

Perfect location, clean and courteous staff all added up to a great stay. Its in an area with plenty of stores ( The Mile) and restaurants. Hotel lobby is on the 6th floor and the elevator to get there was annoyingly slow but overall I would highly recommend this place regardless if your there with a family, friends or on business. The subway to Wrigley is a 1/2 block away from the front door.
The spa was divine and the staff never missed a beat, even at midnight. Breakfast had the best views I've seen in ages. Slept like a rock; already plotting my return.
Disappointing stay at the Talbott--the room felt dated, housekeeping missed basic details, and street noise kept us awake. For the price, I expected much better.

Have stayed at this hotel on several occasions and have never failed to be anything but delighted. Great Bar (draught Stella and Guinness) which was being upgraded at the end of March when I was last there, good food, lovely staff, large clean rooms, comfortable beds, spot on location for the Golden Mile, Joey's Pizzas next door are fantastic. Ignore any bad reviews you read about this hotel as the authors must either have been very unlucky or impossible to please. Highly recommended

We ate at the Prime House restaurant last year, that is why we picked the hotel. Last year the food and service at the Prime House was outstanding. This year the service felt rushed. The waitress even asked why we were eating so early. It was 6:30pm. Our room in the hotel felt cramped. The beds were comfortable. The bathroom had maintenance problems. The maid service and turndown out night was good. All of the staff at the hotel were friendly and helpful. I just was not impressed by the quality of the hotel itself for what we were paying.

We stayed at Hotel Amalfi for four nights in early June and genuinely didn't want to leave. The room was spotless, housekeeping seemed to appear at exactly the right moments, and the beds were surprisingly comfortable for a coastal hotel, so we slept soundly every night despite the church bells in the morning. The staff deserve special mention; the front desk arranged a last-minute boat tour for us and the breakfast team remembered our coffee order by day two. As for the view, waking up to terraced lemon groves tumbling down toward the sea never got old, and the rooftop terrace at sunset was simply breathtaking. Yes, it's on the pricier side, but for the location, service, and those balcony views, we felt it was absolutely worth it. Would return in a heartbeat.

French elegance meets genuine warmth at Sofitel--the lobby's floral scent and hushed luxury set the tone, and my room's view of the city at dusk was unforgettable. Staff remembered my name, the bed was cloud-soft, and breakfast croissants rivaled Paris.

We booked the James expecting a sleek, quiet retreat, but our stay was a letdown from start to finish. The room faced an interior airshaft, so the 'city view' was basically a brick wall and a glimpse of the neighboring rooftop AC units. Worse, the hallways were surprisingly noisy--we heard shouting and slamming doors until past 2 AM, and the thin window did nothing to block the mechanical hum. Housekeeping clearly skipped the details: there was a sticky patch near the mini-fridge, dust on the lampshades, and a coffee ring on the desk. I slept poorly, tossing all night on a mattress that sagged in the middle, and the pillows were limp as pancakes. By morning, I was exhausted and just wanted out. For the price, this felt more like a budget chain than a boutique stay. I won't be returning.
Honestly expected more from Hotel Amalfi. The view was nice, sure, but the room smelled musty and the AC barely worked, and staff took ages to answer anything. Wouldn't stay again.

My corner room on the 24th floor had a sweeping view of the river and the skyline that made me want to linger by the window every evening. The wifi was genuinely dependable, even during peak hours, which meant I could stream a movie without a single drop. Breakfast offered a solid spread, from made-to-order omelets to fresh pastries, though the coffee was just okay. What really stood out was the staff: the front desk remembered my name by the second day, and the housekeeping team left a handwritten note about a local running trail I'd inquired about. I've stayed at pricier properties that made me feel more like a transaction; here, every encounter felt personal and unhurried. A few minor scuffs on the hallway paint and a slow elevator on checkout morning were negligible against the warmth and efficiency of the entire stay. I'd gladly return.

great bed, but when I first came in, I requested a room with a lake view (i requested this over the phone as well), and the front desk woman said 'this is a great room'. I go upstairs and its awful looking. The view was of the neighboring roofs. Then I spent half an hour trying to find a better room. Eventually I got a corner roof with a partial view. Horrible experience. also rooms were small and had crappy look (yellowy wallpaper and bedsheets)

The bathroom was spotless with great water pressure, and the Wi-Fi handled video calls without a hitch. Breakfast offered plenty of hot options, and being steps from the Metro made exploring effortless--exactly what I needed.
Really enjoyed my stay at the InterContinental--the room was comfortable, staff genuinely welcoming, and breakfast excellent. The central location made getting around easy, so I'd happily return.

I travel often for business and this hotel ranks very low on my list. The room had such a strong odor of smoke, it gave me a headache (and I used to be a smoker)! The room service was mediocre and extremely expensive. The hotel is disturbingly huge. Very difficult to navigate your way around it. I waited on hold for twenty minutes to ask a concierge where a pharmacy was located. She curtly gave me cross-street names and hung up. Uhhhhh, how do I know which direction to go in??? Stains on the carpet in the room. A big gauge in the wall, where maybe a thermostat once was??? The shower is decent. All in all, for the price they charge, NO THANKS!!! I'm just glad my company is footing the bill.

We live down the block from the hotel. We arranged to have new floors put in our condo while we were away. The floors were not finished when we returned so we looked for an inexpensive local hotel for one night. I think the Ambassador East was the least expensive hotel within a reasonable distance so we decided to stay there. Over the years I had had some visiting groups stay there. I had also eaten there and been to the bar but I had never stayed there myself. The lobby is elegant. The service is great and the room was large and clean although a little outdated. The location is the best residential area in the city (as far as I am concerned -- I live two blocks away) and it is very convenient to North Michigan Avenue ( a good shopping street) and reasonably convenient to the Loop ( the main business area) There are also probably 50 restaurants in all price ranges in reasonable walking distance including some of the best in the city. I paid less than $100 including tax for one night. I am not sure what their regular rates are but I think my deal was the best travel bargain around.

I booked the Sheraton expecting the dependable comfort of a big-name chain, but the experience left a sour taste. The moment I walked into the lobby, the dated floral carpets and worn armchairs screamed 1990s, and the hallways had a faint musty smell. My room was a mixed bag: the bathroom sparkled, but the carpet by the bed had a suspicious dark stain I avoided stepping on, and the curtains were frayed at the edges. I slept terribly--the mattress sagged in the middle, and the air conditioner rattled loudly every few minutes, keeping me half-awake all night. Breakfast was the final letdown: lukewarm scrambled eggs that tasted powdered, stale croissants, and coffee that was weak and bitter. For nearly $250 a night, I'd expect modern fixtures, a truly clean floor, and at least decent morning fuel. Sadly, this felt more like a budget motel with a fancy sign. I won't be returning.

I was initially very excited to be staying at the Ambassador East hotel. The photos online appeared very classy and upscale and I thought staying there would be a pleasant experience. Upon arrival I was very disappointed - the main lobby was closed for construction making it somewhat difficult to get around. Our room was very dated - old furnishings and linens, damaged tile - it fell quite short for the high price we paid. It is an older building with very thin walls allowing you to clearly hear all other guests in surrounding rooms and also the lovely slam of doors of departing guests in the morning. Doorways are extremely narrow in hallways and room - gives a very claustrophobic feel to the hotel.

Perfect spot for exploring the city--everything was walkable. The staff were genuinely friendly and helpful. WiFi never dropped, and the complimentary breakfast with fresh pastries and strong coffee was a lovely start to each day.
Hotel Monaco looked charming online, but the room felt worn and noisy, with thin walls and a slow check-in. For the price, I expected much better upkeep and service.

We stayed four nights at the Hyatt and honestly wished it could have been a week. From check-in, the staff went out of their way to make us feel welcome--the front desk agent remembered our names the entire stay, and the concierge arranged a last-minute dinner reservation without blinking. Our room on the 14th floor had a floor-to-ceiling window overlooking the harbor, and waking up to that skyline every morning was worth the trip alone. The decor felt fresh rather than dated; warm woods, crisp linens, and lighting that actually worked instead of the usual hotel gloom. Housekeeping was prompt and thorough. If I had one quibble, it's that our trip felt far too short to enjoy the pool and lounge properly. We'll be back for a longer stay.

I wanted to like the Knickerbocker, especially given the price and the convenient Times Square location, but the stay was more frustrating than enjoyable. Check-in took nearly half an hour, and the front desk staff seemed rushed and uninterested in answering basic questions. Our room looked stylish in photos, yet it was surprisingly cramped, with barely enough space to open two suitcases. The bathroom had dusty shelves and a shower that fluctuated between hot and lukewarm. Street noise came through the windows late into the night, and housekeeping skipped our room one day without explanation. The rooftop bar has a nice view, but drinks were overpriced and service was slow. This hotel seems to rely on its name and location more than consistent service. I expected much better for the cost.
Room was musty and the AC barely worked, front desk took an hour to check us in. Breakfast was basically cold eggs and stale bread. For this price, honestly expected way more. Won't be back.

The third-floor room looked straight onto the leafy courtyard, not the city skyline, but that turned out to be a blessing--morning light filtered through the maples without any street noise. The wifi held strong even during evening video calls, which surprised me for an older building. Decor-wise, the lobby keeps its classic Art Deco bones, and the guest rooms walk a fine line: the furniture isn't new, but the crisp white linens and fresh paint keep it from feeling tired. I checked in on a Tuesday and left Thursday, and honestly, that second night flew by. I could have easily stayed one more day just to use the pool terrace again. Breakfast was a simple continental spread, but the coffee was excellent. A solid, comfortable pick, and I'd return without hesitation.

Room was spotless and the view over the bay was unreal--watching the sunset from the bed never got old. Staff remembered my coffee order by day two, which made the whole stay feel personal. Would definitely book again.

Stayed three nights at Homewood and came away genuinely impressed, though I'll admit the lobby made me pause--those dark wood beams and patterned carpet feel a little 2005, not fresh. But my room on the eighth floor flipped that first impression. The view faced the river, and watching the barges ease past during golden hour made the whole trip feel calmer. Bathroom was the real win: a deep soaking tub, excellent water pressure, and towels thick enough to dry off twice. The bed was firm without being board-like, and the blackout curtains actually worked. At $189 a night, I'd call that fair for the size and quiet. Decor could use a refresh, sure, but everything was spotless and functional. I'd return without hesitation.

This hotel was PERFECT for our girls getaway. The decor is fun & refreshing. Loved the roof top bar. Every staff member was friendly & always smiling. The location is perfect for Michigan Ave shopping, the beach, dinner and night life. It was a mile or two from Millenium Station. The concierge recommended a couple places to hang out after dinner and added our names to the guest list (I'm sure they do it all the time but still a nice gesture).

Stayed over Memorial Weekend for 2 nites, 2 rooms. Great Hotel, we always love breakfast in morning,and drinks in even when applicable. Around the corner from magnificent Mile,and close to lots of restaurants. Staff was great, we even checked in early before noon,and other room available less than hour later. Fresh fruit was available to us,and bell guys are cool. Suites are on small side compared to other homewoods but no complaints here, house cleaning kept our room clean,and we felt safe!

How about this had reservation confirmation in hand and still had to argue with the registration desk about price on reservation. She tried to charge me price on bill they slide under your door. Sorry not on my watch! Then about this room you gave me I understand this place is old but for the price you charge how about some indoor plumbing! You take a shower and the tub fills with water will not drain this is absolutely redickulas for this being a Hilton I think you should step back and take a look at how this place is operating. Registration: Fail Parking price: Fail Plumbing: Fail Thank you Hilton for for my super 8 experience in Chicago.

We booked a club room for our anniversary weekend and the welcome amenity (a lovely prosecco and chocolate-covered strawberries) was a thoughtful touch. The room itself was spotless, with a super comfortable king bed and the blackout curtains really did their job. The gym is top-notch for a hotel, and I actually got a solid workout in before we hit the pool. Speaking of which, the pool area is a bit compact, but we snagged loungers in the morning without issue. Club lounge breakfast was the highlight--the made-to-order omelets and fresh pastries were fantastic, and the staff there remembered our names by day two. Sure, valet parking is steep, but for this level of service and comfort, we'd return without hesitation. A solid five stars for a consistently excellent stay.

The Conrad felt more like a corporate checkbox than a luxury escape. Our room had a stale odor, AC rattled all night, and housekeeping missed turn-down despite asking twice. Staff were polite but utterly indifferent--we expected far more for the price.

so my sweetie lures me out under the guise of dinner at the China Grill, upon arrival he tells me his boys are watching the game in a suite upstairs and want to say hi...we arrive at the 35th floor and my oh my!!! SURPRISE!!! ladies and gentlemen THIS is something to be admired...spacious and roomy, yet warm, cozy and inviting...great bed, comfortable furniture, great 42 inch plasmas, and the views are UNBELIEVABLE...my only complaint? a shower should have a door to keep the heat IN...other than that no complaints, room service was great, morning coffee was yummo...overall a fabulous experience!!!

The hotel is just ok. Stayed there for 5 days when visiting friends. They had a renovation going so there was no lobby, bar or anything. Just a decently furnished room for 200 usd. The renovation was not annoying but i think they ahould charge... much less untill its done. You cant beat the location! Very convenient especially if u like chicqgo nightlife!

My daughter and I woke in the morning wanting to go swimming. When we arrived at the pool the water was covered by a white scum. I then attempted to use both of the phones at the pool, one white phone and one emergency red phone, to call the desk. Both were out of service!!!! I am glad there wasn't an emergency. As we were exited the pool area I ran into a hotel employee and told her about the problems and then asked her to call us when the pool was clean.... never heard back.

I've stayed at Hard Rock properties before and usually expect a certain level of polish, but this visit missed the mark by a mile. The bathroom looked decent at first, but the shower drain was slow, and the cheap pump bottles of soap were nearly empty. Our 'city view' turned out to be a brick wall and a vent that hummed all night. Staff were polite at check-in but vanished when we called for extra towels--took three tries and over an hour. Sleep was rough: the mattress sagged in the middle, and the hallway noise from a rowdy group carried straight through the thin door. For the price, this felt more like a mid-tier chain than a rock-and-roll flagship. I wanted to love it, but left tired and frustrated. Won't be back.
The bathroom looked dated, with weak water pressure and worn fixtures. I only stayed one night, but the constant hallway noise was exhausting, despite the convenient downtown location.

My $200 Gucci sunglasses were stolen out of my bag on the 16th. I filed a report with the hotel security and am anxious to hear back from them. This was such a disappointment, as we liked the hotel and were having a great time in Chicago. Our room was really nice, with 2 bathrooms. We had 2 double beds and a comfortable hideaway bed. We had a great view of the lake and park. The hotel charged us $25 to check in early (10am).

I had a very comfortable stay at the Conrad and would gladly return. Check-in was quick and friendly, and the lobby's modern design made a good first impression. My room felt fresh and thoughtfully maintained, with tasteful furnishings rather than the dated look some business hotels have. The bed was excellent, and I slept soundly for three nights; the blackout curtains and strong shower were welcome bonuses. Wi-Fi worked reliably throughout the room, including during video calls, with no frustrating dropouts. Despite being in a busy part of the city, the hotel was surprisingly quiet at night. I occasionally heard a faint hallway door close, but there was no traffic noise or disruptive activity. Staff were attentive without being intrusive, and the breakfast selection was varied and well prepared. Overall, it was a polished, relaxing experience.
Breakfast had plenty of fresh choices and good coffee, while the room was spotless and the decor pleasantly updated. I only wish our stay had been longer.

I really wanted to love the Hard Rock, given its reputation, but my stay fell flat. The location is undeniably convenient--walking distance to the Strip's main attractions and a CVS for supplies. However, the noise was relentless. Our room faced the pool, and the thumping bass from the dayclub didn't let up until after midnight, then the hallway chatter and slamming doors started. I got maybe four hours of broken sleep, waking up groggy and irritated. The bathroom was another low point: the shower pressure was weak, the caulking was moldy and peeling, and the fan sounded like a jet engine. For the premium price, I expected far better. It felt more like a worn-out motel with a rock-and-roll facade than a four-star experience. I won't be returning unless they fix the soundproofing and bathroom maintenance.

Honestly, the James felt more like a flashy hostel than a luxury hotel. The room was impossibly small, the walls paper-thin, and I could hear every door slam until 3 AM. Staff were polite but useless when I asked for a quiet room. Not worth the premium price.

I had high hopes for the Talbott given its reputation and the rates they charge, but my four-night stay fell flat in nearly every way. The walls are paper thin--I could hear my neighbors' conversations and the elevator clanking until well past midnight, so I barely slept more than a few hours each night. The staff seemed*o perform a strange kind of politeness that never felt genuine; my requests for extra towels took two phone calls and several hours. For nearly $400 a night, I expected far better. Honestly, three nights in would have been plenty--I was counting the days until checkout, which is never a good sign. The location is convenient, I'll grant that, but convenience doesn't justify an underwhelming, overpriced experience. I won't be returning and can't recommend it.

I'll be honest--I booked the James mainly for the location, but the stay itself ended up being the highlight of my trip. The lobby has this quiet, understated cool that doesn't try too hard, and the front desk team was genuinely warm without being overbearing. My room faced the river, and the floor-to-ceiling windows made the whole space feel twice as big. The bed was firm but plush, and the blackout curtains actually worked. I'm picky about bathrooms, and this one impressed me--huge shower head, good water pressure, and the Kiehl's products were a nice touch. The gym had decent equipment, though it's small. I grabbed a drink at the bar one night, and the bartender remembered my order the next day, which felt like a small, pleasant miracle. For a few nights in the city, this place hit every mark, and I'd happily return for the views alone.

WiFi was practically useless in my room, and the walls were so thin I heard every door slam. Breakfast featured lukewarm, rubbery eggs, while the bathroom had a constantly dripping shower and a broken exhaust fan.

I was very much looking forward to our stay at this hotel, after hearing all the good things about it. Unfortunately, it was a very underwhelming experience, to say the least. But let me begin with the things that I do like about the hotel. First off, it is located my favorite part of Chicago - the leafy, affluent part of town that is Chicago's equivalent of Manhattan's Upper East Side, complete with sidewalks, quiet tree-lined streets, real old-school townhouses (instead of ugly towering monstrosities that are 21st century condominiums), cute boutiques (instead of Gap, Banana Republic and other mainstream mass-produced brands) and, of course, Hermes of Paris (which warrants a separate mention). I also like the small intimate lobby area with old leather couches, cherry colored wooden furnitures, area rugs and distinct artwork. The very reason why I always tend to gravitate toward smaller boutique hotels instead of impersonal chains. I definitely love the room. While the space issue is not as bad in Chicago as it is in Manhattan, getting a 400-sqft guestroom for our weekend getaway is not an easy task. So we were delighted to see that our room comes with generous, ample bathroom, double sink, massive king bed AND still enough space to walk around, do a chicken dance, and strut my Herve and Louboutins in. My only reservation was the lack of natural light - the windows were definitely inadequate to allow sunlight to find its way into our 11th-floor room, but then again Delaware St is not exactly the widest street in town and there are buildings in front of us, so can't have it all! Yet one thing that really disappointed us was the service, or lack thereof. I mean, seriously. They don't call it the 'hospitality' industry for no reason. I did pay a premium to stay in smaller boutique hotels such as this so I do get a service that is a little bit more personalized than the kind that I would be getting from say, a 3000-room Vegas hotel. First, I called in to reconfirm my reservation. The lady on the phone was anything but courteous and competent. First off, she was not able to find my reservation and I was transferred to the front desk staff, to whom I had to explain myself all over again (my pet peeve when it comes to on-the-phone customer service). The person who manned the reception desk was not friendly, nor was he at all competent either. Case in point - he had to send the slip of paper on which I agree to the nightly rate and duration of stay up to the room after we checked in, which clearly indicated that he must have forgotten when we were actually down there. But the real kicker was when we ordered room service after arriving - it was about 1AM. As a general rule, I am never, ever, a big fan of room service, having had my fair share of bad food that they slap 18% gratuity, 10.5% tax (and still expect a tip) on during my days globetrotting on the company's expense account. Think overcooked steaks, lukewarm soup, bread hard enough to knock someone out, and ice-creams that are already half melted by the time it reaches your suite. So I really wasn't expecting hotels as small as Talbott to have a 24-hour room service, but lo and behold, they do.
