I booked the Ambassador expecting a quiet, central base, but between the rattling elevator shaft and the street-level bar's bass thumping until 2 AM, I barely got three hours of sleep. The room itself was clean enough, but the walls were paper-thin--I could hear the neighbor's TV news and every flush. The staff seemed overwhelmed and disinterested; my request for a fan to mask the noise was met with a shrug and a promise that never materialized. Location-wise, you can't beat the walk to the main square, but that's about all it has going for it. Check-in took twenty minutes, and the front desk didn't even acknowledge my loyalty status. I left more exhausted than I arrived, paying a premium for a night that felt like a dormitory. Unless you're a heavy sleeper or bring earplugs, I'd look elsewhere. Disappointing all around.

As I sit here in my 14th floor room at the hotel Allegro, I listen to the conversation between husband and wife in the room on my left. She seems to have a cough today. In the room on my right, someone seems to use the restroom quite a bit. I hear the water running and the toilet flushing. I also hear footsteps in the room upstairs. Even roadside motels have better insulation between the rooms. I've stayed in about a dozen Kimpton hotels and this is by far the worst. The room is dirty - the carpet covered in spots and stains, the curtains with a large brown stain (I don't want to guess what it is), paint peeling, rips in the wallpaper. The decor is a bit garish, with Pepto-Bismol covered walls, green and yellow pillows and the filthy brown and white carpet. The size of the room is fine and the bed comfortable, but I'm so glad I had earplugs to avoid listening to others' toilets flushing all night. The location is good for downtown theaters or business. Only three elevators serve this 17+ storey building and they run very slowly. Chicago has many nice hotel options -- many I've enjoyed quite a bit. Unfortunately this is not one of them, and even more unfortunate for me: I'm stuck here for two more nights. I was looking forward to staying here because most Kimptons are hip, comfortable and attractive. This is not.
The James was a great downtown base: quiet room, genuinely friendly front desk, and an easy walk to restaurants and the river. The bed was especially comfortable.

we love the location and proximity to everything. The staff was very friendly and courteous. They were so nice to our 2.5 year old boy. got his backpack full of goodies the moment we arrived. We got free wifi and morning drinks by signing up for select guest program . Can't beat that! the only minor issue is the elevator. we have to take 2 separate elevator trips to get to our room. It got a little annoying when we were going in and out often. Otherwise, it was a great stay!

I expected old-school charm but got peeling wallpaper, a broken AC that cycled all night, and staff who shrugged at the noise from the street. Location is fine, but for the price, this place needs serious maintenance. I left exhausted and disappointed.

I had a very pleasant stay at the InterContinental. Check-in was smooth, and the receptionist took a moment to explain the breakfast hours and hotel facilities rather than just handing over a key. My room was spotless, quiet, and had a comfortable bed with surprisingly good pillows. The city view from the higher floor was a nice bonus, especially in the evening. Breakfast offered plenty of choices, from fresh fruit and pastries to made-to-order eggs, and the staff kept everything well stocked. I also appreciated how quickly housekeeping responded when I asked for extra water. The location made it easy to walk to nearby restaurants and attractions. Prices are not exactly budget-friendly, but the service, comfort, and overall attention to detail made it feel worthwhile.
Homewood's fresh decor and convenient location near shops made our visit easy. The spotless bathroom had great water pressure, and although the stay was brief, we felt well rested.

Great location with a nice city view from our window, and the room was spotless on arrival. Wifi was fast and reliable, and the beds were so comfy I slept like a rock every night. Would happily return.

We got an outstanding rate by signing up for the hotels' website newsletter. Affinia has a great location just off Michigan Avenue near the Water Tower. Beware however: parking is expensive in the Gold Coast....$48/night. Right from the start, Victor greeted us and made us feel welcome. Check-in was easy and our room was gorgeous. However, it was a handicapped acessible room and I wanted a tub, so one call to the front desk and we had another room. All rooms have been renovated and they are beautiful, comfortable and well appointed. The rooftop bar is a must-do. The outside patio has heaters and candles, a high table for big groups and little groupings of chairs and sofas to get comfy on and enjoy the views. We didn't sit inside the bar area. Pedro and Quentin were excellent bellmen, and Christopher (concierge) was very helpful. As we left, we shook Victor's hand (he's always there!) and told him we've found our new Chicago hotel!

Expected more from the James. My room smelled musty, the AC rattled all night, and housekeeping skipped my floor entirely one day. Staff were pleasant enough but the value just wasn't there. Won't be returning.
Loved the unique design and the rooftop bar views! Staff were incredibly warm and helpful. Our room was super clean and quiet, a real retreat after exploring. Would definitely stay here again.

Hard Rock was a great choice for our weekend stay and felt worth the price, especially given the central location, stylish rooms, and friendly service. Our room was spotless, with a comfortable bed and blackout curtains that made it easy to sleep deeply. Although the lobby and pool area had a lively atmosphere, we barely heard any noise once our door was closed. Breakfast had a good mix of fresh fruit, pastries, eggs, bacon, and made-to-order coffee; it was busy but staff kept everything replenished. The music-themed details were fun without being overdone, and check-in was quick. I would happily stay here again.

We chose Hotel Amalfi for the view, but honestly, the staff made the stay. Every single person, from the front desk to the breakfast crew, greeted us by name after day one - a small touch that felt incredibly personal. The room itself was spotless, though the bathroom was a bit snug, a fair trade for the private balcony overlooking the water. Mornings were a highlight: strong espresso, flaky pastries, and a spread of local cheeses that fuelled our daily hikes. The only minor hiccup was the thin walls; we could hear our neighbours' late-night chatter. Still, the location is unbeatable - a five-minute stroll to the marina and tucked away from the main drag. I'd absolutely return for the hospitality alone.

A lovely hotel in a trendy part of Chicago which gives it a much more comfortable feel than the downtown hotels. The rooms are very, very well appointed, but not large, and the quality of the materials is wonderful without exception. Unfortunately, the service was below average in every way: they failed to deliver laundry by an important and assured deadline; valets didn't deliver the car and had to be asked twice; the concierge gave us miserable directions that got us lost, and the front desk was unable to rectify any issue. It amazed me that so much incompetence could happen in 6 hours! And even after recognizing their shortcomings, not one sincere or significant apology. A poster child of how bad service cannot overcome a well-built, well-furnished hotel.

The Hyatt's location was perfect for exploring downtown, and the decor felt fresh, not tired. Staff were genuinely welcoming, and given the comfort and service, the rate felt more than fair. I'd happily book again.

I expected more from Swissotel given the rate and its reputation. My room faced the river, but the view was mostly blocked by neighboring towers and construction cranes, hardly the relaxing skyline I had imagined. The decor looked tired: faded carpet, dark wood furniture, and a television that felt several generations old. Worse, the room was far from quiet. I could hear elevator traffic, doors slamming, and conversations in the hallway well past midnight. The bathroom was clean enough but cramped, with weak water pressure, a chipped vanity, and little counter space for toiletries. Staff handled check-in efficiently, but they seemed uninterested when I mentioned the noise. For the price, the stay felt dated and impersonal.
Had a great stay at Hard Rock: breakfast had plenty of fresh choices, the price felt fair, Wi‐Fi was reliable, and I only wished we could have stayed longer.

The room wasvery tiny and was very warm. They give you the illusion that you control the temperature but they do. The bathroom is small. The tub is plastic retro fit as stated in another review, and does crackle under your feet. I, personally, did find the water pressure to be fine and the bath ammenities to be of good quality. The public areas are nice and are good to hang out in. This is basically an old hotel that has been updated. The comment about the closet is true, it is actually indescriable. You can hear everything occuring in the other rooms. The location is convienent but so are many other hotels. If you do stay, fly into Midway, take the Orange Line, you cannot go wrong.

I booked the Hotel Amalfi expecting charm, but the reality was a tired, lackluster stay. Breakfast was a sad affair of watery coffee, stale pastries, and scrambled eggs that had clearly been sitting under a heat lamp for hours. Our room's 'sea view' was mostly a brick wall and a sliver of gray water, which felt like a cruel joke given the price. The decor was aggressively dated--think brown floral carpets and wobbly furniture from the 1980s--which immediately made the place feel grimy rather than quaint. The bed was the worst offender: a lumpy mattress with a sagging middle that guaranteed a night of tossing and turning, punctuated by the noisy air conditioning unit rattling like a dying engine. I left more exhausted than I arrived, feeling completely ripped off. I genuinely cannot recommend this place to anyone.

The bathroom was the real highlight for me--a walk-in rainforest shower with excellent water pressure and those big, fluffy towels that actually wrap around you properly. Breakfast had a solid spread: made-to-order omelets, fresh pastries, and a surprisingly good Greek yogurt bar with local honey. My corner room looked straight out over the harbor, and I spent a good hour each morning just watching the ferries glide in, especially at sunrise when the water turned gold. The room itself was spotless, right down to the baseboards and the glass shower door without a single streak. Housekeeping even folded my stray charging cable neatly on the desk. Minor quirks like a slightly squeaky closet door didn't bother me--the staff were so warm and the location unbeatable. I'd happily return, and I'm already checking dates for next spring.

The room was spotless and surprisingly quiet, and the full kitchen made our weekend feel effortless. Staff were friendly without hovering, and the morning breakfast had plenty of hot options. We'd happily book Homewood again for the comfort and value.
Affinia was a comfortable base for our city trip, with a friendly front desk and a quiet, roomy suite. The neighborhood made getting around easy, and I'd happily return.

This hotel was magnificent! Not only was it a mini palace, but the staff was polite, helpful, and professional. In an e-mail I received before we left for Chicago, the concierge, Les, offered to get us tickets, directions, reservations to anything we'd like to see/do. He also got us an upgrade on our room, and when someone rudely butted in line as we were registering, the registry person said they would upgrade our room just for that. And so we were granted a beautiful suite complete with king size bed and jacuzzi. The bed and the linens were so comfortably both of us slept late every morning!

I expected much more from a hotel with this location and reputation. Check-in took nearly 30 minutes because only one person was at the desk, and no one acknowledged the wait. My room looked tired: scuffed walls, a stained chair, and an air conditioner that rattled loudly all night. The bathroom had weak water pressure and the towels smelled slightly damp. Breakfast was disappointing too--lukewarm eggs, empty coffee containers, and tables left uncleared for ages. I mentioned the noise and cleanliness issues to reception, but was simply told they would 'make a note.' The staff were not openly rude, just indifferent. For the price, this was a frustrating stay and I would choose somewhere else next time.

Honestly expected more from Hotel Palmer given the rate they charge. The one bright spot is the location, which is genuinely convenient, steps from the metro and walking distance to several restaurants. Unfortunately, that's where the good news ends. My room, while not dirty, clearly hadn't been deep cleaned in a while -- dust on the lampshade and a sticky film on the bedside table. The bathroom was the real letdown: a cramped shower with weak water pressure and grout that looked like it hadn't seen a scrub brush all year. For what I paid, I'd expect fresh towels without chasing housekeeping and working lights above the mirror. Between the thin walls and the street noise at 5 a.m., sleep was a struggle. Decent neighborhood, but I don't think I got my money's worth here.

This is about the fourth time we stayed at the Allegro. The previous times, I have nothing but good to say about the Allegro. But my reaction has soured on this place. We have stayed here the past few years on the first weekend in December as a kick off to the holiday season and our shopping. From the very start, this year was a disappointment. I had checked the deals on a number of sites before calling the Allegro. I was quoted one price (higher than what was on line), when I mentioned this, I was told I could have the lower price. At check in, the desk was nice but not friendly. We discovered that our room was not as good as in the past (punishment for asking for a lower price?) The closet had no hangers, we had no place to put our suitcase. No one mentioned the wine reception in the evening. On the second day, we discovered that even our bath mat for the shower was missing. It took two phone calls and almost two hours to get a new one. I wrote the management following our stay. I have yet to receive a reply. Needless to say we will be looking elsewhere when we go into the city the next time. I would advise others to do the same.

Nice big rooms but stinky mildew hallways, fair room service menu and weird elevator set up really hurt my review on the Omni. Location was great but there are a lot of other options. If you get a really good deal on the room, I wouldn't say no.

My stay was beyond comfortable, and the staff genuinely went out of their way to make me feel at home. The breakfast spread was fantastic, and the bed was perfect for a deep sleep. I'm already planning my next visit!

I just enjoyed a 3-day weekend at the Swissotel Chicago. A friend of mine booked it and got a GREAT rate. Cheaper than even a fleabag motel. So keep an eye out for specials. The view was great, the location was prime. The staff was helpful. The room was large (we had 2 double beds). I only have one complaint. Our room was next to some sort of storage or mechanical room where employees (I think) would sneak off to talk on the phone. The sound came right though the vent in our bathroom and we could hear them plain-as-day. Fortunately, the sound was only in the bathroom so it wasn't like it kept us up at night. It was just a little weird. Overall, a great stay and I will definitely stay there again.

I had a very pleasant three-night stay at Affinia and would happily return. My room faced the avenue, with a surprisingly open view of the city rooftops and a nice glimpse of the river between buildings. Traffic was noticeable during the afternoon, but once the windows were shut the room was quiet enough for uninterrupted sleep. The decor is not ultra-modern, but it felt warm and well maintained rather than dated, with comfortable furniture and thoughtful lighting. The bathroom was especially roomy for the area, with a deep tub, strong shower pressure, and plenty of counter space for two people's toiletries. Front desk staff were friendly without being overly formal, and the location made it easy to walk to restaurants and transit.
The room looked tired, the hallway noise carried straight through the door, and our shower barely stayed warm. For the price, The James felt more frustrating than stylish.

I had a really enjoyable three-night stay at the Hard Rock Hotel. The room was stylish and comfortable, with a surprisingly good bed and plenty of space for my luggage. Breakfast was better than expected: the buffet had fresh fruit, eggs, pastries, and decent coffee, while the made-to-order options were worth the small extra charge. Every staff member I dealt with was friendly without being overbearing, especially at check-in and in the restaurant. The hotel has an energetic atmosphere, but my room was quiet at night; I only heard a little hallway noise on the first evening. Rates were not cheap, yet the location, service, and overall experience made the price feel fair. I would happily stay here again.
Our stay at the Conrad was genuinely relaxing, with a beautifully appointed room, exceptionally comfortable bed, and friendly staff who made everything feel effortless from check-in onward.

Booked a 'Sound of Your Stay' package but the guitar in the room was locked away, staff seemed annoyed when I asked about it. Room felt worn, AC rattled all night, and the pool had a weird smell. Not the vibe you'd expect from this brand.

We stayed at the Sheraton for a long weekend and honestly, it exceeded my expectations. The check-in process was smooth, and the front desk agent actually acknowledged our status tier and upgraded us to a room facing the city, which was a lovely surprise. The room itself was spotless and the bed was, as expected, incredibly comfortable--I slept better there than I do at home. The location was great for walking to restaurants and the water.

The only minor hiccup was the pool area being a bit crowded on Saturday afternoon, but we just went back in the morning and had it almost to ourselves. The lobby bar had a great vibe too, perfect for winding down with a craft cocktail. The staff throughout the hotel were consistently polite and helpful. All in all, a really solid, stress-free stay. We'll likely be back.

I had a very pleasant stay at the Hyatt and felt the experience was worth the price, especially considering the central location and consistently helpful staff. My room was bright, clean, and more spacious than expected, with a comfortable bed and plenty of outlets near the desk. The bathroom was spotless and modern, with good water pressure, soft towels, and a walk-in shower, although counter space was a little limited. Wi-Fi connected quickly and stayed reliable throughout, including during video calls and streaming. Despite being near a busy road, the room was surprisingly quiet at night; I only heard occasional hallway noise in the morning. Breakfast was fresh and convenient, and check-in was efficient. I would happily stay here again.

The Hyatt exceeded expectations--the lake view from my room was stunning, and the lobby coffee bar became my morning ritual. Staff remembered my name by day two, which felt genuinely thoughtful. A smooth, hassle-free stay from check-in to checkout.

I really wanted to love Hotel Monaco given the price, but our stay fell flat. The noise was the worst part -- our room faced the street, and between the bar downstairs and the streetcar clanging until well past midnight, sleep was nearly impossible even with earplugs. At nearly $400 a night, you'd expect soundproofing, decent towels, and a working thermostat; we got none of the above. The room also felt smaller than the photos suggested, and the 'luxury' wallpaper was peeling near the AC unit. Breakfast was a genuine letdown too: a cold buffet with watery eggs and stale pastries, not worth the $28 upcharge. Honestly, the two nights felt long rather than too short, and we checked out early on the last morning. For that kind of money, I expected far more. We won't be back.

I really wanted to like the Hotel Allegro, but it felt like a missed opportunity at every turn. The location is fine, but walking into the room felt like stepping back into 1992, with tired floral curtains and worn, scuffed furniture that absolutely did not match the photos online. Cleanliness was a major letdown; I found a hair on the pillowcase and the bathroom grout was stained and grimy. The breakfast was chaotic and cheap--powdered eggs, stale pastries, and lukewarm coffee that ran out quickly. Honestly, the place felt overpriced for what you get, especially when there are better options nearby. The bed was comfortable enough, but that's the only positive. The hallways had a strange, musty odor, too. For the money I spent, I expected a charming, updated boutique experience, but instead I left feeling relieved to check out. I can't recommend it unless you're purely after a bed for one night.

We arrived at the Omni on 2nd September for a 6 day stay. I took ill when I left the plane after travelling from Manchester so I saw more of the room than I anticipated. I couldn't go out for 4 days. The room was spacious and clean. The bed was extremely comfortable. The bathroom was large and very clean. What more could you ask. We had coffee and juice left outside our door every morning at the time we requested. I managed to go to the 5th floor to see the sun terrace (outside the gym) Having a sun terrace in a city hotel is a great idea but the terrace was a bit grim. A few sunbeds on a concrete floor. There was also noise from an air conditioning unit. It could do with a bit of cheering up. What I saw of Chicago was very pleasing, it has something for everyone. Would I go back to the Omni? yes I would.

I expected more from the Hard Rock given the price and branding. Our room looked worn, with scuffed furniture and a bathroom that felt cramped and poorly maintained; the shower curtain smelled damp and the sink drained so slowly it pooled during use. The window faced a parking structure and service area, not the city view advertised in the booking photos, so keeping the curtains open was hardly appealing. At check-in, the front desk agent was distracted and barely acknowledged our concerns about the room. Noise from the hallway and bass from somewhere below continued well after midnight, and the mattress was lumpy enough that I woke up repeatedly. We left tired and disappointed.

The Ambassador East is located in the Gold Coast neighborhood of Chicago. It is just a few blocks from the train station, so it was easy to get anywhere in town. The hotel is a National Historic Landmark so the lobby is elegant and beautiful. We loved the Pump Room bar with tons of B & W photos of celebrities. The service was wonderful and everyone was friendly and helpful.
The Talbott felt wonderfully welcoming, with a spotless room, plush bed, and helpful staff who made check-in easy. Loved being able to walk to nearby shops and restaurants.

I expected more from the Knickerbocker given the rate and the location. The lobby looks polished, but the experience fell apart once we got upstairs. Our room was surprisingly worn, with scuffed furniture, a stained chair, and an air conditioner that rattled loudly all night. Housekeeping missed our room the first day, and after calling twice we only received fresh towels, not the cleaning we requested. The shower pressure was weak and the bathroom door would not stay shut. Staff at the desk were courteous enough, but seemed overwhelmed and offered little beyond an apology. The rooftop was crowded and service there was painfully slow. Being close to Times Square was convenient, but it also meant constant noise. For the money, I would choose another hotel next time.

The Swissotel's location is genuinely its only saving grace, putting you right in the heart of everything, which was a godsend for our business meetings. Unfortunately, that's where the positives end. My room on the tenth floor faced the courtyard, so the promised city view was a dull, concrete wall. Worse, the so-called 'soundproofing' is a myth; I could hear the housekeeping carts rumbling at 7 AM and the muffled television from the room next door well into the night. It was exhausting. Breakfast was a chaotic, overpriced affair. The scrambled eggs were watery, the pastries tasted stale, and the coffee machine had a queue that snaked around the entire buffet. By the second morning, I'd given up and grabbed a croissant from a nearby cafe. For the nightly rate, this level of noise, bland food, and grim outlook feels like a serious letdown. I left more tired than when I arrived. A real shame for such a prime spot.

I expected more from the Omni given the rates and downtown location. Our room looked tired, with scuffed furniture, a stained chair, and a bathroom fan that rattled loudly whenever the light was on. The bed was fine, but the air conditioner cycled all night and made sleep difficult. Check-in took nearly 25 minutes because only one person was working while a line formed behind us. When I mentioned the noise the next morning, the response was polite but no one followed up. Housekeeping also skipped our room despite the service request being on the door. The location was convenient, and the lobby is attractive, but those positives did not make up for the lack of attention. For the price, I would choose another hotel next time.

I booked this hotel with great expectations. I had family visiting from outside the country and wanted them to have a good experience in Chicago. Upon arriving to the hotel (at the exact time I indicated in my reservation) I was told I've been 'downgraded' to a lesser quality room. I travel very often and never had this before. Moreover, I did not hear a single 'I'm sorry', it was like usual business. What bothered me the most was that the receptionist kept telling me 'I will decrease the rate for you' 'what do you think, nice eh?' like he was doing me a favor!!!! They decreased the rate to that of the rooms they gave us of course (which is the legal thing to do, since I am sure is illegal to charge me for one room and give me a lesser value one for the same money). They did not care that I wanted higher level room independent of value. I did not know what to say, since this never happened to me before, also with family present did not want to start arguing. The rooms were nice (not as nice as I thought) and location is good, however be aware that they might not honor your reservation and not even apologize for this. That is enough for me not to go back again.

The Palmer House has a beautiful lobby with a great bar and restaurant. The rooms are way too small!!! Two people in a room with a King size bed can barely move around. Not enough room for two suitcases. Our room was very outdated-reminded us of the movie The Shining. VERY NOISY!!!! Don't expect a quiet stay. You can hear EVERYTHING that your neighbors are doing and saying not to mention everything that is happening in the hallways. We requested a room change as soon as we checked in. The room that we originally were in had a huge square cut out of the wall that had exposed pipes, bricks, dirt and dust. Oh and the construction for their renovations starts at 7 a.m. during the week. We will never stay at the Palmer House again. You are better off spending a few more dollars at a different hotel.

I had a very comfortable three-night stay at the Hilton while in town for work. The lobby was busy in the evenings, but check-in was handled quickly and the front desk team was genuinely pleasant, even when I arrived later than planned. My room was quiet, clean, and had a good-sized desk where I could actually get some work done. The bed was excellent and the blackout curtains made it easy to sleep in after a long day. Breakfast had more variety than I expected, with fresh fruit, eggs, pastries, and decent coffee. I also appreciated having a gym that was clean and not overcrowded early in the morning. The location made getting around simple. I would happily stay here again.

Stayed in April for two nights. I hesitated selecting the Sheraton becaue I had a very poor stay there earlier this year. As far as I'm concerned, that's two strikes and I won't give them a chance at # three. Doormen wouldn't help on arrival, huge line at c/i, lousy room, malfunctioning remote, unresponsive staff, and incorrect bill. If you want to be close to Michigan Ave, try the Westin or Intercontinental and spare yourself the problems. I don't understand why certain places never improve. Is it that tough to properly train a staff?

My wife and I came to spend the weekend in downtown Chicago for shopping and we found this Conrad hotel well located close to everything downtown and of a size that doesn't make you feel lost in the Convention world. We have had this feeling when staying at larger hotels in the past. Our Suite has view on Michigan avenue with a bit of the Lake at the end. Staff was very professional, pleasant and friendly making us feel very comfortable. Internet is free n the rooms and I am making my review from there.

Checked in late and left far too soon--the bed was so plush I slept through my alarm twice. The decor felt elegantly current, not gimmicky, and the bathroom's rainfall shower made morning prep a genuine treat.

I'd heard the Talbott was a classic Chicago institution, so I booked a weekend here expecting charm. What I got was a tired room with threadbare carpet and a bathroom that smelled faintly of mildew no matter how often I ran the fan. The 'courtyard view' turned out to be a brick wall and a dumpster. Service was indifferent--I waited 20 minutes at the front desk while two staffers argued about a schedule, and nobody acknowledged me. The air conditioning rattled all night, and the pillows were flat as pancakes. Location is decent, near the Gold Coast, but you're paying for the address, not the experience. Breakfast was overpriced and lukewarm. Honestly, I'd rather stay at a chain next time. This place needs a serious refresh and a dose of hospitality training. Won't be back.

We stayed at this hotel for a conference. The lobby and the conference areas were immaculate. The restaurants (one of which was Shula's Steakhouse) and bars were great. The saff was exteremely helpful. The rooms left a lot to be desired...Our nonsmoking room smelled of smoke. The A/C system was ancient and tempermental, and the bathroom was old and in need of a makeover. It was surprising to see since the physical plant was so nice. We would choose, however, to stay elsewhere. Espcially for the money we paid.

Paid over $400 a night and barely slept--the walls are paper-thin, and I could hear every hallway conversation until 2 AM. Staff were polite but dismissive when I asked to move, and for that price, this place simply wasn't worth it.
Despite the convenient location, the Sofitel was disappointing: traffic noise kept me awake most of the night, and the indifferent staff barely acknowledged our concerns.

We got an awesome deal through Priceline for a Friday - Sunday stay at $75 for each night. The hotel is very centrally located on Michigan Avenue 'The Magnificent Mile'. You can walk to a ton of shops & there are plenty of restaurants handy as well. The hotel staff was very friendly, and the room itself was gorgeous. Very modern decor. Not drab & typical like most other chain hotels. If staying in Chicago we definitely will be staying there again. Price for valet parking overnight was insane ($42/day), but what do you expect in a big city.
Really enjoyed my stay at the Hilton--the room was spotless and quiet, the bed incredibly comfortable, and the staff made check-in feel effortless. The breakfast selection was a pleasant bonus.

Hard Rock exceeded our expectations for a fun, comfortable stay. The lobby and room decor felt fresh rather than overdone, with stylish music-themed details and everything looking well maintained. Our room faced the city, and the evening skyline view from the window was a real highlight. Staff members were upbeat, quick to help with directions, and remembered our names when we returned later in the day. Breakfast had a good mix of hot options, fruit, pastries, and made-to-order eggs; the coffee was better than typical hotel coffee too. It was busy, but tables were cleared quickly and service stayed friendly. We would happily stay again.
Slept like a log at the Sheraton--surprisingly quiet despite the downtown location, and the city skyline view from my floor was a treat. Wifi was fast and never dropped once. Would happily return.

The staff made us feel genuinely welcome from the moment we arrived, and the rooftop pool was the perfect escape after a day exploring. Our room was spotless and quiet, making it incredibly easy to relax. I'd happily return.

If you have not tried the Millennium Knickerbocker for a stay in Chicago, do it now! We have stayed (and enjoyed) at the Drake, Intercontinental and others, but we always now come back to the Knickerbocker. Why? If 'Charlie' the doorman is on duty and you pull up, he will welcome you. He'll probably ask your name. Why? Because he wants to call you by your name every time he will see you during your visit. Somehow he even lets the other employees know your name and all of a sudden, doorman, receptionist, bellman, waiter are referring to you by name. The employees are what makes this hotel. Yes, it has everything to offer like all hotels, but the others don't have the fine people (including the cleaning staff) these folks have. Try it, you will like it. We look forward to our next visit already...

I stayed at Affinia for a long weekend and honestly came away pleasantly surprised. The location is a massive win--you're right in the middle of everything, yet the rooms stay quiet enough for a solid sleep. I had a kitchenette, which I wasn't expecting, and it came in handy for breakfasts before heading out. The bed was firm but comfy, and the blackout curtains actually worked. Staff at the front desk were friendly without being overbearing, and they let me leave my bags after checkout without any fuss. The gym was small but had what I needed--free weights and a few machines. Wi-Fi held up fine for streaming. It's not fancy, but everything felt clean and well-maintained. I'd definitely book here again for the value and convenience.

I'll admit I was a little wary about the decor after seeing some older photos online, but honestly the lobby's marble floors and dark wood paneling felt more classic than dated--our room had a subtle retro charm that grew on me. Breakfast was a pleasant surprise: freshly baked croissants, made-to-order omelets, and a fantastic local honey that I piled onto thick-cut sourdough. The view from our fifth-floor window overlooked the treetops and a sliver of the harbor, golden at sunrise, which made morning coffee feel like a small ceremony. Yes, this place isn't cheap, but between the spotless linens, quiet corridors, and genuinely helpful staff who remembered our coffee order by day two, I'd call it fair value. I'd happily return for a weekend treat.
Hotel Monaco was a pleasant stay: the bathroom was spotless with good water pressure, the room stayed wonderfully quiet, Wi‐Fi was reliable, and I slept deeply in the comfortable bed.

The Conrad sounded promising, but the reality fell flat. The room was dated and the air conditioning barely worked, making for a restless night. Staff seemed overwhelmed and distant, which really dampened the whole experience for the price.

I have stayed at the James a few times, it is my go to hotel in Chicago. This last trip makes me think it is time to start looking for other options. The Good: Location is awesome, just off Michigan Ave, Trader Joe's across street for some healthier snacking. It is a great location, easy to walk most anywhere. The door staff are very friendly and helpful. The overall feeling is modern, upbeat. Turn down service with cookie is nice. Free Wifi (which worked to varying degrees throughout stay) The Bad: They claim to be a 4.5 star hotel, which to me, means better then a 4 star and online with a 5 star (without a pool). They used to have Kiehls toiletries and now have 'Harmony' brand. Additionally, they now have the large bottles attached to the wall which you get to share with the other guests that stayed in the room before you. It is what I would expect from Holiday Inn or my gym, but not a 4.5 star hotel. I asked about the switch (mainly because when I booked they still had Kiehls in website description) and they claimed that the reason they went the communal bottle route was to be 'green'. That is hard to believe, as it's not like the hotel is making other efforts to be green (they still have incandescent light bulbs, housekeeping leaves the lights and radio on when they do turn down, they don't recycle in room, etc). They are obviously trying to cut costs, and it shows. More: the rooms are in need of some updating, they are looking somewhat tired. My third floor room was quite loud with the motorcyclers trying to prove their manhood out front (not their fault). Don't take the stairs (as the stairwell is straight out of horror movie), even though the wait for one of the two elevators might be awhile. The phone staff was fairly rude (granted, they didn't like me questioning their toiletry change). I feel bad giving such a low rating, but it really did not come close to my expectations (from previous stays there). I will start trying out new hotels in the area.

We booked a standard room for a weekend escape and were genuinely impressed by the level of quiet. Despite the hotel being fully booked, we never heard a peep from the corridors or neighboring rooms--the insulation is superb. The Wi-Fi was a pleasant surprise, too; I streamed a movie on my laptop in bed with zero buffering, and my partner's video call in the lounge area was crystal clear. The bathroom was a highlight: a walk-in rain shower with excellent water pressure and those lovely, thick Hermes amenities. The room itself was spotless--fresh linens, not a speck of dust on the surfaces, and the carpet smelled clean, which is rare. We slept like logs and left feeling genuinely rested. Only wish we'd stayed another night.
Homewood was a comfortable surprise--our room was clean and quiet, the bed slept well, and the staff made check-in easy. The complimentary breakfast was a nice start each morning.

Stayed here for four nights on a work trip, and honestly, the Intercontinental more than lived up to its name. The lobby is grand without feeling stuffy, and the check-in process was smooth even though we arrived a bit early. They held our bags and texted us the moment the room was ready, which was a nice touch. The room itself was quiet, well-insulated from street noise, and the bed was genuinely comfortable--I slept better here than I do at home most nights. The pool area is worth a visit even if you aren't swimming; it's got that old-school charm that makes you feel like you've stepped back in time. Breakfast buffet was pricey but generous, with made-to-order eggs that weren't overcooked. Staff were consistently friendly, from the valet to the housekeeping team. Would happily book again.

We stayed here from Nov. 30 to Dec 2 and had a wonderful time. The hotel is just beautiful and the service was excellent from check in to the maid staff to the bartenders in Kitty O'Shea's. We had a room with a king bed that was very comfortable and had very nice feather pillows. You can request other types if you have a problem with feathers. The large flat screen TV was very nice. Bath products were by Crabtree & Evelyn and included shampoo, conditioner, mouthwash and bady lotion. Plenty of coffee was provided. We drank and had snacks at Kitty O'Shea's. The crowd was fun and there was live Irish folk music each night. Good selection of beer and good Shepards Pie, Cheese Dip and Crisps! The location worked very well for us. We walked to the Art Museum and Buddy Guys Blues Club is right across the street. And shopping was a breeze using the shuttle! The cab ride to the Museum of Science and Industry was quite far though and cost about $15 each way. An excellent weekend getaway!

everything that i read from other reviews was pretty much on the money, they have excellent customer service, the employees there really cared about their guests, there was always coffee, tea, hot chocolate in the lobby, good hot breakfast and dinner with wine and beer, the doormen were nice and willing to help out for directions, the room did the job, there was a kitchen, 2 flat screen tv's, and a pullout couch included, it was close to the 'eL', but for us we found the buses to be more useful. I would recommend getting a pass, we got a 3 day pass and it was well worth it for $14 which we got at jewel osco, not too far from the hotel, for the most part the majority of the people that were there were older people on a business trip and families, but us three girls didn't mind, so i would definitely recommend this place, it was one of the cheapest places were found out of all the other hotels.

I stayed at The Talbott for 3 nights on business and was very pleased. The staff was friendly as can be immediately confirming the lore of the midwest. I was upgraded to a suite which was bigger than my apartment and certainly more luxurious. The free wi-fi came in handy as I needed to work remotely while there. Everything from the comfort of the bed to the staff and location made this a great stay. Oh, and I got to workout at the huge Equinox right next door for free.

My family and I stayed at the Hyatt on Wacker Dr. on March 27, 2012. We were excited about the great price we got for your 4-star hotel through priceline. Unfortunately, we were not impressed. In the past, we have stayed at the Hyatt in downtown San Diego for spring break on the Marina, but chose to stay closer to home this year. The room was not clean to our standards when we arrived, even though we paid for an upgrade. We asked for it to be cleaned while we were sight seeing and were assured it would be looked after. Upon our return, nothing had been moved in the room to re-clean including the tea my sons had made prior to our excursion so I can only assume, it wasn't even checked as promised. We only had 3 towels for the 4 of us and had to call for more. They were promptly delivered but room service took 40 + minutes to deliver us a knife and corkscrew we essentially paid for because we felt compelled to tip even though we had to call and ask for it twice! The curtains were dirty and frayed by the vacuuming, the bed skirt had a foreign stain on it, the honor bar/fridge was gouged and dirty, too! The mirror was dirty and the beds appeared to have been jumped on - not neat and tidy at all....There were boxes of trash in the hall and an old refrigerator or two as well. Very disappointing to say the least. I have buyer's remorse and wish we had just taken the train home and stayed in our own beds! We were compensated for our upgrade - $20.00 but given the price of parking, taxes, and etc. at this point I wouldn't recommend this Hyatt to anyone. My husband travels and uses his Hyatt business travel points quite often and also expected better from your 4-star hotel. I felt compelled to let you know how unhappy we were with your facility.
Not worth the hype at all. Our room smelled musty, the AC barely worked, and housekeeping skipped our floor twice. For the price we paid, the Monaco felt tired and understaffed. Won't be back.

I expected more from Hard Rock, but the stay felt overpriced and poorly managed. The bathroom looked stylish at first, yet the shower drain backed up and left water across the floor, while the towels were thin and worn. Staff at check-in seemed distracted and barely acknowledged our concerns; when we called about the drain, no one came until the next afternoon. Noise was another major issue, with loud hallway conversations, doors slamming, and music thumping late into the night. Even with earplugs, I slept in short stretches and woke up exhausted. The location was convenient, but I would not return unless service and soundproofing improve.
Disappointing stay at The Knickerbocker: the room felt worn, service was oddly slow, and street noise kept us awake despite the premium price. I expected a much more polished experience.
The Palmer's dated decor and thin walls made for a noisy night, though the room was clean. I was relieved the stay was only one night, as it felt disappointing overall.
Gorgeous property with stunning views, and the staff went out of their way to make our stay special. Rooms were spacious and immaculate. Would absolutely come back!
Sofitel was wonderfully quiet at night, with a lovely city view from our room. The marble bathroom felt luxurious, and the comfort and service made the rate feel well worth it.

The room had a musty smell, and the corners were dusty, which made the short stay feel far too long--and spotty Wi-Fi only added to the frustration. Location was central, but that didn't rescue an otherwise disappointing visit.

Great location near Times Square, but the lobby's dated decor and a room that smelled musty soured things fast. Breakfast was a sad, cold buffet. For the price, I expected much more from the Knickerbocker.

Apart from the location, great, but it stops there. Upon check-in, I was informed I would have a queen bed. I asked for a king size bed, and I was told there would be a charge for going up to a king. GIVE ME A BREAK, a surcharge for going from a queen to a king. When I got up to the room, it was like a oven. I could not get the air to work and needed to call twice before getting service. Everything in the room had a charge associated to it, even down to the coffee, $1.00. Now what's up with that? I was very disappointed in the size of the bathroom. Very small. I have stayed there twice and with so many other options, I feel this will be my last.

We just returned from 4 nights at the Ambassador East. What a gem! The location in the Gold Coast neighborhood is perfect for finding restaurants and walking the Magnificent Mile. There is a train station about 2 blocks away. The room was very comfortable, with nice amenities, and there is free Internet service on the 2nd floor. Best of all was the bell and lobby staff! They really went out of their way to be helpful and greeted us warmly each time we left and arrived. I would say that this was the nicest hotel staff I've encountered in all my travels.
The room looked dated, and despite the Fairmont name, service felt slow and indifferent. Breakfast was overpriced, and the noise from the hallway made sleep difficult.

We stayed at the Fairmont for four nights over a long weekend and honestly have very few complaints. Our room on a higher floor had a gorgeous view of the mountains and the water, and the bed was one of the most comfortable I've ever slept in at a hotel - I actually looked up the mattress brand before checking out. Housekeeping was prompt and thorough every day, and the front desk straightened out a small billing mix-up within minutes without any fuss. The pool area never felt crowded even though the hotel was fairly full, and the concierge booked us a last-minute dinner reservation at a place that turned out to be the highlight of our trip. Location is excellent too, an easy walk to everything we wanted to see. None of this is cheap, but you get what you pay for. We'd happily return.

My stay at Affinia was far below what I expected for the rate. The room looked tired, with scuffed furniture and a weak air conditioner, and the view was mostly a brick wall and fire escapes. Noise was another issue: I could hear doors slamming in the hallway well past midnight and traffic started early in the morning. Wi-Fi technically connected, but it dropped every few minutes and was too slow for a video call. Breakfast was disappointing as well--lukewarm eggs, dry pastries, and coffee that tasted like it had been sitting out for hours. The staff were polite when approached, but no one seemed able to resolve the internet problem. Convenient location aside, I would not choose this hotel again.

I wasn't entirely sure what to expect from the Fairmont, but I left genuinely impressed--and a little sad to go. The bed was so comfortable that I slept through my alarm twice, which never happens at home. Our room faced the inner courtyard, and aside from the faint hum of the HVAC, it was wonderfully quiet; I heard zero hallway noise all weekend. The wifi held up perfectly, even during evening video calls from the lounge. If anything, the three nights felt too brief--I'd have happily stayed another day just to use the pool more. Service was attentive without hovering, and the breakfast spread was worth waking up for. Minor quibble: the bathroom door stuck slightly, but that hardly overshadowed an otherwise polished stay. I'd return in a heartbeat.

I had a very enjoyable two-night stay at the InterContinental. My room was spotless when I arrived, including the bathroom, desk, and even the windows, which made settling in easy. The bed was comfortable, and housekeeping kept everything equally tidy after the first night. I was on a higher floor with a broad view over the city lights and rooftops; it was especially nice with coffee in the morning. Wi-Fi connected quickly and stayed reliable enough for video calls and streaming without any frustrating dropouts. The lobby staff were pleasant and efficient, even when I came back late. Honestly, the visit felt too short--I would have happily stayed another couple of nights to enjoy the room and location a bit more.

I unfortunately stayed for 3 nights at the Knickerbocker Hotel ...I should have checked out on day 1. The bathrooms were filthy dirty with tangled hairs on the floor behind the door and after a few nights of scratching and the feeling of skin crawling...I pulled the bed away from the bedhead and watched as little rice sized brown bugs scurried over the white sheets...bed bugs! Which I might add the hotel are saying are flying insects from the windows being left open from when the window cleaners were there (fortunately I took photos to the contrary) Finding the bed bugs...I looked at the mattress protector and pillows and found long hairs on both...I was disgusted at the hygeine and would never stay again at this establishment.
The Talbott was a pleasant stay: reliable Wi-Fi, a spotless and comfortable room, and an easy walk to restaurants and shopping. It felt like excellent value for the price.

The Affinia turned out to be a genuinely pleasant surprise. The bathroom was a standout--spacious, flawlessly clean, with a rainfall shower that had excellent pressure, plus those lovely little Aesop toiletries that felt like a proper treat. Check-in was swift, and the staff, from the front desk to the bellman, were wonderfully attentive without being overbearing; they even remembered my preference for a high floor without me having to ask twice. My only real complaint is that my two-night stay felt far too short to fully enjoy the cozy, modern room and the cozy lobby bar. For the location and the level of service, I honestly felt the price was fair--not a steal, but certainly worth it for a comfortable, hassle-free city break. I'd happily return.

We stayed at the Hotel Ambassador for four nights in early October and honestly it exceeded what we expected for the price. Our room on the fifth floor was a good size, spotless, and the bed was genuinely comfortable, which matters a lot after long days of walking around. The front desk staff deserve a special mention: they gave us great restaurant recommendations, arranged a late checkout without any fuss, and even printed our boarding passes when the business center was busy. Breakfast was a highlight too, with fresh pastries, decent coffee, and eggs made to order. Location was excellent, a short walk to the metro and plenty of cafes nearby. Only tiny complaint was slow elevator service at peak times, but that's minor. Would absolutely return next trip.

Stayed three nights for a work conference and honestly, the Hotel Monaco was the best part of the trip. The location is perfect--steps from the French Quarter but quiet enough that you actually sleep. My room had this great little balcony overlooking the courtyard, and the bed was absurdly comfortable. I'm picky about pillows, and these were just right.

What really stood out was the staff. From the valet who remembered my name every morning to the front desk clerk who printed my boarding pass without me even asking, everyone seemed genuinely happy to help. The evening wine hour in the lobby is a nice touch too--met some fellow travelers and actually chatted instead of staring at my phone.

Only minor gripe: the bathroom sink drained a bit slowly. But honestly, I'd book again in a heartbeat. That rooftop hot tub at sunset? Worth it alone. Great value for the vibe.

My stay at Swissotel was brief, but it felt like exactly the right amount of time to unwind. The room was spotless on arrival, with fresh linens, a perfectly clean bathroom, and no dust or overlooked corners. I especially appreciated the quiet atmosphere; the bed was very comfortable and the blackout curtains helped me sleep deeply through the night. Breakfast was a real highlight, with a generous selection of fresh fruit, pastries, hot dishes, eggs, and good coffee. Staff kept the buffet tidy and were attentive without being intrusive. I would happily return for a longer visit next time.

Hotel Amalfi was a comfortable choice for our weekend, with a quiet room, genuinely friendly staff, and an easy location for getting around. Breakfast was fresh, and everything felt clean and well cared for.

Fantastic spot for exploring the city--everything was walkable. Staff were warm and efficient, and our room had a gorgeous rain shower. Despite being central, it was surprisingly peaceful at night, letting us recharge completely.

We stayed at the InterContinental for three nights and honestly wished we'd booked a full week. Our room on the 21st floor was spotless, not a stray hair or smudge anywhere, and housekeeping kept it that way without us ever having to ask twice. The view over the city skyline was spectacular, especially at dusk when all the lights came on. The bed was comfortable, though I'd expect nothing less at this price point. Wifi was fast and reliable throughout, which mattered since I had to hop on a couple of video calls from the room and never had a single dropout. Breakfast was excellent too. A few small bumps at check-in with the room not being ready, but nothing that soured the experience. Would absolutely return.
Hotel Allegro was a fun downtown base--our room was quiet, the bed was genuinely comfortable, and the front desk pointed us to a great late-night pizza spot. Would happily return.

Great stay at the Hilton--spotless bathroom with a big tub, strong wifi throughout, and breakfast had fresh fruit and made-to-order omelets. Walking distance to everything downtown. Would happily return.

My wife and I redeemed some of my Hilton Reward Points to stay a few nights at the Palmer House. The hotel is absolutely beautiful. From the moment you walk into the lobby you can tell that this place is nice. As we were Diamond members we got upgraded to a suite which was great because we were provided access to their executive lounge (free food & drinks). The service was excellent and the location of the hotel is within walking distance of many sights on the south side of Chicago. I would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone interested in coming to Chicago.

Going to the Internet Retailer 2010 at the last minute and this was the only hotel left available with shuttle services. First of all, from reading other reviews, now I know I got ripped @ $249 a night when Priceline folks are sniping these rooms for $79 (albiet, I got free wifi). The hotel is nice; but it can only get so nice for an oldie...no matter how much money you dump into it. Shower head was really low (I'm 6'1'), water pressure was low. It is in a decent part of town with a hype bar close by (check out reviews on Yelp!) For some off reason I ended up with two double beds (they asked me a few times if I was traveling alone). If traveling here: 1 - make sure you get a better deal than I did 2 - confirm your exact needs with reservation over the phone and in person 3 - Don't have super high hopes My room was neither up to par as a business class (although the 22nd floor is called the executive floor) nor was it a good fit for the romantic couple...it wasnt even spacious enough for those last minute get awayers (sp?) trying to save money.

My stay at the Hyatt was frustrating from the start. The room faced a busy intersection, and even on the 18th floor I could hear traffic, sirens, and late-night voices well past midnight. The view was mostly parking garages and office buildings, hardly what I expected for the rate. The mattress felt worn and the air conditioner clicked on and off constantly, so I slept in short stretches rather than actually resting. I booked two nights for a quick break, but by the second morning the stay felt far too long. Staff were polite, but a delayed response to my request for extra towels did not help. The lobby looked nice, yet the room itself felt dated and not worth the price.

I stayed at the Allegro in July for 4 nights for a business trip. The room was spotlessly clean and the bed was great. I had read reviews that said the bathrooms were tiny, but ours was perfectly fine, with funky, fun doors. The decor is a lot of fun. We were on the 15th floor and there was absolutely no street noise. The front desk staff was very friendly, and before we even made it to the desk, a lovely man took our bags and brought them up to our room within moments of our arrival. We were within walking distance to all the theaters and even walked one night all the way to Navy Pier. For people who were upset about no free coffee - there's a Dunkin Donuts about a block away. I definitely recommend this hotel!

Hotel Allegro was a great base for a long weekend downtown. The lobby has a fun, theatrical feel without being overdone, and the front desk team was genuinely friendly when we arrived late after a delayed flight. Our room was compact but thoughtfully arranged, with a very comfortable bed, good blackout curtains, and enough outlets near the desk to get some work done. I also appreciated that it was quiet at night despite being so close to the theaters and restaurants. We walked to the river, the Loop, and several shows with no trouble. The only minor issue was that the bathroom counter space was limited, but everything was spotless and well maintained. I'd happily stay here again for the location and welcoming service.

Stayed at the Fitzpatrick as a result of all of the glowing reviews on TripAdvisor and to avoid the normal corporate hotel. Good location but the room was dirty, and not just from the last housekeeping. It was dingy: a place where you needed the slippers they provided. And this was a suite. Also, the refrigerator was caked with ice and didn't work. Furthermore, because my travel agent had mixed up the dates I was to travel, I showed up a day late. The hotel said it wasn't a problem and that I wouldn't be charged for the no-show the night before. I had my travel desk verify this with the hotel management the same day. Then the Fitzpatrick charged me for both nights and refused to reverse the charges after many attempts to resolve. Neither I nor my corporate travel desk will use the Fitzpatrick again. Two dots only because it's in a good location and because the lobby was clean. I'm generally easy to please and slow to complain but this was bad.

We stayed at the Sheraton for three nights and left genuinely disappointed. The photos online promised a lovely outlook, but our 'view' was mostly a grey parking garage wall with a slice of rooftop AC units humming away. Breakfast was the biggest letdown: the scrambled eggs were lukewarm and watery, the fruit looked tired from the day before, and the coffee was so weak we ended up paying extra at a cafe across the street. Sleep was a struggle too. Even though our room was far from the elevator, the hallway noise carried badly, and every night around 11pm we could hear music and laughter from the bar two floors down until well past midnight. The bed itself was decent, but that hardly matters when the walls are this thin. For the price, we expected far better.

I really expected more from a property with the Swissotel name. Check-in took almost 40 minutes because the front desk seemed understaffed and confused about my reservation, and nobody apologized properly. The room itself was worn out: stained carpet, a shower head that dribbled water, and the AC made a rattling noise all night so I barely slept. Housekeeping skipped my room on the second day entirely and I had to call twice to get fresh towels. Breakfast was the biggest letdown; cold eggs, empty trays that stayed empty for 20 minutes, and a bill that somehow included items I never ordered. Location is convenient, sure, but at this price point I've stayed in much better hotels. For what they charge, the service should be flawless, not this sloppy. I won't be returning.

Honestly really disappointed with my stay at the Homewood. The ads make it look like a cozy extended-stay spot but the reality is way off. My first room had a stained couch and the AC rattled all night, so I barely slept. They moved me the next day, which was fine, but the new room's kitchenette was missing half the dishes and the dishwasher smelled weird. Housekeeping skipped my room twice despite my requests. The breakfast was the one bright spot the first morning, but by day three the eggs were cold and half the trays were empty with no staff around to restock. The location is okay, nothing special. For the price I expected a lot more. I won't be back and can't really recommend this place to anyone.

I expected a much smoother stay at Homewood, especially for the price. Check-in took nearly 25 minutes because the front desk was unattended, and no one apologized once they finally appeared. Our suite looked tired: stained carpet near the sofa, a sticky kitchen counter, and a bathroom fan that rattled loudly all night. The bed was reasonably comfortable, but the hallway noise started early and the walls seemed paper-thin. Breakfast was disappointing too--lukewarm eggs, empty coffee containers, and very little seating. I mentioned the cleanliness issues at checkout, but the response was basically a shrug. The location was convenient, but I would not choose this hotel again.

Honestly, I left the Hotel Amalfi feeling pretty deflated, especially given the price we paid. Check-in set the tone; we waited nearly twenty minutes while the sole receptionist struggled with a system that seemed to crash twice. Our 'sea view' room turned out to be a cramped box overlooking a construction site and a sliver of water, and the soundtrack was relentless drilling starting at 7 AM. The bed was hard as a rock, and the pillows were flat as pancakes. Breakfast was chaos--food lukewarm, coffee machine perpetually out of order, and not enough seating. It felt more like a hostel pretending to be a boutique hotel. The location is genuinely great, and I'll give the housekeeping credit for being thorough, but that doesn't make up for the noise, the uncomfortable room, and the manager's dismissive shrug when I complained. Save your money.

Staff were friendly, room was well kept like a typical Hyatt location. Hotel is huge, with two buildings and over 2000 rooms. Good location, close to Michigan Ave and the subway. Parking is $48/day. Ouch! I bid on it on Priceline for $59.

My stay at Homewood was more frustrating than relaxing. The room faced the parking lot, and although traffic was light, doors slamming and voices in the hallway carried late into the night. The bed looked comfortable but was much too firm for me, so I slept poorly and woke several times. Wi-Fi was another disappointment: it connected briefly, then slowed to a crawl whenever I tried to stream or join a work call, even after restarting the router connection. The room itself was reasonably clean, but the furniture showed wear and the bathroom needed better ventilation. For what I paid, I expected a quieter room, dependable internet, and a more comfortable night. Staff were polite when I mentioned the problems, but nothing was done to improve the stay.

I never write these reviews, but felt that it was important to state that this hotel should not be the #1 2008 travelers choice. Terrible Service, Lazy Doormen/bellmen/concierge/valet, Lack of Respect, allow dogs to bark all morning after multiple complaints, Phantom charges to room, front dest at checkout and checkin were pompus. The icing on the cake was me watching the doormen stand and watch while a father tried to open a door to push his stroller through with his infant son, and the doorman watched on doing nothing. Me and my girlfriend are young, look young in how we dress, but in all honesty make more money than most...and we were treated like cheap poor kids. I had dinner reservations at Spaiggia and wanted to order a car to pick us up, the concierge exclaimed that, 'You know its not jeans and running shoes right Mr. Blank?' Assuming I was too dumb to realize that a 5 star $200/person restraunt wont allow tennis shoes because I am young? Very Dissapointed. Very nice looking, comfortable beds, great room service, contemporary, younger crowd, but service was terrible.
Spent a restful night at the Fairmont; the city view was beautiful, the marble bathroom felt luxurious, and the comfortable room made the price seem well worth it.
Disappointing stay. The room smelled musty, the AC barely worked, and the 'free breakfast' was cold and picked over by 8am. Front desk staff were indifferent at check-in too. Won't be back.

The Fairmont looked impressive online, but the stay was a letdown for the price. My room faced a neighboring building and a rooftop full of air-conditioning units, so the 'city view' was mostly brick and machinery. Noise was another issue: I could hear doors slamming in the hallway and music from an event downstairs well past midnight. The room itself was comfortable enough, though the furniture showed wear and the bathroom needed better cleaning around the fixtures. Staff were polite at check-in, but not especially welcoming, and my request for a quieter room was brushed off without much explanation. With the high nightly rate and added fees, I expected a more polished experience. It was acceptable, but nowhere near worth what I paid.

My stay at the Affinia was a disappointment overall. The room looked tired, with scuffed furniture and a bathroom that could have used a deeper cleaning. Breakfast was especially underwhelming: the hot items were lukewarm, the coffee tasted stale, and the small buffet was repeatedly left empty during the morning rush. The WiFi was unreliable as well; it dropped several times and became so slow in the evening that I gave up trying to work. Noise was another problem, with doors slamming and conversations carrying clearly from the hallway late into the night. I had hoped for at least a decent city view, but my window faced a brick wall and a jumble of pipes. The location is convenient, but it did not make up for the poor condition and lack of comfort.

I have never experienced terrible service like this especially at such a highly rated hotel. I had booked the hotel room for my parents for their anniversary weekend and stopped by earlier in the week to have the charge for the room put on my card as a gift. When my parents arrived, they were told that the front desk staff was new and did not complete the charge correctly. My parents then had to charge their own anniversary trip. Additionally, my father had requested a non-smoking room to stay in and was reassured 3 times that his room was non-smoking. When my parents got to the room it reeked of smoke and there was an ashtray and matches on the desk tabletop. When my father caled down to the front desk to ask about this the guy at the front desk asked if my dad wanted him to come up and remove the ashtray and matches - something that would clearly not resolve the fact that they were put in a smoking room after being reassured 3 times that the room was non-smoking. NEVER AGAIN.

The breakfast buffet was a chaotic mess of congealed eggs and lukewarm coffee, and I barely slept thanks to a rattling AC unit. My 'city view' faced a brick wall, and the dusty corners under the bed made the whole room feel neglected.

The Intercontinental's classic lobby charms, though the room decor skews slightly tired. Still, the spotless bathroom and lakeside views justified the rate. My one-night stopover felt fleeting--I'd happily trade two more days there.
Breakfast was lukewarm and sparse, street noise kept us awake, and the dated decor felt tired. Our room overlooked a bleak parking lot, making the stay even less appealing.

I travelled to Chicago last week with my daughter for some Christmas shopping. We booked the Conrad based on the reviews on Tripadvisor. It lived up to all expectations. Great big room, with two king size beds. Very comfortable. Breakfast was great, loads of choice and plenty on the plate. Great location, connected to a shopping mall which was very useful the day it snowed. All and all, a great hotel and we would go back in the morning. Chicago is a great city with very friendly people.
Homewood looked worn down, with a noisy AC unit and a room that wasn't properly cleaned. Breakfast was sparse and the front desk seemed uninterested when I mentioned the issues.

Hotel Monaco was a great choice for a weekend downtown. The lobby has a fun, slightly quirky style without feeling overdone, and the front desk team was genuinely warm when we arrived early with our bags. Our room was quiet, very clean, and had a comfortable bed with plenty of pillows; I also appreciated the large windows and the little sitting area by the desk. We walked to restaurants, shops, and the theater in just a few minutes, which made it easy to come back and rest between plans. Coffee in the morning was a nice touch. The elevator was a little slow during the busy evening rush, but that was the only minor inconvenience. I'd happily stay here again.

The room was dingy and dusty, with hair on the pillows, and the indifferent staff barely acknowledged us. While the beach is close, the bleak view of a concrete wall made the stay feel like a total waste.

The Affinia is virtually the perfect hotel for a visit to Chicago. My wife and I stayed in an upgraded suite. Very large room, that is modern and has all the little touches. The staff was extremely helpful and professional. The location is excellent. The price is a good value for what you get. We simply couldn't find anything to criticize. Highly recommended!

Expected much more from the Fairmont. Our room wasn't ready at check-in, the staff seemed disinterested, and the pool area was crowded and noisy. For the price, honestly a pretty disappointing stay overall.

The Hotel Palmer was exactly what I needed after a long travel day, and honestly, it felt like a steal for the quality. My room was spotless, from the crisp white linens to the gleaming bathroom fixtures, and the housekeeping had clearly paid attention to every detail. The building itself is wonderfully solid--my room faced the street, but I heard nothing but a faint hum of traffic, which faded completely once I closed the window. I slept like a log on that firm, comfortable mattress; it was the best rest I'd had in weeks. The location is unbeatable, yet somehow the space felt serene and insulated from the bustle outside. For the price I paid, especially given the prime spot and the meticulous upkeep, I'd say it was well worth it. I will definitely be back.

I really wanted to like this place, given the historic charm, but our stay was a letdown from the moment we checked in. The front desk staff were curt and dismissive, barely looking up from their phones when we asked about late checkout. Our room, while visually nice, had a grimy film on the bathroom sink and hair on the baseboards that made me question the cleaning standards. Worse, I slept terribly; the walls were paper-thin, and I could hear every footstep and muffled conversation from the hallway until past midnight, plus some kind of mechanical hum from the AC unit that wouldn't shut off. The bed itself was lumpy, with a sagging middle that left my back aching by morning. For the price we paid, I expected far more attention to detail. A genuine disappointment that didn't live up to its reputation.

I expected more from a Sheraton, especially for the price. Check-in took nearly 30 minutes even though there was only one person ahead of me, and the front desk staff seemed distracted rather than apologetic. My room looked tired: stained carpet near the window, a rattling air conditioner, and a bathroom fan that ran loudly all night. The bed was comfortable enough, but the walls were so thin I could hear hallway conversations and the TV next door. Breakfast was overpriced and lukewarm, with empty trays left unfilled for a while. The location was convenient, but that was really the only positive. I mentioned the noise at checkout and got a polite nod, nothing more. Disappointing stay overall.
Loved the welcoming staff and spotless room at Omni; the bed was wonderfully comfortable, and the downtown location made dinner and sightseeing easy. Would happily stay again.

Stayed at the Talbott for over a week and enjoyed our stay. Room was a little noisy as we were next to the lift, but everything else made up for that. Positives: Bed was very comfortable, great to have real shower, free internet, gym usage, staff (all friendly) and location. Negative: Lift noise, lifts slow and restaurant (there are so many great restaurants around - don't bother staying in) Would stay again!

Honestly, I left feeling pretty let down. We booked the Ambassador for a weekend away, hoping for that boutique charm the photos suggest. Instead, we got peeling paint in the bathroom and a light fixture that flickered all night. The staff were polite, but stretched thin--we waited twenty minutes at the front desk just to get a simple question answered. Housekeeping never came until we called twice, and even then, they only dropped off towels. Our room faced the main street, and the soundproofing was a joke. You could hear every bus and siren until 2 AM. Location is convenient, sure, but for what they charged, I expected so much more. It felt tired, worn, and overlooked. Disappointed is putting it mildly--I won't be back and can't recommend it to anyone seeking even basic comfort.

Our trip was our annual anniversary trip. The hotel did not honor my choice of king size bed. Instead we received two double beds. This seriously decreased our enjoyment of our stay at the Hyatt. There were two cups of coffee complimentary in the room. No complimentary coffee anyplace else in the very large hotel. Location was more of a business district, not appropriate for pleasure trip. Employees of Hyatt were very friendly and helpful, other than the failure to deliver the reserved room.

Our third stay at the Homewood Suites Chicago proved to be just as great as the previous two. The staff are consistently friendly, polite and professional - and this applies whether they are working at the front door, servicing the rooms, managing the breakfast room or on the reception desk. They genuinely seem happy to be working here and can't do enough for their guests. The rooms are large and clean and seem to have good insulation from each other (we didn't hear a thing from our neighbours and the hotel was quite busy). The hotel is well placed for walking to the shops on Michigan Ave, or catching a bus or subway. There is a Jewel Osco and a Trader Joes each within a couple of blocks, which are perfect for stocking up on groceries etc. My husband heartily recommends 'Binnies Beverage Depot' for a huge variety of beer. Now all we need is an excuse to return to Chicago next year - then we can make it four years on the run at the Homewood Suites, because we wouldn't stay anywhere else!

Great place, great room, great location. Even though there was a big meeting going on (Rainbow Girls in all their enormous gowns) the only consequence for us was slow elevators. Ballroom is amazing, shops on ground floor a nice throwback. Lake views from upper floors -- we were on 17 I think -- are worth it. Concierge advice about restaurants etc was excellent. Definitly would return.

This hotel was very beautiful. I went with a group of 4 friends and we had a blast. It was very centrally located and was close to all sorts of transportation. The Continental breakfast was magnificent! I didn't see much of the staff but all of the men at the front door were extremely helpful.

Slept like a rock on the plush Fairmont bed, and the wifi never glitched once during my work calls. Waking up to that skyline view was the best part. Three nights honestly flew by--would happily have stayed another week.

Expected way more from the Hard Rock. The music theme is fun for about five minutes until you realize the walls are paper thin and the bar noise carries all night. Room was tired, AC rattled, staff seemed annoyed we even asked for anything. Won't be back.

Great stay at Hotel Palmer! The staff were incredibly welcoming and the room was spotless with a lovely view. Breakfast had plenty of options, and the location made exploring easy. Would happily return.
Our room was spotless, and the bathroom had a roomy shower with great water pressure. Breakfast was fresh and filling, while the friendly staff made check-in and every question easy.

I stayed at the intercontinental during the last weekend in September for a 'pleasure trip' -- the InterContinental was in a great location and the staff was excellent. The room was clean and comfortable -- and came equipped with a new LG flat panel tv. Had breakfast at Zest (hotel restaurant) -- a bit pricey but decent if you want a buffet. The hotel is in walking distance to millenium park, museums and the aquarium. There is also a lot of shopping - window shopping is best though, considering the sales tax is 9.5%! (and possibly raising to 11%) Great stay. I highly recommend it and would stay there again.

Stayed here for a conference and left genuinely underwhelmed. The room smelled musty, the AC rattled all night, and housekeeping never replaced our towels. Overpriced for what feels like a tired property that's clearly seen better days.

We stayed at the Conrad for four nights and I honestly can't find much to fault. The front desk team remembered our names after the first morning and even mailed back a charger we left behind in the lobby.
