Breakfast was a highlight: fresh pastries, made-to-order eggs, and strong coffee that rivaled the place around the corner. Our room on the 20th floor was remarkably quiet despite being in the middle of everything; once the door closed, we heard nothing but the hum of the AC. Wifi stayed fast and reliable throughout, which mattered since my husband had to join a few video calls. Housekeeping deserves a shout-out too. It's not the cheapest option in town, but we felt it was worth every cent and would happily return.

We stayed at the Intercontinental for a long weekend, and the location was unbeatable--right in the heart of the city, with the metro entrance steps away. I was worried about street noise, but our high-floor room was remarkably quiet; I slept like a log, deeper than I have in months. The bed was plush without being too soft, and blackout curtains did their job perfectly. Housekeeping kept the room spotless, fresh towels appeared twice daily, and the bathroom sparkled. The only minor hiccup was a slow elevator during checkout rush, but that didn't dampen our experience. If you want a serene, convenient, and impeccably clean base, this is it. I'd book again tomorrow without a second thought.

My husband attended a conference in Chicago for the weekend of June 22nd and I decided to tag along for the shopping! We flew into O'Hare and took a cab to the hotel, cost about $30. Everybody from the doorman to reception desk to concierge were extremely friendly and helpful. We had a room on the 9th floor which overlooked the construction, but we were hardly in the room so it didn't bother us. We were also never awakened due to construction noise and my husband is a very light sleeper. The room was clean and spacious enough for us. The bed is very comfy. We ate in the restaurant downstairs several times for breakfast and lunch and all meals were great. The location of this hotel is perfect. You are about 1&1/2 blocks from Michigan Ave and the Hancock tower. Can't beat that! There is also an adorable pet store called Tails In The City across from the hotel! I brought our dog back a couple of toys! They are very nice as well. All in all, no complaints. The hotel is clean and beyond what we were expecting. The staff is always friendly and the location is superb. It's a safe neighborhood-I walked around by myself and felt fine. We would definitely return.
Fresh, tasteful decor and a lovely view over the city made our room feel special. The central location was incredibly convenient, though our weekend stay felt far too short.

I really wanted to love this place, given the Sofitel name and the price point, but our stay was riddled with small letdowns that added up quickly. Check-in took an eternity, and the front desk agent seemed utterly indifferent, barely making eye contact while handing over our keys. Our room, though spacious, had a musty smell and a stained carpet near the minibar that we had to ask to have vacuumed twice.

The air conditioning sounded like a freight train all night, so sleep was almost impossible. Breakfast was another low point; the croissants were stale, and the coffee tasted burnt. I mentioned the AC issue at checkout, hoping for some acknowledgment, but the response was a shrug and a generic apology. For these rates, I expect polish, and honestly, we were relieved to leave. I'm not sure I'd gamble on a return visit.

I expected much more from a Fairmont stay, especially at the rate we paid. Check-in took nearly 30 minutes because the desk seemed understaffed, and nobody acknowledged the delay. Our room looked tired: scuffed furniture, a stained chair, and a bathroom fan that rattled all night. The air conditioning barely worked, so the room stayed stuffy despite several calls to the front desk. Housekeeping also missed our room one day and brought towels only after another long wait. Breakfast was expensive and surprisingly average, with lukewarm coffee and empty buffet trays not being refilled. The location was convenient, but that was about the only positive. This felt more like an aging business hotel than a luxury property.
Disappointing stay at the Fairmont: the room was only passably clean, the bathroom felt dated, and hallway noise kept us awake, despite the otherwise convenient downtown location.

I was genuinely surprised by how comfortable this stay turned out to be, especially given the hotel's slightly older reputation. The lobby has that classic, polished feel--marble floors and dark wood--and while the guest corridors show a few scuffs, my room itself felt fresh and well-kept, with a crisp white duvet and modern bedside USB ports. Breakfast was a real highlight: the made-to-order omelet station beat any generic buffet, and the fresh pastries were still warm at 7 a.m. I slept like a log on the firm mattress, and the blackout curtains actually did their job despite the bright streetlights below. The wifi was consistently strong--streamed a movie in bed without a single buffering pause. The only tiny disappointment was the pool being chilly, but that didn't dampen an otherwise smooth, efficient, and pleasant two nights. I'd happily book here again for business or a quick city break.

I thought the Swissotel was a great hotel. The rooms were very spacious and clean, especially for downtown Chicago standards. Most importantly, the rooms were quiet. I never heard people in the hallways when I was trying to sleep. The only downside was that the beds were not anything special. Sure, like all hotels in Chicago, this hotel caters to wealthy and/or business clients with ridiculous minibar and parking price. However, if you are aware of that prior to arrival, its not a big deal (ie finding a different place to park the car, bringing our own snacks for the room). It would be nice though if hotels such as the Swissotel had a microfridge in the room for guest use. Staff was very helpful. Bellmen instantly got cabs upon request, and the front desk was efficient and helpful. Overall, if I can get a good rate again, I'll stay at the Swissotel the next time I am in Chicago.

The Omni is really showing its age. The hallway smelled like old carpet and the air conditioner rattled all night, making sleep impossible. Staff were polite but offered little help. Definitely not worth the premium price.
The Hilton looked impressive online, but my room was dated, the air conditioning barely worked, and housekeeping skipped us entirely. For the price, I expected a much smoother stay.

The service was painfully slow and the staff seemed overwhelmed, though the room itself was clean. For these prices, the dated hallway carpet and the busted espresso machine in the cafe were a real letdown. I expected far more polish.

I really wanted to like this place, but the hotel james fell short in almost every way. The location is honestly the only bright spot -- it's walking distance to plenty of restaurants and shops, which made getting around easy. Unfortunately, that's where the positives end. Our room was not properly cleaned before check-in; there were crumbs on the desk and what looked like an old stain on the duvet. The bathroom was cramped and dated, with a shower that alternated between scalding and freezing no matter how carefully we adjusted the handle, and the Water dripped weakly the whole time. As for the staff, they seemed distracted and disinterested whenever we asked for anything, whether it was extra towels or a simple question about checkout. For the price we paid, I expected far more. Won't be returning.
The InterContinental looked impressive online, but my room felt tired, the air conditioning barely worked, and breakfast was chaotic. For the price, I expected much better attention to detail.

The view was mostly of other buildings, which was a letdown. While the room felt grungy and under-vacuumed, the location was decent for clubs. The bathroom, however, had clogged drains and a musty smell. Very disappointing for the price.

Stayed here for a conference and left feeling underwhelmed. The room was tired, with scuffed furniture and a view of a wall. Staff were polite but painfully slow, and the so-called luxury breakfast was cold and overpriced. For this price tag, I expected far more polish.
Breakfast was lukewarm and sparse, hallway noise kept us awake, the cramped bathroom felt dated, and our 'city view' was mostly a parking garage.

Really enjoyed our weekend at the Conrad. The room was quiet and beautifully finished, bed super comfy, and the concierge got us a last-minute dinner reservation when everything nearby was booked. wouldn't hesitate to come back.
The view was mostly a parking garage, and hallway noise kept me awake until late. Staff seemed indifferent when I mentioned it, making the stay feel disappointing.

This is a tough one to review... as the star ratings were from 1 star to 5 and had to figure out an average.... 2 is where it was. Here are my tips and props/complaints: Room: 1 Star. I had a corner suite. The room was pretty nasty actually (2703..STAY AWAY FROM IT!!!). There was a CONSTANT banging noise from above. When I first got in I thought it was the person above me bumping and grinding. After an hour, I knew even if it was someone high on speed and redbull would not be going that strong. Well, the sound continued on for 3 days. Not that I minded too much as I keep things on for white noise... but it sure would bug others. Also, there were about 10 cig burns on the carpet and sofa. In addition, it looked like someone left the iron on the sofa. Also, there is a gray furry pillow on the bed that looks like a big dead rat. I could not imagine all the DNA left on that thing either. *gags* Bathroom: Nice size but not great. The faucet was lose (really lose) and the toilet would not flush right. Service: Great. Everyone I encountered did a great job making me feel welcome. Good stuff. Food: I had meetings there, so experienced the breakfast and lunch they made. It was really good... much better than most hotels. Bar: Very cool. Good music, great service and good drinks. The scene was decent as well. Small bar, but was not cramped. So, maybe other rooms are nicer... well hell they better be. Regardless, if ONE room is like that (especially a 'suite'), I have to think others are like that as well. It is too bad though. The views are great and they actually have windows that open... big shocker for the city in general!

This was a wonderful stay. The staff was extremely helpful , The rooms are especially large, and the fact they have a small kitchen makes everything a lot more easy. The breakfast and supper were excellent. They go out of their way to make you feel comfortable - for instance, they have take-away plates you can take up to your room. the business center, gym and pool also make this my first choice next time in Chicago.

I had a very pleasant stay at Hotel Palmer and would happily return. My room was comfortable, quiet, and thoughtfully laid out, with a genuinely comfortable bed and enough space to unpack without feeling cramped. The bathroom was spotless and modern, with good water pressure, plenty of towels, and a walk-in shower that stayed hot throughout. Every staff member I met was welcoming and professional, from check-in to the morning coffee service, and they were quick to offer helpful local recommendations without being overbearing. The only disappointment was that my two-night stay felt far too short; I would have liked another day to enjoy the hotel and neighborhood. Considering the location, comfort, and level of service, the price felt fair and well worth it.
Loved our stay at the james! Spotless room with a gorgeous rainfall shower in the bathroom, fresh pastries at breakfast, and the front desk couldn't have been friendlier. Totally worth the price.

I had a very pleasant stay at Swissotel and would happily return. The check-in was quick and friendly, even though I arrived later than planned, and my room was clean, quiet, and nicely laid out. The bed was especially comfortable, and I appreciated the large windows and thoughtful touches like plenty of outlets and good water pressure. Breakfast offered a decent variety, from fresh fruit and pastries to hot dishes, although the restaurant became busy around 9 a.m. The location was convenient for getting around, with shops and public transport within an easy walk. Staff were consistently polite and helpful without being overly formal. My only minor complaint is that the Wi-Fi slowed down in the evening, but overall the hotel felt comfortable, well managed, and worth the price.

We booked two nights at Hotel Palmer expecting a charming getaway, but honestly, one night would have been more than enough. The constant hum from the ventilation system made sleeping a miserable chore, and the thin walls meant I heard every door slam and every conversation in the hallway. It simply wasn't worth the premium rate they charge for a room with a peeling bathroom ceiling and a carpet that felt perpetually damp. We were counting the hours until checkout. Breakfast was a bleak affair too--tepid scrambled eggs, stale pastries, and coffee that tasted burnt. The only high point was the front desk staff's apology, but a kind word doesn't fix a sleepless night or justify the bill. We left exhausted, relieved, and thoroughly underwhelmed.

Booked the Fairmont for a milestone anniversary and left deeply underwhelmed. The bathroom was the first red flag: a grimy shower curtain that stuck to you, a sink faucet that sprayed water everywhere, and a constant, faint musty odor. Our room faced an air conditioning unit and a brick wall, so the 'city view' was a joke. Worse, we heard every door slam in the corridor all night, plus the plumbing gurgling from neighboring suites--zero soundproofing. The staff, while polite, were shockingly indifferent; when I mentioned the noise and the damp towels at the front desk, the response was a shrug and a scripted 'we'll look into it,' which never happened. For the price, I expected far more care. It beats me how this place gets the ratings it does. A disappointing stay that did not match the brand's reputation at all, and I can't recommend it unless you get a lucky room.

I had a very enjoyable stay at the Omni. From check-in onward, the staff were warm, professional, and genuinely helpful without being overbearing; they quickly arranged a late dinner reservation and offered useful local suggestions. My room was comfortable and spotless, with a surprisingly peaceful view of the city skyline and river from the higher floor. The decor felt fresh and polished rather than dated, especially in the lobby and bathroom, though the room still had a pleasantly classic character. The bed was excellent, and everything I needed was close at hand. My only complaint is that the stay felt far too short--I had just settled in when it was time to leave. I would gladly return for a longer visit and recommend the hotel to both business and leisure travelers.

I only stayed at this hotel for one night, the location was great but the elevators drove me crazy. After the first long wait I started to time how long it took from the moment I pushed the button until the elevator arrived, never under 10 min. even late at night. I went up to the rooftop for and after dinner drink with my husband... 1 margarita was $14! I wans't drinking because I'm pregnant so I had a soda water for $4... if I would have known I would have had tap water. Overall... great rooms, OK staff , horrible elevators, overpriced drinks.

My wife and I just spent 3 nights at The Talbott. The room was spacious, comfortable and well-appointed. The hotel is quiet although there is some construction nearby. Linens and towels first-class. Free Wi-Fi in the room. The location is terrific, just one block to Michigan Avenue. We will stay here on future visits.

We stayed at the Swissotel for a three day weekend, and were disappointed to see the construction when we arrived. Is it just me, or is this information not clearly stated on their website? A giant tarp where a lobby should have been was pretty weird and unwelcoming. The room itself was fine. More bland and generic than the 'European elegance' claimed on their website. The lack of hot water, was definitely not fine though. There were a couple pluses to our stay at Swissotel. The location is good, the bed was comfortable and the room was clean. These few good points certainly did not redeem our experience, and I wouldn't pick this place again, even post-construction.

I just returned from a stay at this fabulous hotel - what a treat! The hotel website offers a great rate, and what I found was affordable luxury. I asked for a high floor & found myself with a fabulous view, in a room where there was an orchid spray in the bathroom, terrycloth robes and slippers, turndown service, Roger Gallet toiletries, a fluffy down conforter, and a wonderful pillowtop bed. The bathroom was so clean that it sparkled. The service was impeccable as well. Even my room service breakfast was way above average with an incredibly generous basket of excellent croissants, brioches, & pain au chocolat. The decor was unique & the location convenient. Check out the stunning flowers throughout the lobby. This is a topnotch hotel.

Honestly, this stay was a letdown for what we paid. The Sheraton charges premium rates but the wifi in our room barely worked, dropping every few minutes and making it impossible to get any work done, which was the whole reason we booked. When I mentioned it at the front desk, the staff member just shrugged and said 'it happens sometimes' without offering any fix or even an apology. Housekeeping skipped our room entirely one afternoon and we had to call twice to get fresh towels. For over $300 a night, I expected far better service and a connection that actually functioned. The room itself was clean enough, though dated and smaller than the photos suggested. By the last day we were genuinely ready to leave, and the four nights felt much longer than they should have. Won't be returning.

Loved my weekend here, honestly too short. The room was spotless and the decor felt fresh and updated, and the breakfast spread with fresh pastries and good coffee got mornings off right. Would happily return for a longer stay.

I had a very pleasant stay at Homewood. The suite was clean, comfortable, and thoughtfully arranged, with a small kitchen that made the longer visit feel much easier. My room faced the quieter side of the property, so I rarely heard anything beyond an occasional hallway door, and I slept well each night. The view was not dramatic, but the windows looked out over a tidy courtyard with trees and plenty of daylight, which was a nice change from facing a parking lot. The location was especially convenient, with restaurants, shops, and major roads only a short drive away. Every staff member I met was warm, professional, and quick to help, from check-in to answering questions about the area. I would gladly stay here again.

Hotel Amalfi was a letdown despite its convenient central location, just a short walk from the station and several restaurants. The room felt tired, and the view was especially disappointing: our window faced a narrow inner courtyard with bins and noisy air-conditioning units. The bathroom was cramped, with stained grout around the shower, weak water pressure, and barely any space to put toiletries. Breakfast was included but uninspiring--lukewarm coffee, dry pastries, and limited fruit that was not replenished promptly. Staff were polite enough, but the overall condition of the hotel did not justify the rate. I expected more comfort and care for the price.

I stayed at the Fairmont Chicago for one night - I'm a frequent business traveler and am very familiar with travel rituals. I checked in late (almost 10pm) due to flight cancellations from my home airport -- Atlanta. I took the shuttle to the airport (best option in lieu of the over priced taxis), and it was my first time staying at the hotel. Upon arrival, I immediately noticed the entrance, which appeared very welcoming and warm to me. I checked in with no problems -- and the desk person even asked if I'd prefer a king or double (reconfirming my reservation preference). I always take the king when I can, and the bed was fantastic! It was suited with great linen and these incredible down & feather pillows named Encompass made by The Pillow Factory -- I checked the tags, since I plan to buy some! I ate dinner at the hotel restaurant - Aria, which they mention they like to be considered separate from the hotel -- and YES, it does stand out all on it's own. The food is Asian fusion, and truly wonderful -- as a gourmand and life-long foodie, I appreciate great food when I taste it! The hotel service was good as well. Only drawback was the breakfast buffet at the restaurant -- seems they need to stick with their dinner theme solely. They missed the mark on relatively simply things like scrambled eggs on the buffet, which tasted a bit 'metallic'. But they made up for it by getting a special order made immediately after I passed on the buffet. I would highly recommend this hotel -- it has atmosphere and a great view (if you can get a room with one), fabulous dinner -- just pass on the breakfast buffet.

Honestly, I wasn't sure what to expect with the Affinia, but it ended up being the perfect home base for our long weekend. The location is fantastic--we walked to the park, grabbed late-night bites, and never touched the subway once. What really stood out was the front desk crew; they remembered our names by day two and went out of their way to swap our room when street noise got annoying. The room itself was cozy but cleverly laid out, with a comfortable bed and a small kitchenette that saved us a fortune on breakfast. Bathroom was spotless, water pressure was great. I've paid double for hotels with half the charm. A few dated spots here and there, but the vibe was so welcoming that I honestly didn't care. Would absolutely book again.

I can see how this place must have been gorgeous at one time but they really need a makeover. 1. There was a huge gaping hole in the carpet on the bedroom floor. I kid you not. How can they have guests in a room where the carpet looks like it had been mauled by a giant earthworm? 2. The furniture was severely chipped. Ok. I dont mind chipped furniture if I am slumming it in my just-out-of-college-sister's apartment. But for 170+ a night, I want a room that does not look like it was furnished with stuff retrieved from a dumpster drive 3. The receptionist while I was checking in was super curt. I know it was late but isnt that sort of your job? Not everything was horribly bad though. The one star is for the bathroom that was super clean. I do not recommend this place at all.

I had a very pleasant stay at the Sofitel. The lobby felt polished without being overly formal, and the front desk team handled check-in quickly while still taking time to answer my questions about the area. My room was quiet, comfortable, and thoughtfully laid out, with a genuinely comfortable bed, good lighting, and plenty of space for luggage. I especially appreciated the large windows and the spotless bathroom, which had strong water pressure and nice toiletries. Breakfast was fresh and well presented, although the coffee service was a little slow during the busiest period. The hotel's location made it easy to walk to restaurants, shops, and public transport. Overall, it offered the kind of dependable service and calm atmosphere that made returning after a long day especially enjoyable.
Beautiful lobby, but our room felt worn and oddly cramped for the price. The elevator wait was ridiculous, and housekeeping never came despite two calls to the front desk.

Loved the quirky decor and the free evening wine hour by the fireplace. Staff remembered my name and my coffee order, and the bed was unbelievably comfortable. Perfect downtown location, would absolutely return.

My wife and I just spent a long weekend at the Hardrock Chicago hotel, and although I am not one to normally write long email, I felt it necessary to bring some of the disappointing experiences from our recent syat (2/14 to 2/17) to your attention.Issues included: Our friends ordered chocolate covered strawberries to be delivered to our room upon arriving on 2/14 and we never got them. Our friends later (on 2/16) asked us if we had received the strawberries, and we responded no. They then brought this to the attention of the hotel and we were pleasantly surprised to have received a complimentary bottle of champagne. We were then disappointed again, upon checking out, however, when we were accidentally billed for the 'complimentary' champagne - which was later subtracted from our bill. The in-room DVD player didn't work. It was approximately 11 PM on 2/15 when we called the front desk for help with trouble-shooting the issue. The person responded friendly that 'Al, the engineer, will be calling you back shortly' to help. 10 minutes later there was a knock on the door, and it was Al. A great and friendly guy, but we were waiting for a call back, not the arrival of a service tech - keep in mind it was late and we were already in bed. When Al was not able to fix the DVD player, he graciously told us 'order a movie on us' - thru the in-house movie selection. The problem: that didn't work either. Again, Al was awesome, and called the service provider, but they weren't able to fix it until after midnight. Finally, after midnight Al called us back, but by then the 'movie watching' mood had sort of passed. I ended up watching the film 'Hitman' alone as my wife had already gone to sleep.The thermostat in our room didn't work, regardless of the temperature we set it to (set to 65 degrees - actual temperature = 76 degrees). We had so many other unresolved issues that we didn't feel it necessary to voice any more. ...read more

Homewood was a comfortable, welcoming stay with a spotless room and genuinely helpful staff. I especially appreciated the quiet atmosphere and convenient location, which made everything feel easy from check-in to checkout.

Breakfast was a cringe-worthy affair: lukewarm scrambled eggs that tasted of nothing, stale pastries, and coffee that was closer to dishwater. The wifi flickered in and out so unpredictably that I gave up trying to stream anything and just stared at my phone's 'no connection' icon. Oddly, our three-night stay felt both interminable and rushed -- endless hours of nothing to do in the room, yet checkout arrived before we'd ever relaxed. The noise was the real killer: walls thin enough to hear the neighbor's TV and a hallway that echoed with slammed doors until 2 a.m. For Hilton's reputation, this was a profound letdown. I left more exhausted than when I arrived, and I won't be back.

We stayed at the Hilton for four nights over a long weekend and honestly it exceeded what I expected. Our room on the 14th floor was spotless when we arrived, and housekeeping kept it that way every day without us ever having to ask twice. The bed was one of the most comfortable I've slept in at a hotel, big and soft with plenty of pillows, which is rare. Location-wise you can't beat it, we walked everywhere we wanted to go. The breakfast buffet was pricey but worth it once, and the executive lounge snacks saved us a few times. One small hiccup with the TV remote was fixed within ten minutes of calling the front desk. Check-in was quick and friendly, and the bell staff handled our luggage cheerfully. Would absolutely book again for our next trip.

We stayed four nights at this Hilton and honestly couldn't wait to leave. The photos online showed a beautiful city view, but our window faced directly at the neighbouring office building, so we kept the curtains drawn most of the time. The room itself showed its age: stains on the carpet, dust on the bedside lamps, and hair in the bathroom that clearly hadn't been cleaned before our arrival. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely. The staff were polite enough at check-in, but every request afterwards felt like an inconvenience; it took three calls and nearly two hours to get extra towels. Even the breakfast staff barely acknowledged us. Four nights felt far too long in a place like this, and at these prices we expected much better. We won't be returning.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly, it exceeded expectations. The lobby has a sleek, modern vibe that sets a nice tone. My room was spotless, with a super comfy bed and blackout curtains that actually worked--slept like a log. The location on East 39th is a huge win, super close to Grand Central and a quick stroll to Koreatown for late-night bites. Staff were friendly without being overbearing, and the check-in process was a breeze. Only tiny gripe: the bathroom could use a bit more counter space, but that's minor. The rooftop bar is a hidden gem with great city views. Would definitely book here again for the price point and convenience. Solid pick for a city trip.
Slept like a log in the blissfully quiet room, and the wifi never dropped once during my work calls. Waking up to that skyline view over the river made the whole stay feel worth it.

I left Hotel James feeling more relieved than rested. The room's decor looked tired, with scuffed furniture, faded carpet, and lighting that made everything seem dingy rather than cozy. The bathroom was especially disappointing: cramped, poorly ventilated, and marked by mildew around the shower seal; the water pressure also dropped to a trickle in the morning. Our two-night stay somehow felt much too long because the noise from the hallway carried straight through the door. Staff at check-in were curt and offered no useful information, and when I mentioned the bathroom issue, they said someone would look into it but nobody came. For the price, this was far below expectations.

Stayed here for a long weekend and honestly couldn't have picked a better base. The room was spacious, spotless, and the bed was like sleeping on a cloud--I actually wanted to check out late just to enjoy it more. The staff made the difference though; from the doorman who remembered my name to the front desk helping me sort out a lost charger without any fuss, everyone seemed genuinely happy to help. The location is brilliant for sightseeing, but the real highlight was the breakfast spread--fresh pastries, made-to-order eggs, and the best coffee I had all trip. My only tiny gripe is the gym could use a few more free weights, but that's nitpicking. Would absolutely book again next time I'm in town.

I had a very pleasant stay at Affinia and would happily return. The location was especially convenient, with restaurants, shops, and public transportation all within an easy walk, yet my room was surprisingly quiet at night. The suite was spacious by city standards, with a comfortable bed, a small sitting area, and plenty of storage for a longer visit. Everything was clean and in good condition, although the bathroom could use a little updating. The front desk staff were welcoming and quick to help when I needed directions and a late checkout. I also appreciated the relaxed atmosphere; it felt more personal than a typical large hotel. Wi-Fi worked reliably, and housekeeping did a thorough job each day. Overall, it was a comfortable, well-located, and good-value stay.

we stayed here in january when it was -20. but even then we enjoyed it so much we could not wait to get back. chicago is a great town to visit and the homewood suites is the place to stay, period. now we stayed from the 9/5/2009 to 9/5/2009 and enjoyed every day. (p.s. the weather was in the high 70s). to get back to the hotel, it was fantastic, it has everything you need and its write in the heart of the city. two seperate rooms were very handy as we had our teenage son. full kitchen, (laundry on 7th floor) seveal foodmarkets within walking distance, everything within walking distance. you wont need a car and at $42 for valet parking you wont want one. dont take my word for it , check it out you wont be disappointed. oh and did i mention free breakfast and dinner . job done. its a no brainer book now. p.s. theres also a beach within walking distance

The room was shabby and smelled like stale smoke, plus the AC sounded like a lawnmower all night. Staff were indifferent, and the 'rock star' vibe felt more like a cheap motel. Total letdown for the price.
The Affinia's convenient location was the highlight, but the dated decor and only moderately clean room made the high price feel unjustified. I expected much better.

Hotel Monaco looked charming online, but the stay was far more frustrating than expected for the price. Our room faced an alley and the noise from delivery trucks started before 6 a.m.; the windows did very little to block it out. The air conditioner rattled all night, and the room felt stuffy even after we adjusted it. There were stains on the carpet near the bed and the bathroom had only one nearly empty bottle of soap. I mentioned both the noise and missing amenities at the desk, but was told maintenance was 'busy' and nobody followed up. The location is convenient, and the lobby is attractive, but that did not make up for poor sleep and indifferent service. I would choose somewhere else next time.

I had high hopes for this Sofitel given the price, but our stay was sadly underwhelming. The bathroom was the biggest letdown -- the shower drained so slowly that water pooled around our feet, and there was visible mold along the grout near the tub. Housekeeping came late most days, too. On the plus side, the location is genuinely convenient, just a short walk from the metro and plenty of restaurants, so getting around was easy. Our room faced a narrow back alley, so instead of city views we stared at air conditioners and brick walls the whole week. Breakfast repeated the pattern of disappointment: cold eggs, watery coffee, and a buffet that never got restocked on time despite the hefty price. For a property with this reputation, I expected far more attention to detail. Won't be returning.

We went with the great reviews on Tripadvisor. The location, rooms, amenities and price via Expedia were good. My complaint is the poor service at every stage - the check-in was slow (even at 1am), the concierge (Sarita) was hopeless, staff were generally rude. Also there was some sort of generator box under the bed which hummed all night - we turned it off and it also seemed to turn off the air conditioning. Finally, just to let you know that there is a major construction site in front of the hotel and roadworks at 2am with trucks that beep continuously everytime they reverse!!! Would I stay here again? - maybe if I got a good deal and had a back room but there are plenty of other great hotels nearby.
Our room overlooked the city skyline, and the fresh, understated decor felt inviting. Everyone at the Omni was warm and efficient, and the central location made walking to restaurants and shops easy.
Overpriced for the experience: the bathroom was cramped and dated, hallway noise kept me awake, and while the central location was convenient, it didn't make up for the poor value.

Just back from 5 night stay at Omni and would thoroughly recommend it. Staff bent over backwards to assist in anything, no matter how minute. Great location on magnificent mile and lots to do there both for adults and my 10yo daughter. If i had to find a fault it would be the extra charges, taxes etc for room service, bar and restaurant, but where is cheap these days? Would definitely recommend it, especially for families.
Homewood looked tired, the hallway smelled stale, and our room's air conditioner rattled all night. Breakfast was picked over by 8, and the front desk barely acknowledged the complaint.

I had a very pleasant stay at the Fairmont and would happily return. From check-in onward, the staff were warm, professional, and genuinely helpful without being overbearing. My room was spacious, quiet, and spotless, with a comfortable bed and a great city view. I especially appreciated the small details, such as the excellent water pressure, quality toiletries, and plenty of outlets near the desk. Breakfast was varied and fresh, though the restaurant became busy later in the morning. The lobby had an elegant atmosphere, and it was nice to have a quiet place to sit between meetings. The location also made getting around easy, with several restaurants and attractions within walking distance. Service at checkout was equally smooth. It is not the least expensive option, but the comfort and attentive service made it feel worthwhile.

I really wanted to like Hotel Allegro, and the location near the theaters is genuinely convenient, but that's about where the positives end for me. Check-in took forever because there was only one person at the front desk, and while she was polite, she seemed completely overwhelmed. The room itself was tired--worn carpet, a bed that dipped in the middle, and a bathroom that had clearly seen better decades. Housekeeping didn't come until almost 5 PM, and when I asked for extra towels, it felt like I was putting someone out. The noise from the hallway was constant; I could hear every door slam and conversation. I get that it's an older building, but for the price, I expected better upkeep, maybe some attention to detail. It's a forgettable stay, and I won't be rushing back.

I'm genuinely impressed with how comfortable our stay was at Homewood. The room was spotless and the bed was honestly one of the best I've slept in at a hotel in a long time--firm but not hard, great pillows. The kitchenette came in handy for late-night snacks, and the mini-fridge kept our drinks properly cold. Breakfast had a solid rotation: made-to-order omelets one morning and decent waffles the next. The staff at the front desk were friendly without being overbearing, and they even gave us a great recommendation for a local taco spot that was packed with residents. The only minor hiccup was the elevator being slow at peak checkout time, but it didn't ruin anything. We'll definitely book here again when we're in the area.

The view of the harbor was stunning, but the dated carpet and peeling wallpaper in our room felt like a time warp. Our two-night anniversary stay dragged on, as constant hallway noise and street chatter made any quiet escape impossible.

I expected more from a Hyatt, especially for the rate we paid. The location was convenient for meetings downtown and close to restaurants, but that was the main positive. Our room faced the street, and traffic, sirens, and late-night voices made it hard to sleep even with the windows shut. Breakfast was disappointing: lukewarm eggs, sparse fruit, and a crowded buffet that was not replenished quickly. Coffee was weak, too. The room itself looked worn, with a stained chair and slow-draining shower. Staff were polite but seemed overwhelmed when we mentioned the noise. Overall, it did not feel worth the price.

I really expected more from a Hilton, honestly. The lobby looks impressive when you walk in, but that's where the good impression ends. Check-in took almost forty minutes because their system was down and nobody seemed to know how to handle it manually. My room wasn't ready until nearly 4pm despite a confirmed early check-in request. The room itself felt tired -- stained carpet, a bathroom door that wouldn't stay closed, and the AC rattled all night so I barely slept. Housekeeping skipped my floor entirely one day and when I called down, no one came. Breakfast was the biggest letdown: lukewarm eggs, ran out of coffee twice, and a fifteen-minute wait for a table even though half the restaurant was empty. Staff tried to be polite but everything felt disorganized and understaffed. For the price, I'd book elsewhere next time.

I expected more from a Hyatt, honestly. The room itself was okay at first glance, but the bathroom was grimy around the tub edges, the showerhead sputtered inconsistently, and there was a persistent damp smell no amount of venting seemed to fix. Sleep quality was poor both nights -- thin walls meant hallway conversations and door slams came through clearly, and the AC unit rattled loudly every time it kicked on. To be fair, the location is genuinely convenient: right by the metro stop, plenty of restaurants within a five-minute walk, and easy airport access. But convenience alone doesn't justify the price. At nearly $300 a night, dealing with a musty bathroom and two rough nights of sleep felt like a bad deal. I won't be rushing back.

Disappointing stay at the Knickerbocker. Traffic noise kept me up all night despite requesting a quiet room, staff seemed indifferent at check-in, and while Times Square location is convenient, I won't be returning.

Stayed at the Monaco for a romantic weekend getaway and it was simply fantastic. Very convenient for walking to museums, shopping and park nearby. The room has a great box window that you can sit in and enjoy the view. We also requested a goldfish which was a pleasant surprise and added to the charm and uniqueness of the hotel. Helpful staff, wifi, Aveda products, decent restaurant downstairs for brunch, easy to get a taxi and nothing beats the location. I would definitely recommend staying at this hotel, for business or pleasure.

If you want to stay in a fabulous hotel in the city and you're willing to pay a little extra, I'd recommend this place.Also, pay the extra for a corner room - the views of the city are spectacular.A short walk to Michigan Avenue. Excellent service from the valets, concierge, lobby agents, and waitstaff in the restaurants. The food in the restaurants was great and room service wasn't too shabby either.Well worth the money!

We booked the Hilton specifically for a weekend getaway, expecting the usual standard of comfort. The location is undeniably convenient, but that's about the only positive I can muster. Our room smelled strongly of stale smoke, despite being a non-smoking floor, and the air conditioning unit sounded like a lawnmower all night. We asked for a fan, but were told they were all in use. The bathroom had a broken toilet seat and a hairline crack in the sink that just felt unhygienic. Breakfast was a chaotic free-for-all, with empty chafing dishes and lukewarm coffee. For the price we paid, this felt more like a budget motel experience. I genuinely expected better housekeeping and a front desk that was more than just apologetic. I left more tired than when I arrived. Won't be returning.

where do I start. The GM was a nice guy for handling the incident I had. Anthony -the Concierge - set me up with a massage when the reservation at the spa i requested was unavailable. Anthony said he knew this spa and it was nice. He set me up and quoted me a price of $125, When i got to the spa (which was actually a seedy nail and hair salon) i saw on the front window that a massage for an hour was $100 with 20% off. At the end of the massage I gave the lady $100 and said thanks you can keep the change, She insisted that I got 'A Hotel Rate' because Anthony set me up. She called Anthony and confirmed the rate then told me she had to go and pay Anthony the difference - $45. She then offered me a ride to the hotel since she was going there which I declined. In short - shady dealings with this place. I was quite taken back. The GM Selman comp'd me a night but , I felt swindled big time. Stay somewhere else. The concierge has something going on...

I had a very comfortable stay at Homewood. The suite was clean, quiet, and genuinely useful for a longer visit, with a small kitchen, full-size refrigerator, and enough seating to spread out instead of living from a suitcase. The bed was comfortable, and housekeeping kept everything in good shape without being intrusive. I appreciated the complimentary breakfast, especially on busy mornings, and the evening social was a nice bonus after a long day. Staff at the front desk were friendly and quick to help when I needed a late checkout and directions to a nearby restaurant. The fitness room was modest but perfectly adequate. A few fixtures looked slightly dated, but nothing affected my stay. Overall, it felt more relaxed and spacious than a typical hotel, and I would gladly return.

We booked at another hotel a block away and spent a unhappy night. We walked over to the Talbott and the courtiest staff showed us a room and we booked the rest of our stay. The room was very attractive and well furnished with double sinks in the bathroom. The tub is large and the shower a pleasure. The location was quiet as requested. The staff was always cheerful and very helpful. Tim and Stephanie provide excellent concierge services! The breakfast at the Basil Cafe is a great way to start the day. We travel a lot and appreciate the ambiance of a good hotel. I would highly recommend the Talbott for your stay.
Despite the convenient location, traffic noise kept me awake, the Wi‐Fi barely worked, and our two-night stay felt far too long for such an underwhelming Sheraton experience.

We booked through a travel website. This hotel is currently undergoing major renovation and will be renamed in September. The public areas are still being renovated but the hallways and rooms are done. The hallway was so dimly lit, we couldn't see how to use the key card. The shock came when we entered the room. Whoever designed it obviously did not take function or a guest's comfort into consideration. The bed was a mere 15 inches off the ground - a mattress (rock hard) over a platform. The 'nigh stands' were shelves attached to the wall at around 12 inches height. The room was stark - all off-white, no color. No art work or any decoration at all. The full-length drapes completely blocked the air conditioning unit; if it were winter and the heat was on, I think this could be dangerous. There was a desk & chair but no clock/radio in the room; there was a wall mounted LCD tv with very poor channel selection. The bathroom was very small but clean. The problem with it was that the tub was almost 2 ft high and difficult to step in to. An older person could have never stayed in the room. Because of the renovation, there was no restaurant on-site. No vending or ice available on the floor either I can't see anyone ever becoming a repeat guest at this hotel. I would never stay there again.

We stayed at Homewood for four nights and were genuinely pleased with the whole experience. The location couldn't have been more convenient -- a short walk to the train station, restaurants, and the main shopping street, which made getting around effortless. The wifi worked reliably throughout our stay, strong enough in the room for video calls and streaming without a single dropout, which is rare in my experience. The staff were warm and helpful without being overbearing; when we asked for a late checkout on our last day, they arranged it with no fuss and even printed our boarding passes. Considering the nightly rate included a solid breakfast with fresh options and free parking, it absolutely felt worth the price. Would happily return and recommend it to friends visiting the area.

The wallpaper in the bathroom was peeling, and the plumbing groaned all night, making rest nearly impossible. Breakfast was a lukewarm buffet of stale pastries, and street noise bled through the thin windows without mercy.

I booked the Swissotel expecting the dependable quality that comes with the brand name, but my stay left me genuinely underwhelmed. Our room faced the internal courtyard, and while that meant it was mercifully quiet, the view was essentially a grey wall and the top of the mechanical plant room. The bathroom felt like an afterthought from the early nineties, with a clunky, cracked tiled surround and a shower head that sprayed in every direction except on me. The carpet in the hallway had visible stains, and the room itself, despite the recent refurbishment claims, still had dated, beige furniture that creaked ominously. Honestly, for the nightly rate, I expected far more polish. You're paying for the location and the name, but the experience itself felt tired. I would think twice before booking here again, especially since there are fresher, better-value options a few blocks away. It wasn't a disaster, but it was a disappointment.

If you are looking for a hotel that is truly in the best location, the Intercontinental is it--right on the Magnificent Mile, next to the Chicago River, across from the Wrigley Building. My daughter and I stayed here for a getaway, and quickly were able to get to Milennium Park, shopping, Navy Pier, great dining, exploring festivals and strolling through beautiful areas along the lakefront and Chicago River. Check-in was easy and we were treated with courtesy throughout our stay. Maria, one of the concierges, was especially helpful in finding us a unique place to eat. The room was lovely and comfortable, although our tub didn't drain well. Just a wonderful stay!
Hard Rock was a fun surprise--our room was spotless, the beds were seriously comfortable, and the pool staff kept the vibe relaxed. Great location too; we walked everywhere.
Staff were indifferent, the decor looked tired, and breakfast was a disappointing spread of lukewarm items. The cramped bathroom had worn fixtures and poor water pressure.

Just spent three nights at the Amalfi Hotel, while in Chicago on business. Booked a king-corner room and loved it. Largest room I've ever had in a hotel in Chicago, incredibly comfortable, very clean. The breakfast and evening cocktails were a nice bonus too. And the location couldn't be beat. Walking distance to the the River, the Loop, Michigan Ave shopping and convenient to public transportation. I noticed a number of reviews commented on the noise; yes there is some street noise, and the building across the street is under construction (the noise from that was usually between 730-4, if you want to sleep late during the week ask for a room on the back side) but really, in downtown Chicago it's not going to be silent, if you want silence stay in the suburbs. If you want a great hotel (at a great price) right in the thick of everything, stay at the Amalfi.

I had a very pleasant two-night stay at the Omni during a quick Chicago visit. My room faced Michigan Avenue, and the city view was especially nice at dusk when the buildings and traffic lights came on. Despite being so close to the activity outside, the room stayed surprisingly quiet; I only noticed street noise when I opened the curtains and listened for it. The bed was comfortable with crisp sheets and supportive pillows, and I slept through both nights without waking up. The bathroom was roomy, spotless, and had a strong shower with plenty of hot water, plus enough counter space for my toiletries. Staff at the desk were friendly and efficient, and the location made walking to restaurants and shops very easy.

The hotel is staffed by very nice but many inexperienced people. Executive lounge has limited hours and no access outside of those hours. Other areas similarly lack the level of service that is expected for this type of hotel. One of the individuals at the concierge desk twice gave us bad information about public transportation and the hours at one place. While the location is good, this particular hotel is simply not a good representation of what Swissotel is supposed to be, and there are far better choices in Chicago. It would not be my choice for a return stay.

Really enjoyed my stay at the Hilton. Check-in was quick even though I arrived late, and the front desk agent was friendly and gave me clear directions to the elevators and breakfast area. My room was spotless, with a comfortable bed, good blackout curtains, and enough outlets near the desk to work without hunting around. The bathroom had strong water pressure and plenty of towels. I also appreciated how quiet the floor was overnight; I slept better than I expected in a busy hotel. Breakfast had fresh fruit, eggs, pastries, and decent coffee, so it was easy to get moving in the morning. The lobby felt welcoming and well maintained. Parking was a little pricey, but overall the service and comfort made it worthwhile.
Loved our stay here--the sea view room was worth every euro and the breakfast spread was impressive. Staff went out of their way to help with ferry schedules. Would happily return next summer.
The hype is all wrong for this place. Room was tiny, walls paper-thin, and the 'vibe' couldn't mask the stale smell and rude front desk. Paid a fortune for a headache. Never again.
Stayed two nights at the InterContinental and was impressed by how smoothly everything ran; the room was quiet, breakfast had plenty of options, and the concierge gave us excellent dinner advice.

I really wanted to like this place, but the Affinia let me down at nearly every turn. Check-in took over twenty minutes while the front desk clerk fumbled with the computer, and nobody offered an apology. My room looked tired, with a stained armchair and an AC unit that rattled all night no matter what I did. The 'suite' bathroom had a slow drain that left the sink filling up every morning. Housekeeping skipped my room entirely one day and left only two towels the next.(Location is fine, I'll give them that, but at these prices I expected far more.) When I mentioned the noise at checkout, the response was a shrug. Skip this one and book elsewhere.

I stayed at the James in June, and I must say, it felt like I was in some ultra-swanky boutqiue hotel. From the uniforms of the staff.. which consists of a small J pin that they wear with nice suits and such, to the wonderful, comfortable beds, the James just makes you feel ultra-relaxed. The gym in the hotel was fantastic for a hotel gym, and the machines were all new and in fantastic condition. I really enjoyed the complimentary Kiehl's products as well as the soft, cushy beds with futons. Location-wise, it's just off Michigan ave, and it's close to all the shops and restaurants. I'd definitely stay here if I'm' ever back in Chicago.

I checked into this hotel, Rm 1760 on 11/13/2010. Next day, I woke up with bed bug bites, numerous, on my arm and back. We reported this to the management who assiged us to rm 1901 and promised to get the room inspected and 'taken care of'. I insisted that they get all my clothes laundered, which they did. Interestingly, no one from the management, other than the security guy who came when we first complained, even offered any apology for the inconvience. I missed couple of meetings that day. The next day, I called as I forgot something in the previous room, only to discover that the room was already assigned to the next guest. So much for reporting!
Street noise and a rattling vent kept me awake most of the night, and our view was just a brick wall. Staff seemed indifferent when we mentioned it.

I was a little wary about booking Homewood given the price, but after three nights, I genuinely feel it was money well spent. The room wasn't just tidy; it was spotless, with fresh-smelling linens and a carpet that showed no signs of wear. The bathroom surprised me--plenty of counter space, a powerful showerhead with great water pressure, and a mirror that didn't fog up immediately, which is a small victory. What really sealed it, though, was the sleep quality. The blackout curtains did their job flawlessly, and the mattress had that perfect firmness that supports you without feeling like a board. I woke up refreshed each morning, which rarely happens in hotels. The check-in was smooth, and the lobby had a nice, quiet vibe. For a comfortable, hassle-free stay that doesn't nickel-and-dime you, this place hits the mark. I'd book again.

Our weekend stay felt far too long; the tired, brown decor screamed 1980s and the peeling wallpaper in the bathroom was off-putting. The room wasn't properly dusted, and for the hefty price, I expected polished upkeep, not a musty carpet that smelled old.

I had a very comfortable stay at the Conrad. The room felt bright and thoughtfully arranged, with a genuinely spotless carpet, crisp bedding, and no dust hiding around the desk or nightstand. The decor is modern without being overly flashy; muted colors, warm wood, and good lighting made it feel fresh rather than cold or dated. I especially appreciated the bathroom, which was spacious and immaculate, with a large walk-in shower, strong water pressure, and plenty of counter space for toiletries. Breakfast was better than expected, offering fresh fruit, pastries, made-to-order eggs, and several healthy choices, with attentive service even during the busy morning rush. Staff were friendly and efficient throughout the visit, and the quiet room made it easy to sleep. I would gladly return.

We stayed at Hotel Palmer for four nights and honestly couldn't have been happier with the choice. The location is perfect--a quiet street but still a five-minute walk to the main square, which meant we got peaceful mornings without being isolated. Our room overlooked a small courtyard, and the soundproofing was excellent; we never heard a peep from the neighbors. The bed was firm but supportive, and the blackout curtains worked wonders after late nights. Breakfast was a highlight: fresh pastries, local cheeses, and made-to-order eggs that weren't swimming in grease. The staff remembered our preferences by the second day, which felt genuinely thoughtful rather than scripted. Only minor hiccup was the shower pressure being a bit weak, but the water stayed hot. We'd absolutely return and would recommend it to anyone wanting a comfortable, unpretentious base.

My stay at the Amalfi was a very brief one. I booked the hotel based on all of the glowing reviews I saw here on Trip Advisor. When I arrived, I sat down at a desk with an amazingly aloof clerk. I felt like I stepped into an episode of the Twilight Zone. The room was very small and dark. Then the Internet wasn't working. I wasn't informed about this on my check in and couldn't be given a time frame when it would be back up. I walked the neighborhood and found another hotel more to my liking, gathered up my belongings and went there. If you're one of those people who likes trendy upscale and chi chi locations and hotels, you'll lurve this place. But if you like a hotel with lights on, working internet and a good view and real breakfast, go someplace else.

Stayed here for three nights and left genuinely impressed. It wasn't cheap, but for the location and quality, I felt it was worth every penny. Our room on the 28th floor offered a stunning panorama of the city skyline, especially at sunset when the windows caught the golden light. The bathroom was a real highlight - spotless, with a powerful rain shower and soft, thick towels that felt luxurious. Despite being in a busy area, the soundproofing was superb; we heard nothing from the street or neighboring rooms, which made for incredibly restful sleep. The bed was firm yet comfortable, and the blackout curtains did their job perfectly. Breakfast was extensive with fresh pastries and made-to-order eggs. Staff were professional and attentive without being intrusive. If you're after a solid, reliable base with great views and silence, this is it. I'd happily return.

I love this hotel. It is one of the best that I have stayed in. The lobby was beautiful and the room was nice and comfortable. The made services was terrific. No matter what time we left the room it was made up when we came back. I asked the maid for a couple of extras and she was very nice and friendly. That is what I liked about the hotel the staff was so nice and friendly. I was there with my daughter for a girl's weekend from Thursday - Sunday. Everyone from the doorman to the concierge to the people at the desk etc. was wonderful. I can't say enough good about this hotel. Yes the bathroom was small, but I wasn't moving into the room. I was just staying there a few days and was hardly in the room anyway. I will definitely stay there again
The Hard Rock looked fun online, but my room was tired, the hallway smelled of smoke, and check-in dragged on forever. Way too expensive for such a disappointing stay.
Well located and well staffed. The Amalfi was a clean and comfortable place to stay. It lacks a restaurant or bar but many are near by. Free continental breakfast and evening cocktail.

We were checked into a room with empty beer bottles,dirty shorts in the closet and an unclean bathroom. There was no manager available for an hour to take any complaints. The front desk lady said the manager was on a LUNCH break at 7 PM!!!!!!! We missed our show at Navy Pier because of the extra time it took in moving into another room etc. Finally when I got to talk to the manager and complained about beer bottles she offered to send me wine and cheese to make up for the inconvenience!!! This was totally inappropiate since I had children including a teenager with me. She gave me a $30 compensation for ruining our family holiday!!!! Staff was somewhat reluctant to take request of extra blankets at night. They kept telling me to look into the closet for extra blankets. I asked for two blanket, but they delivered one. I had to keep calling to get settled for the night. I saw a filled out comment form from the prior guest in our room on the study desk, who had taken the trouble of filling it out, but no one collected it or cared for it. Noisy rooms. Can hear the doors open and close all night. The breakfast items kept running out and had to make calls to get them replenished. I will not recommend this hotel to any one even at discounted rates!!

Hotel Monaco was a really enjoyable base for a weekend in the city. The location made it easy to walk to restaurants, shops, and the river, but the room was quiet enough at night that we slept very well. I liked the playful decor and the little extra touches, especially the comfortable robes and the complimentary coffee in the morning. Our room was not huge, though it had plenty of storage and a surprisingly comfortable sitting area. Everyone at the front desk was friendly without being overbearing, and they gave us a couple of genuinely useful dinner suggestions. The only minor issue was that the bathroom lighting was a bit dim. Otherwise, the hotel felt clean, relaxed, and well run, and I would happily book it again.

We arrived for a weekend stay and really enjoyed the hotel. The cocktail hour was so full of people that we could not get in. The second night we went earlier and it was very nice. The staff was very helpful and had a good knowledge of the area. The rooms were modern and very clean. We will stay there again.

This hotel had a great location, but you can do much better for the money. The hallways smelled of smoke, dirty elevators, furniture in the lobby was thread bare. The staff was very helpful. The room was large, bed comfortable but the room was so musty and old smoke lingered. If you have any allergies don't stay here!

I was really looking forward to a luxurious weekend at the Conrad, but it fell short in every meaningful way. The noise was the first problem--our room faced the street, and sirens and traffic kept me up until 2 a.m. despite the advertised soundproofing. The bathroom looked nice at first, but the shower pressure was dismal, and the glass door leaked water all over the floor. Breakfast was a crowded, chaotic buffet with lukewarm eggs and stale pastries; the omelet station had a 20-minute wait. Worst of all, the Wi-Fi kept dropping every ten minutes, and the front desk suggested I 'move closer to the router.' For nearly $400 a night, I expected calm, comfort, and functioning basics. Instead, I left exhausted and annoyed. I won't be returning.

We booked Homewood for a weekend getaway based on the photos, and honestly, we should have known better. The hallway smelled like old carpet and stale cigarette smoke, which was a bad omen. Our 'king suite' was basically a standard motel room with a fake wall divider. The bed was lumpy, and the pillows were flat as pancakes. We found a hair in the bathroom sink, and the shower pressure was a pathetic drizzle.

To make matters worse, the air conditioner sounded like a lawnmower all night. We called the front desk twice about it, and the second time, they just said 'we'll have someone look at it tomorrow.' There was no offer to move us. The complimentary breakfast was a sad spread of powdered eggs and soggy cereal. For the price we paid, I expected so much more. This place is tired and overpriced. We left a day early and won't be back.

My two nights at the Hyatt felt far too brief, but the spotless room and that gleaming rainfall shower made every minute count. The front-desk team was genuinely warm, and the bathroom's fresh towels were a lovely touch.

Just got back from 2 days up in Chicago shopping with girlfriends. First time I have stayed at the Omni. I did so because I saw a $129.00 rate that included $25.00 of free food on Travelzoo. The three of us (55 year olds) all stayed in one suite with 2 double beds and a VERY comfortable pull out sofa. We had plenty of room. Food in the restaurant was great, service was outstanding from everone we came into contact with, early morning delivery of free coffee, juice and hot chocolate was fabulous and recommendations from the staff on where to eat, time of movies, shopping areas, etc was really helpful. Need I mention the outstanding location? Simply the best! We all decided that the Omni is our new favorite hotel.
For InterContinental prices, I expected better: the room smelled stale, the AC rattled all night, and the front desk brushed off my complaint.
The quirky decor was charming, but the wall-thin noise from the street and hallway made sleep impossible. Service felt indifferent, and the broken AC in our room sealed a disappointing stay.

Stayed here for a conference and left pretty deflated. The room was dated, with a musty smell and paper-thin walls--I heard every door slam. Staff were polite but overwhelmed, and housekeeping skipped our floor until late afternoon. Not worth the star rating.

Absolutely loved my stay at Hotel Monaco! The rooftop pool was a dream, and the staff went above and beyond when I asked for late checkout. Comfy beds, great cocktails, and a perfect location for exploring.

has gone downhill so much we almost checked out. We stayed in the Dean Martin Celebrity Suite for 3 nights while entertaining customers in Chicago. We've stayed there for many years and while not up to date like the Four Seasons or the Peninsula, it has always been a comfortable and clean, service oriented hotel. Not only has room service been eliminated (if you want room service it comes from Marios Italian restaurant down the street, so is ONLY Italian), complimentary morning coffee is no longer available, mini bars have been removed from the rooms, etc. etc. The only restaurant, the Pump Room was closed for a private function on Saturday night, the bar also, so we weren't even able to have an after dinner drink with our guests. Surely the function was planned before we made our reservations, but we weren't told of it. We also learned that the bell staff (who have been there for 13 and 8 years) is being eliminated. So, in other words, anyting to do with 'service' is gone from this hotel. I hear they are going to begin renovations in December, but that is no excuse to let an old glory 'go to pot' in the meantime. We won't be staying here when we go back in July or for Thanksgiving. We even had to pay for internet. Mind you, our bill for 3 nights was 900.00+, no room service, no restaurant/bar charges. Highway robbery for what you get ow at the Ambassador East. Sad.

I really wanted to love the James, given the location and the vibe, but the stay left me feeling drained. Check-in was painfully slow with only one person at the desk, and they seemed annoyed by basic questions about the pool hours and breakfast options. The room itself was advertised with floor-to-ceiling windows, but mine overlooked a dingy airshaft, and the curtain had a large, grimy tear near the bottom. The mattress had a significant dip on one side, so I woke up with a sore back both mornings. Housekeeping never came by unless I called twice, and even then they forgot fresh towels. The hallway smelled like stale cleaning chemicals, and the ice machine on my floor was broken the entire weekend. This place costs a premium, but the service just isn't there. I've had better experiences at mid-range chains. Not worth it.

Stayed here for three nights and left genuinely puzzled by the good ratings. The bed was comfortable, I'll give them that, but the noise was relentless--thin walls meant I heard every door slam and hallway conversation from 6 AM onward. The 'city view' turned out to be a brick wall and a vent. Breakfast was chaotic, with lukewarm scrambled eggs and coffee that tasted burnt, plus staff who seemed annoyed when I asked for more pastries. The air conditioning unit rattled all night and the room never really cooled down. When I reported a leaky bathroom faucet at reception, the woman just shrugged and said maintenance would come 'when possible'--they never did. For the price, I expected way better. The location is convenient, sure, but that's the only real upside. I've had friendlier service at budget chains. Won't be returning.

I had a very pleasant stay at the Hotel Ambassador. The room was spotless when I arrived, with fresh linens, dust-free surfaces, and plenty of space to unpack. The decor is not especially trendy, but it felt well cared for rather than tired; the classic furnishings actually suited the building's character. The bathroom was compact but bright and genuinely clean, with good water pressure and a shower that heated up quickly. My only minor complaint was that the counter space was limited. The bed was comfortable, and despite being in a lively neighborhood, the room stayed quiet enough for me to sleep soundly both nights. Staff were friendly and efficient throughout, and the location made it easy to get around. I would happily stay here again.

Booked a Deluxe room for a three-night city break and left feeling thoroughly underwhelmed. The photos online are far more flattering than reality. Our room was tired, with stained carpet near the window and a bathroom that desperately needed regrouting. We asked for a quiet floor but got one facing the main road, which meant sirens and traffic noise until well past 2 AM. The air conditioning was either freezing or nonexistent, and the thermostat seemed to have a mind of its own. Breakfast was chaotic; the scrambled eggs were watery and the coffee tasted burnt. Staff were polite but overstretched, taking twenty minutes to bring extra towels. On the second night, the minibar wasn't restocked despite asking twice. For the price, this is nowhere near the standard you'd expect. It's acceptable if you're just passing through, but I wouldn't recommend it for a special occasion. Disappointing overall.

We stayed at the Swissotel for four nights and honestly it exceeded what we expected. Check-in was quick and the front desk staff even remembered our names after the first day, which felt like a nice personal touch. Our room on a higher floor had an amazing view of the city skyline and was spotless when we arrived. The bed was genuinely comfortable -- my husband usually complains about hotel pillows but he slept great every night. Breakfast had a huge spread, everything from fresh fruit and pastries to made-to-order eggs, and the coffee was actually good, which is rare. Location was perfect too, walking distance to the main shopping street and a metro station right around the corner. Only tiny gripe was slow elevators at peak times, but that's minor. Would definitely come back.

The Allegro in downtown Chicago is a great stay/ part of the Kimpton Group boutique hotels the Allegro offers a classy stay in a beautiful room for a moterate price/ they offer complimentary and decent wine gratis in the late afternoon and the hotel allows you access to everything the loop has to offer in this remarkable city. i would recommend parking outside of the downtown area and taking the 'EL' into the loop which leaves you about 2 minutes from the hotel/ otherwise you are looking at hefty parking fees for a car you dont need in this part of the city . the rooms are small but beautifully done with great colors,comfortable beds and in my case great views. if you go to kimpton group website and sign up for specials you will be alerted to great rates on certain days / kimpton does a great job and their properties are 'class acts'

Stayed three nights at Hotel Monaco and came away genuinely impressed. The wifi was rock-solid from the moment I connected--I streamed video calls and work files without a single drop, which is rarer than it should be downtown. My room's bathroom had a rainfall shower with strong pressure and plenty of hot water, plus fluffy towels that actually smelled fresh. Street traffic was audible on the lower floor, but the double-paned windows and white-noise machine in the closet kept it easy to sleep by midnight. Location couldn't be beat: four blocks from the train, a two-minute walk to a decent coffee shop, and an easy stroll to the riverfront for evening walks. Staff were friendly during check-in, and the lobby's quirky decor grew on me. Would happily book again.

my husband and l stayed here after a very hectic week in new york. The room was very spacious and clean, the bed was huge and extremely comfortable. I really liked the Aveda bathroom products, great smell. We had room service the first night and it arrived really quick and piping hot. Compliments to the chef. The concierge was very helpful as we needed to find a few places and we were meeting up with friends and did not know how to get to Navy pier, directions were given to us accompanied by a map. The weekend we were there it was their annual air and navy show, this was spectacular. The whole of the last day of the show we spent at Navy pier and the Millenium park. Location of the hotel is very good for most things especially shopping. If we are ever in Chicago again we will definately stay here.

Disappointing stay at Hotel Ambassador: the room was dated, housekeeping missed basic details, and the front desk seemed uninterested when we reported the noisy air conditioner. Definitely not worth the price.

I was really looking forward to this stay, but the Sheraton missed the mark in nearly every way. The lobby looks like it hasn't been updated since the early 2000s, with worn carpet and furniture that's seen better days, and our room felt just as tired. The bed was uncomfortably firm, and the pillows were flat, so I spent most of the night tossing and turning. To make matters worse, the hallway noise was relentless--guests were chatting loudly until 2 a.m., and the thin walls meant I heard every door slam. The staff was polite but completely overwhelmed; the front desk took twenty minutes to check us in, and when I asked for extra towels, they never arrived. By morning, we just wanted to leave. Everything about this felt dated, disorganized, and drained of any charm.

I had a large, roomy, clean 2 bed room with a large bathroom, big minibar snack assortment and was tucked away nicely in the corner so that there was no hall noise. Customer Service here was absolutely incredible, from the doorman to the front desk, to the gentleman who delivered my toothpaste to my room when I requested it. Sure, you get a little outside noise, but it is a big city, that is not unusual! I really enjoyed my stay here and strongly recommend it.
The Hilton was a comfortable stay: the bathroom was spotless, Wi-Fi worked reliably, and the central location made getting around easy. Breakfast offered plenty of fresh, tasty choices.
Great breakfast spread, but the weekend felt way too short. The wifi was flawless for streaming, and the city view from our 15th-floor room was stunning at night.

Booked Swissotel expecting their usual high standards, but this stay fell flat. Breakfast was a chaotic scrum - cold scrambled eggs, dried-out pastries, and coffee that tasted burnt, with staff more interested in clearing plates than refilling the buffet. The wifi was practically useless in my room; I had to sit in the hallway to send a single email, and even then it dropped twice. The bathroom looked modern at first, but the shower pressure was weak and the drain gurgled constantly, leaving a puddle on the floor no matter what I did. As for the view - I paid extra for a city panorama, but got a direct look at a concrete ventilation shaft and a sliver of rooftop, which felt like a cruel joke. For the price, this was a disappointing, forgettable experience that made me question the brand. I won't be back.

Just wanted to let everyone know if you are looking for a hotel with high rise construction next door the Swissotel Chicago is the one for you. My wife and I went there last year and there was just an empty lot next door, this year there is a loud construction site next door. So 8 am Saturday morning you will hear the workers starting. I am sure once the summer in Chicago comes around they will work all night. Just think as they keep adding floors you will be able to look the workers in the eye and wave from your room that used to have a view of the Navy Pier. Now you will get an up close and personal view of people pouring concrete. On top of it the hotel is doing construction of there own. The front of the hotel is block and lucky for us the protestors that are standing in front of the hotel were able to tell use where the new entrance was. The protestors were there because the Swissotel hired a company to redo their sound system that does not hire union workers. If you ask the workers about the noise and they say we can't hear it. I am sure the Swissotel does not want word getting out about this. If you insist on trying it for yourself don't pay for your room in advance they will not let you out of the room and then you are stuck.

In my experience the Ambassador hotel didn't seem to be a 3 1/2 star establishment. The building and lobby were nice but the hotel room was extremely dated. The carpeting was very old and worn. The floor - carpeting and tile both seemed dirty which made me very uncomfortable. I would imagine that many years ago this was a very nice hotel. Currently, it's indespirate need of renovation.
My Hilton room was spotless, with crisp linens that made for a restful night. The decor felt fresh and polished, and the bright, modern bathroom was a real plus.

I booked this hotel for my family of 4 to stay overnight to see the Magnificent Mile Christmas Lights Parade. I chose it because it had a sofa sleeper and one bed. We arrived at our hotel around 3:30 PM to check in. We came at this time because the front desk worker said that we could not check in until 3:00 PM. After giving him our name, the manager said,'OK, we have your king smoking suite available'. We quickly corrected him to let him know that we were traveling with two very young kids and we reserved a non-smoking room. He insisted that his computer said that we reserved a smoking room. We went back and forth, then he asked us if we had a copy of our reservation. Luckily, we were able to pull the reservation up on our phone. It clearly said non-smoking. After showing him our reservation, he explained that there was nothing that he could do to correct the situation because they had no other rooms available.
