So why in the world did he need to see our reservation!! We decided to see if we could handle the smoking room. It turns out that the entire floor was smoking and for a non smoker there was no way that we could sleep in a smoking room on a smoking floor with our two young children. The manager eventually called around and found a hampton inn near by with one bed. We canceled our room reservation. We live about an hour away from downtown so we made the late night trip back home. My family was very disappointed. My husband is a gold member with Hilton. Let's just say we will be switching back to Marriott. The hotel lobby was dated. The smoking room that I saw looked very dated as well. They made an error and never owned up to it, nor did they do anything to compensate us for such a huge inconvenience.
Disappointing stay overall -- room smelled musty, the AC barely worked, and staff seemed annoyed whenever we asked for anything. For the price, I expected much better. Won't be returning.

I had a very pleasant stay at Hotel Amalfi and would happily return. The room was clean, comfortable, and thoughtfully arranged, with a good-sized bed and fresh linens. I slept surprisingly well each night; the mattress was supportive, and the curtains kept the morning light out. Despite being fairly close to the main street, the hotel was quiet after about 10 p.m., with only occasional hallway sounds. The WiFi worked reliably for emails, streaming, and planning day trips, although it was a little slower during breakfast hours. The staff were welcoming and quick to help with restaurant recommendations and directions. My only complaint is that the stay felt too short--I wish I had booked an extra night to enjoy the area and the hotel at a more relaxed pace.
Disappointing stay at Affinia--the room looked worn, housekeeping missed basic details, and hallway noise continued late. For the price, I expected a much cleaner, quieter experience.

I was expecting an experience comparable to my stays at the Olympia in Seattle. The decor and overall feel of the hotel was much above average but not inspiring. Biggest disappointment was the inadequate internet connection in the room. The wireless was very slow and the hard-wire from the wall did not work at all. I did request a replacement of the wall wire, but it did no help. This hotel can do better than this. With a 5 star rating, it should be an experience to be pleasantly remembered -- but, was just a mediocre experience for me. Even the bed covers were not that special. Needs more intense management. Next time, I will try the Trump facility Thanks
The Ambassador made our weekend easy from the start, with a quick check-in, a comfortable room, and staff who were genuinely helpful when we needed dinner suggestions.

It's not a bad hotel. It's just so...disappointing. As a Diamond member, I expect slightly more than a room with two double beds with no view. I'm not distraught over this, but come on. Ditto the continental breakfast in the executive lounge, which has nothing but fattening pastries, bagels and cereal. Low-level Hampton Inns have a free breakfast that puts this to shame. And what's with the lounge not opening until 6:30am? Business travelers often need to be GONE by 6:30, not sitting down to their meager breakfast. The in-room wifi is a pain to access, and I somehow got stuck with the $19.99 plan even though I selected the basic plan. (Don't get me started on how a $89/night Hampton Inn can offer free wifi and a full-service Hilton & Towers seemingly can't...). Finally, what's with the two bathrooms per one hotel room? It's an unseemly waste of space, especially when the rooms are so meager. And the gold-plated bathroom fixtures scream 1992, not 2009, as does the picture-tube TV (vs. flat panel). Overall, this is a huge disappointment over which Conrad should be ashamed.

We stayed at the Hotel James for three nights and honestly can't figure out how it gets such decent ratings. Check-in took forever because apparently only one person works the desk in the evenings, and when we finally got to our room the AC was barely blowing cool air. Asked twice about it before anyone came up. The hallway carpets were stained and the whole place just felt tired. Breakfast was the biggest letdown, lukewarm eggs, ran out of coffee both mornings, and no one refilled anything. Our window overlooked the loading dock, so we were woken at 5:45am bydeliveries every day. Bathroom had a musty smell that never really went away. Staff were polite enough but completely ineffective. For the price, there are far better options nearby. Won't be returning.

Sad to say the InterContinental didn't live up to the photos. My room smelled musty, housekeeping skipped my floor one day, and the front desk took ages to sort a billing error. For the price, very underwhelming.

I wanted to like the Talbott because the location is excellent, but the stay was frustrating from the start. Check-in took nearly 25 minutes even though there was only one person ahead of me, and nobody explained the delay. My room looked worn, with scuffed furniture, a weak shower, and an air conditioner that rattled loudly all night. Housekeeping also missed replacing towels after the first day. The hallway noise carried straight through the door, so sleep was difficult. Staff were polite when I mentioned it, but nothing really changed. For the price, I expected a more comfortable, better-maintained hotel and would probably choose somewhere else next time.
Wifi kept dropping all week, the bathroom had mold in the shower corners, and the room never felt clean. Only plus was the location, right by the metro. Otherwise a big letdown.

We stayed at the Conrad for four nights over a long weekend and honestly I can't think of a single complaint. Our room on a high floor had a genuinely impressive view of the city skyline at night, and the bed was so comfortable I actually looked up where they buy their mattresses (turns out some things you just can't order). Housekeeping was discreet and spot-on every day. The location worked out better than expected since we could walk to a ton of restaurants and it's a short ride to the museums. One small thing that stood out was the front desk calling to check if our room was fine an hour after check-in, which has never happened to me anywhere else. Not the cheapest option in the city, but for an anniversary trip it was absolutely worth it. Would return without hesitation.

We booked the Hyatt mainly for its location, and honestly, it exceeded every expectation we had. The lobby is grand without feeling stuffy, and the front desk agent noticed it was our anniversary and surprised us with a room on a higher floor. That little touch set the tone. Our room was quiet, spotless, and the bed was genuinely comfortable--not too firm, not too soft. I'm picky about pillows, and I slept like a log all three nights.

The breakfast buffet was pricey but worth it for the made-to-order omelets and fresh pastries. We also used the pool one rainy afternoon, and it was surprisingly uncrowded. The only minor downside was the elevator wait during checkout rush, but two of three cars were running and it wasn't a big deal. If you want a smooth, comfortable stay in the heart of the city, this Hyatt is a safe bet. We'd book again without hesitation.

The Talbotts' worn glamour is charming from the lobby, but that charm evaporates by the second night. Our 'deluxe' room had a frayed carpet and a window facing a brick wall, so I slept poorly, disturbed by hallway noise and an AC unit that rattled like a loose muffler. The staff were polite but overwhelmed; housekeeping ignored our door sign twice, and front desk claimed they couldn't fix the thermostat until the next day. At $340 a night, this felt like a $190 experience. We checked out after only one of our two planned nights--not because the stay was too short, but because the mattress sagged and the bathroom smelled faintly of mildew. The location and vintage bar are lovely, but you're paying for history, not comfort. I'd pass on a return.

First let me say, I try not to be too critical, but in some cases the truth is warranted! We checked in and things seemed fine. Location was excellent. Woke up the first morning, to a slightly rumpled bed covered in 'stains', I hope-filthy and not 4 star hotel quality. Requested a linen change and heard a knock on the door- a gentleman was there to let me know if I wanted it done to take off the privacy sign, I did and no one even came until later in the day. The room was big enough, had no drawers, suposedly remodeled but carpet didn't reach the wall, toilet paper holder fell off constantly and shower head was broken. The mirrors were great and the water was always hot! The walls were paper thin, I heard every conversation the guests next door had. They were not noisy but you could hear everything including the t.v. through the walls and vents. Internet was $13.00, worked for a bit and then not again, I called customer service and spent 25 minutes on the phone and they asked if they could work on resetting the system and call back later. The hotel did give us a credit for the charges. At this point, enough was enough, we packed our bags and checked out. The front desk was very helpful- kudos to Rocco for caring and being the only friendly staff we saw other than the bell hops!!

Disappointing stay at the Sheraton. Check-in took forever, my room smelled musty, and the AC barely worked. Staff seemed indifferent when I mentioned it. For the price, I expected much better. Won't be back.

The Conrad exceeded expectations from the moment I walked in. The bathroom was a standout--a massive walk-in rain shower with excellent water pressure, plus thick, plush towels that actually felt spa-quality. As for the decor, it felt refreshingly current, not sterile or tired; the warm wood accents and soft lighting created a genuinely cozy atmosphere. Our room was spotless, with no dust or wear and tear visible anywhere, and the housekeeping team did a meticulous job each day. Breakfast in the restaurant was a lovely surprise: the made-to-order omelets were perfectly fluffy, and the fresh pastries were still warm. Even the coffee was properly strong. Everything felt seamless, calm, and genuinely cared-for. I left feeling rested and impressed, and I'd happily book again without hesitation.

Disappointing stay overall. Room smelled musty, the AC barely cooled, and housekeeping skipped our floor twice. Front desk staff were indifferent when we complained. Location was fine, but I won't be back.

We booked the Omni almost on a whim for a long weekend, and honestly, it turned out to be the best decision of the trip. The location is unbeatable--steps from the Mag Mile but quiet enough that we slept like logs. What really impressed me was the check-in process; the front desk agent remembered my name and even had a list of local coffee spots ready when I mentioned we were jet-lagged. The room itself was huge for downtown, with a couch area that meant we weren't tripping over our suitcases. The pool was warm, the gym had actual squat racks, and the housekeeping staff folded my stray charging cable into a neat coil. Only minor gripe: the elevator wait during checkout rush. But honestly, we're already planning our return in the fall.

I recently stayed at the Fairmont Chicago and found it to be a fantastic hotel. Staff was always courteous and helpful - from the front desk staff at check-in to wait staff in Aria restaurant, to the maid who cleaned my room. The rooms were recently updated, with large flat-screen TV's, beautiful linens, and exceptional toiletries in each room. My room even had a view of Monroe St. harbor. It is truly a first-rate hotel. Location is south of the river and east of Michigan Ave -- as we normally stay north of the river it seems a little out of the way (if that's possible in downtown Chicago), however its location significantly lowers street noise. The hotel has excellent access to Millennium Park, the Aon center (there is a connecting concourse), and is about 4 blocks from shopping on North Michigan Ave. I ate dinner in Aria and it was fantastic! Room service for breakfast was quite good as well. Overall, I'd stay again in a minute if I had business in the loop, or leisure plans in Millennium or Grant Parks.

We stayed at the Omni for a long weekend and honestly expected more for the price. The WiFi was practically unusable, dropping every few minutes, which made it impossible to get any work done. Our room overlooked the parking garage and a stretch of rooftops with AC units humming away, so there was nothing pleasant to look at. Sleep was a struggle too: the walls are thin, we heard hallway conversations and elevator dings well past midnight, and the mattress sagged in the middle. The staff didn't help matters. Front desk agents seemed annoyed whenever we asked for anything, and a request for extra towels took nearly four hours to arrive. Housekeeping skipped our room one day entirely. Convenient location, but between the noise, the weak connection, and the indifferent service, we won't be returning.

Despite the bustling town below, our room was wonderfully quiet. The balcony view over the bay was breathtaking at sunset, and the spotless bathroom felt luxurious. Given the prime location, it was worth every penny for such a serene escape.

Elegant lobby, comfy beds, nice sheets but, we were given a (not fancy, a little dated) room on the 5th floor which had a view of the monstrous venting structure, and was located off the lobby so we heard the elevator all night. At the Hilton, one is charged for Internet access on each device per hour. (We stayed in the middle of Ohio and received total access for free.) We didn't drink the $6.00 water or try the $28. Breakfast buffet. The staff was friendly, but of course you tip for a smile. They did give us a cot for free as we had asked for a room with a fold-out couch as we were a party of 5. Didn't use the gym or pool on the 8th floor, but looked nice (small pool.) No view of the water possible, though we were right at Grant Park. We tried to view the fireworks from a higher story, no such luck. ...read more

The view from my room on the fifteenth floor was the standout--a sweeping panorama of the skyline that made me linger at the window every evening. The bathroom, while compact, felt wonderfully modern with a rainfall shower head and thick, plush towels that were replenished without me even asking. Staff were consistently warm and efficient, from the valet who remembered my name to the front desk who helped me rebook a dinner reservation when my schedule shifted. The decor, thankfully, doesn't lean into that tired beige-and-maroon look; instead, it's sleek with dark wood accents and tasteful, contemporary art that feels intentional rather than generic. Everything functioned flawlessly, and the bed was genuinely comfortable. A few minor scuffs on the hallway baseboards are the only hint of wear. Overall, a polished, dependable stay that exceeded my expectations--I'd happily return.

I expected much more from the Fairmont, especially at this price. My room faced the street, and traffic, late-night voices, and delivery trucks made it far noisier than it should have been. The air conditioner also clicked on and off, so I barely slept and woke up tired both mornings. Wi-Fi was another frustration: it repeatedly dropped during a video call and was too slow to reliably load emails. The room itself looked tired, with scuffed furniture and a bathroom that needed better cleaning around the sink. Even though the stay was only two nights, it felt much longer because every small issue added up. Staff were polite, but no one offered a meaningful solution.

I had a very pleasant stay at the Sheraton and would happily return. Check-in was quick and friendly, even though I arrived later than expected, and my room was spacious, quiet, and exceptionally clean. The bed was comfortable, with good-quality linens, and I appreciated having plenty of outlets near the desk. The lobby feels modern without being overly formal, and the staff were consistently polite whenever I needed directions or extra towels. I also enjoyed breakfast; there was a good variety of fresh fruit, pastries, eggs, and coffee, and the dining area never felt chaotic. The fitness center was well maintained, although it got a little busy in the evening. Wi-Fi worked reliably throughout my stay. Overall, the Sheraton delivered a comfortable, dependable experience with a few thoughtful touches that made it feel easy and relaxing.

The Swisshotel is awesome. Very high class. It is expensive , but so is every hotel in Chicago. It is off from the dingy areas of our city , yet a long walk to Navy Pier, so you will need to pay for the cab. Note to all the Magnificent Mile is boring as can be. I live in Chicago and the hotel is a better experience than the Mile of Navy (BORING) Pier.

Stayed three nights for a business trip and honestly couldn't have picked a better spot. The location is unreal--steps from the riverfront and a quick walk to all the good restaurants, yet the room was eerily quiet. I slept like a rock through two busy weekdays, which never happens in downtown hotels. My corner room faced the water, and watching the barges glide by at sunset was a peaceful bonus I didn't expect. The staff genuinely stood out--front desk remembered my name on day two and the bartender mixed a perfect old fashioned without me even asking. Check-in was swift, and housekeeping was thorough without being intrusive. Only minor gripe: the hallway carpets felt a bit dated. But the vibe, the calm, and the friendly service make me want to come back for a leisure stay.

The rooms felt refreshingly modern--not a hint of dated decor--and the wifi held steady for both work and streaming. I slept deeply on the plush bedding, and given the location and service, the rate felt entirely justified. Would gladly return.

I booked the Fairmont for a milestone anniversary, expecting the usual grandeur. Instead, we got a room overlooking the HVAC units and a constant, low hum that never stopped. The 'classic' decor felt tired, with scuffed baseboards and a bathroom grout that was frankly gross. Service was glacial--we waited forty minutes for ice, and the concierge seemed annoyed by basic questions. Breakfast was a disaster: cold eggs, burnt toast, and a server who forgot our coffee twice. The pool was packed with non-guests, and the gym had two broken treadmills. I've stayed at far nicer properties for half the price. This felt like a brand living on its reputation, not its reality. Really disappointed, especially given what we paid.

I am writing in regards to our stay April 22-24. We were celebrating our honeymoon and were disappointed with our stay. There was construction going on in the hotel and we were not notified of it prior to our stay. My husband had ordered champagne and strawberries for the room to be in there prior to our arrival...it wasn't. When he called to place the order again, it never showed up. We were so disappointed and surprised by the lack of service that we decided to forgo ordering them for a 3rd time. Our room was very small, drab and lacked the romantic setting we were looking for. We had called to request a room with a large tub, similar to the ones in the photos, prior to our arrival, noting that we didn't mind an upgrade cost. Instead, the tub was incredibly small. We have stayed at the Intercontinental in other cities before and had such high expectations for the Chicago location, especially considering we were celebrating such a happy, once-in-a-lifetime occasion. The service and amenities just didn't match up.
Sofitel's marble bathroom and deep tub felt genuinely upscale, and the room stayed impressively quiet at night. The central location made sightseeing easy, so the higher rate felt justified.

I really wanted to like this place, but the noise from the street was relentless all night and the AC kept rattling. The front desk was polite but couldn't offer a room change. For the price, I expected far better sleep quality and a bit more genuine hospitality.

Stayed here for a long weekend celebrating my partner's birthday, and honestly, we were both blown away. The guitar-shaped tower is iconic, of course, but the vibe inside is what really sets it apart. We had a club-level room with a strip view, and the sunset over the palm trees was unreal - totally worth the upgrade. The staff at check-in were super friendly, even though the lobby was packed, and they surprised us with a small cake and a handwritten note for the occasion. We spent most of our time by the main pool - it gets busy, but the DJ kept the energy up and the cabana service was quick. Cocktails were strong and pricey, but you expect that. Dinner at the Mexican spot on property was surprisingly solid. Location can't be beaten for easy access to the strip, but the soundproofing meant we slept like babies. Would definitely book again for a special trip.

I picked this hotel mainly for the location, and it didn't disappoint. Being right by the harbour made exploring the city on foot effortless, and the train station was a quick stroll away. The check-in was efficient, though I did have to wait a few minutes for a room to be ready, which was fine. My room had a fantastic view of the water, and the bed was incredibly comfortable - I slept like a log. The breakfast spread was substantial, with a great mix of local pastries and hot items. The only slight downside was the air conditioning being a bit noisy, but it wasn't a dealbreaker. Overall, a very solid, comfortable stay that I'd happily book again.

The vintage charm still feels fresh, and the staff's warm efficiency justified every penny. Waking up to the glittering skyline from our high floor was pure magic--a classic stay that quietly exceeds expectations.

My stay at the Ambassador was genuinely pleasant, and I left feeling like I'd gotten real value for the money. The room was spotless from top to bottom; I checked the corners and baseboards out of habit, and there wasn't a speck of dust anywhere. The bathroom was compact but smartly arranged, with a walk-in rain shower that had solid water pressure and thick, fluffy towels that actually dried you off. I'll admit the decor leans slightly retro--think warm woods and muted golds--but it's well-maintained and has a cozy, almost vintage charm rather than feeling tired or neglected. What impressed me most, though, was the sleep quality: the blackout curtains seal out all street light, and the mattress has that perfect firm-but-giving feel. I woke up once for water and fell right back asleep, which never happens at home. Service at check-in was quick and friendly, too. I'd happily book here again for a quiet, comfortable city break.

The hotel is in a good location. It is very contemporary in decoration. Beautiful flowers in lobby. The room service was very good. Concierge services were also very good. We were treated well. The shower water pressure was very poor. Also, at checkout our room bill was conveniently not available so they mailed it to us, which we were charged for the 3rd night when our room was actually prepaid. It was courteously taken care of after contacting hotel. Bar was very small and uninviting and there was very poor selection for appetizers/food. read more

I really wanted to love the Knickerbocker given its reputation, but our stay fell flat. The noise was relentless -- our room faced the street and the bar below kept us up past 2am both nights, with doors slamming in the hallway constantly. The wifi was spotty at best; it dropped every time I tried to join a video call, which was the whole reason I booked. The bathroom looked sleek in photos but in reality the shower tolled lukewarm and the drain gurgled ominously. As for the view, we paid extra for a 'city view' and got a wall of scaffolding with a sliver of brick. Staff were polite enough, but for this price I expected far more. Disappointing.

My wife and I stayed for 2 nights and loved it. Our stay was booked for us by Virgin Atlantic when we booked our flights from London to Chicago. We were not quite sure what to expect but were reassured by the Hilton brand name. In the event we found that the airline knew what they were doing when they suggested this hotel. On arrrival we got a warm welcome and the check in was quick and efficient. The interior of the hotel is spectacular and looks like has been refurbished to reflect the decor as it would have been when it was built. The room we were given was a good size with 1 Queen bed which was particularly comfortable. The hotel is conveniently located with restaurants nearby. The first night we ate at the hotel's own gourmet restaurant (The Lockwood) which did not disappoint. The breakfasts are also served in this restaurant. We had the buffet both mornings and these were good value for the quality offered. Generally we found the service in this hotel good and the staff very helpful. A nice touch was that when we checked out of the hotel to go to our next destination the car we had booked to pick us up was a few minutes late arriving. A member of staff supervising the doormen saw us looking a bit lost and came over to assist us find the car when it did arrive. Overall I would thoroughly recommend this hotel for both business and leisure stays for both quality and value for money.

The bathroom had peeling grout and a weak, lukewarm shower, and our room felt grimy with dust on the baseboards. The so-called 'city view' was a brick wall, while the faded carpets and 80s furniture made the whole place feel sadly neglected.
Our stay at the Fairmont was genuinely lovely, with a beautiful room, exceptionally comfortable bed, and warm, attentive service. The location made exploring easy, and we would happily return.

First let me say, the front office people at Hotel Monaco are wonderful and the location of the hotel was just what I'd hoped. There are some other problems; the furnishings are quite rundown, and housekeeping wasn't very helpful. We booked a suite and the sofa bed, chair and coffee table in the living room area had all had some very hard use. I've attached pictures, so you can see the considerable gap in the sofa and the lack of pillows. Comfortable it was not! The chair bottom is all broken down too. I invited one of the Assistant Managers to view our furniture, and a slight adjustment was made in our rate. As to housekeeping, we had ordered an in-room coffee service (which Kimpton's web site says is there, but you have to specifically request) and at no time did housekeeping leave us coffee. We had to call the front desk every day. And, housekeeping neglected our fish and on our next to last day we found it floating dead at the top of the fish bowl. I had requested water be added to the bowl when I noticed it going down and my note was disregarded. These things may not matter to you, but if you plan to spend a week, like we did, you might want to be comfortable. The bedroom and bathroom were superior; just the living room was bad.

Swissotel exceeded expectations--the corner room had stunning lake views and a ridiculously comfy bed. Breakfast was fresh and varied, and the staff remembered my name by day two. Location near the waterfront made evening strolls a breeze. Would happily return.

Beautiful lagoon views from our room made mornings feel special, and the decor felt pleasantly modern, not tired. Breakfast had fresh pastries and made-to-order eggs, easily justifying the price. A cozy, smart stay we'd repeat.
Homewood was a comfortable stay: the room was spotless, the bathroom fresh and well-kept, breakfast had plenty of hot choices, and the friendly staff made check-in easy.

Booked this for a work trip expecting the Omni name to mean something, but it felt more like a budget motel with a fancy lobby. The room was dated, the carpet had a suspicious sticky patch, and the A/C rattled all night, so the noise never let up. I paid over $200 and honestly, I've had better sleep in airport lounges. The 'complimentary breakfast' was a sad spread of powdered eggs and stale pastries, with coffee that tasted burnt. You'd think for that price they'd at least spring for real juice. Location was decent for the convention center--about a ten-minute walk--but that's the only saving grace. Between the thin walls, hallway chatter until 2 a.m., and the constant elevator dinging, I left more exhausted than I arrived. Definitely not worth the money, and I wouldn't return unless someone else was covering the bill.

I used to stay at the Homewood Suites all the time on business but have not stayed there on business since 2005 - since that time my company has been doing business in the suburbs instead of downtown. During December of 2007 and this year 2008 I did stay there a few days with my family and was greeted as if I never left. There is a lady named Connie who works the breakfast shift and she greets everyone and always remembers you from years before. A wonderful lady indeed - my wife even commented to me on the way to Chicago if that lady would still be there and would still remember and yes she does! Its a great place to stay.

I had a really pleasant stay at Affinia and would happily return. The location made it easy to get around, but the room was surprisingly quiet at night, which I appreciated after long days in the city. My room felt spacious for New York, with a comfortable bed, a small kitchenette area, and enough storage that I didn't have to live out of my suitcase. The front desk team was friendly and gave useful restaurant suggestions without being pushy. Housekeeping was consistent, and everything was clean and well maintained. The lobby has a relaxed, welcoming feel rather than the usual rushed hotel atmosphere. It's not ultra-luxury, but it was comfortable, convenient, and genuinely good value.

I had a very pleasant two-night stay at the Hilton. My room was on a higher floor, and the wide windows looked out over the city skyline; at night the lights made it worth lingering with a coffee before bed. The room itself was comfortable and quiet, with decor that felt fresh rather than overly trendy--warm wood accents, clean carpeting, and a useful desk. The bathroom was spotless, with good water pressure, plenty of counter space, and a large mirror that made getting ready easy. Everyone I encountered, from the front desk to housekeeping, was genuinely welcoming and quick to help with directions and a late checkout request. It felt reliably well run, and I would happily stay here again.
Breakfast had plenty of fresh options, and the updated decor gave the hotel a welcoming feel. Our room was spotless and comfortable; we only wished we could have stayed another night.

The room was spotless with a plush bed, and the marble bathroom felt luxurious. Despite being near the elevator, it was surprisingly quiet. Breakfast offered fresh pastries and made-to-order eggs--a perfect start. I'd happily return.

Swissotel was a really pleasant surprise. Check-in was quick even though we arrived early evening, and the staff gave us a clear rundown of the facilities without sounding rehearsed. Our room was spotless, quiet, and had a great city view; the bed was especially comfortable after a long day of walking. Breakfast had plenty of fresh options, from fruit and pastries to eggs made to order, and the coffee was better than expected for a hotel buffet. We also used the pool area, which was clean and relaxing, though it got a little busy around midday. The location made it easy to get around by taxi and on foot. I'd happily stay here again.

Our two nights flew by--I wished for one more lazy morning. The room stayed blissfully quiet despite downtown buzz, and the wifi never stumbled. Breakfast's scrambled eggs and fresh pastries hit the spot, making the whole stay feel effortless.
Loved our stay at the Hyatt. Room was spotless with a super comfy bed, and the front desk upgraded us just because we asked nicely. Location made getting around easy. Would happily book again.

The location is convenient, but the room felt tired and the hallway noise was relentless. The promised 'city view' was mostly a brick wall, and breakfast was a sad, lukewarm afterthought. Overall, this stay was a miss for the price.

I found this hotel in the 'Small Luxury Hotels of the World' booklet having stayed in many of these in recent years, and they were indeed above and beyond average hotels. I therefore chose it for a 4 night stay while visiting from England. The Talbott was excellently located, although i had a view of a building site, and did have an ambience and some charm, however it was a little dirty and faded around the edges and the service was appalling. I had to wait in the foyer well after check in time, having previously attempted to check in earlier, tired and in need of a rest, while a 'final check' was done to my room. The valet parking was not outside when requested, breakfast was not included in the price, all the things requested of reception did not occur, and there were very few touches which make a hotel stay special. I have stayed in hotels which are so much more elegant, where the staff and service are first rate for half the price of this hotel. I was severely disappointed and cannot recommend it at all.

This was a gorgeous hotel from the outside and in the lobby. However, when we reached the elevator things started to look quite dingy. Our bathrooms in our room had grout that was in need of a deep scrubbing and had an overall appearance of dirty. Wireless internet is available, but that's an additional fee. Are you kidding? Even the roach motel offers wireless for free! Also, the fitness room was available for only $15 per day. Wow, I thought the room rate was enough to cover that. When I used the coffee supplies in the room, they were not replenished. I called the next morning requesting more and was told that wasn't housekeeping's area but they would send some up. No kidding, nearly 90 minutes later I got the cream and sugar! Glad I wasn't in a big hurry. I'll definitely be staying next door for half the cost and a lot better accommodations the next time I'm in Chicago!

We stayed at the Intercontinental for three nights last weekend. It is a located in a fantastic spot on the Magnificent Mile, right near the Chicago River and the NBC building. We had a double room in the main tower. The room was very clean and updated. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The negatives about this hotel is that you have to pay extra to use the fitness centre and internet access. Also, parking is high ($45 valet/day). Overall, we had a great stay and would recommend this hotel. We paid $90 on Priceline and felt that this was a reasonable price.

At the last minute, my son and I decided to take a quick trip to Chicago to see the Cubs. After checking Priceline I decided to book the Omni because of the great price for airfare and hotel. We arrived at the hotel around noon and our room was ready(I had called ahead and requested early arrival).The front desk treated us like we were there best customers-very friendly and accomodating. The room was wonderful with all the modern conviences you would expect in an upscale hotel. The room was spotless and the bed was VERY comfortable. There was not one sign of bed bugs as mentioned in a previous review-maybe those bed bugs were from their luggage and were transferred into their room!!!We then went to the hotel restaurant and had lunch. Our service was great as was the food. We also tried several restaurants around the Omni-all within walking distance. The service, cleanliness and location of the Omni were incredible. We will definitely go back.

I expected more from an Omni, especially at this rate. The location was convenient, but almost everything else felt tired and poorly managed. Our room had a strong musty smell when we arrived, and the air conditioner rattled loudly enough to wake us during the night. I called the desk twice about it; someone eventually came up, looked at it for a minute, and said maintenance would check it later. They never did. The bathroom was not especially clean either, with hair around the tub and an empty tissue box. Check-in took forever despite only two people ahead of us, and the staff seemed more distracted than apologetic. For a supposedly upscale hotel, the worn furniture and lack of follow-through were really disappointing.

I had a very pleasant stay at Hotel Palmer. The lobby has a classic, slightly grand feel, but the service was relaxed and genuinely friendly rather than formal. My room was comfortable and quiet, with a good bed, plenty of storage, and a desk that made it easy to catch up on work. Everything was clean when I arrived, and the housekeeping staff did a nice job during the rest of my stay. I especially appreciated being able to walk to several restaurants, shops, and nearby attractions without needing a car. The elevators were busy around check-in, though they moved along quickly. Staff at the front desk were helpful with directions and a late checkout request. Overall, it was a convenient, comfortable stay, and I would happily book here again.

We stayed at the Homewood for four nights over spring break and it ended up being one of the better hotel experiences we've had in a while. The complimentary breakfast actually had variety every morning, not the same sad bagels on repeat, and my kids went crazy for the waffle maker. Our room had a full kitchen, which sounds like a small thing but meant we could heat up leftovers and keep drinks cold without trekking downstairs. The bed was genuinely comfortable, none of that thin lumpy mattress stuff. Housekeeping came promptly when we asked for extra towels, and the front desk guy at night gave us a solid tip about a taco spot two blocks over. Free parking was a bonus in an area where most places charge big. Would book again without hesitation.

The Fairmont turned a quick business trip into something genuinely special. The lake view from my room was stunning, and the staff remembered my name by day two. That level of care makes all the difference.

I expected more from the Omni given the rate and location. Our room looked tired, with scuffed furniture and a loud air conditioner that cycled on all night. The bathroom was especially disappointing: the grout around the tub was stained, the shower pressure was weak, and there was barely enough counter space for two toiletry bags. We faced an interior courtyard and the 'view' was mostly neighboring windows and rooftop equipment, so keeping the curtains open felt awkward. WiFi technically connected, but it dropped repeatedly and was too slow for a video call. We only stayed one night, yet the experience somehow felt longer because of the poor sleep and several small frustrations. Staff were polite, but not enough to make me want to return.

I had my wedding ceremony and reception at the Sofitel. It seems as though I had the same experience as 'Judy L.' I read her review and thought 'that's exactly what happened to me!' Here's what happened: The good news: The actual event was great. Most notably, the food was absolutely incredible; I think almost every one of our guests has raved to us about the food. The same goes for the cake, which was made by Take the Cake. The service by the waiters and other staff was also very good. The bad news: Michelle, the Director of Catering, honestly made my wedding planning process a nightmare. While we were negotiating the contract, she promptly responded to my emails and phone calls; after the contract was signed, it was a constant struggle to get in touch with her to get my questions answered, to schedule the tasting, etc. She frequently took over a week to respond to a simple email, and she occasionally never returned my email or phone call until I called her a second or third time. I assumed things would get better within the month--or even the week--prior to my wedding, but they actually got even worse. Michelle just could not get it together, and if it weren't for my wedding coordinator's assistance in forcing her to finally get things right, I don't know what would have happened. Thus, if it weren't for Michelle's inability to do her job, I would have had a great experience. But, as it is, when I think back about my experience with the Sofitel, I unfortunately have very negative thoughts. And that's incredibly disappointing, considering it was a major part of the best night of my life.

Booked the Hard Rock expecting rock-star treatment, but the room felt tired and the hallways were noisy all night. Staff seemed indifferent, and that 'vibe' didn't make up for a scratchy mattress. Left disappointed.

My stay at Hotel Monaco was exactly what I needed--stylish without being stuffy, and located just steps from everything I wanted to do. The check-in was quick, and the front desk clerk genuinely took time to mark up a map with her favorite local spots, which I appreciated way more than the usual scripted suggestions. The room itself was comfortable, with a surprisingly cozy bed and a bathroom that had plenty of hot water and counter space. I also liked the little extras, like the yoga mat and the complimentary wine hour in the lobby--it was a nice way to unwind after a long day of walking. The only tiny hiccup was the street noise at night, but it wasn't enough to ruin my sleep. All in all, I'd happily book here again for a weekend getaway.

I had a very pleasant stay at Hotel Ambassador and would happily return. The check-in process was quick and friendly, even though I arrived a little later than planned, and the staff at reception were helpful throughout the visit without being overbearing. My room was clean, quiet, and more spacious than expected, with a comfortable bed and a good shower. I especially appreciated the little details, such as plenty of outlets and reliable Wi-Fi. Breakfast had a nice variety, including fresh fruit, pastries, and hot dishes, and the dining area never felt rushed. The location was also convenient for getting around, with restaurants and public transportation nearby. A few furnishings looked slightly dated, but everything was well maintained and the overall experience was comfortable, relaxed, and good value.

We had a wonderful stay at Hotel Monaco. The room was spotless, with crisp white linens and a smell of fresh lemongrass the moment you walked in. The bathroom felt modern and luxurious, featuring a rainfall shower with excellent water pressure and plenty of fluffy towels. Our window faced the harbor, and watching the boats bob in the morning light was a genuine treat, even with the slight street noise. I was a bit worried the decor might feel old, but it's actually a clever mix of classic charm and updated touches--velvet chairs next to a sleek desk, that sort of thing. It felt thoughtful, not tired. The staff were all smiles, and the location made everything easy. Definitely a place I'd book again.
For the price, Fairmont was a letdown: our room smelled stale, the air conditioner rattled all night, and requests for extra towels took hours to arrive.

The Palmer's location on State Street is genuinely hard to beat for sightseeing, which is the only reason I'm giving it two stars instead of one. Unfortunately, that's where the positives end. Our room, advertised as recently renovated, looked tired and worn, with a suspicious stain on the carpet near the mini-fridge and a layer of dust on the headboard. The bathroom was the real letdown--the shower pressure was pitiful, the grout was discolored, and the provided toiletries smelled like cheap generic soap. Housekeeping did the bare minimum, leaving wet towels on the floor and not replacing the coffee. At $280 a night, this felt like a $90 motel experience dressed up in a fancy lobby. The location saved the trip, but the value simply wasn't there.

Absolutely loved my stay at Hotel Allegro. The location is unbeatable--right in the theater district, so we walked everywhere and never touched the car after parking. The lobby has this quirky, artsy vibe that feels more boutique than chain, and the staff genuinely seemed to enjoy their jobs. They upgraded us to a corner room with tall windows and a surprisingly comfy king bed; the pillows were perfect. Yes, the bathroom is small and the walls are a bit thin (we heard the elevator ding all night), but the nightly live jazz in the lounge more than made up for it. The blackout curtains worked wonders, and the in-room coffee was actually decent. For the price and location, this is a solid, character-filled pick--I'd book again in a heartbeat.

First of all, Expedia.com charged me for an additional person per my instructions but when I arrived at the Hotel these monies were not included and the complimentary breakfast was not offered. The Hotel service person who checked us in forgot to give me back my parking ticket but left a generic message for me stating that there was an envelope at the front desk. I had to wait in line for another 20 minutes to discover this the whole time this person was looking at me and never said a word!! I was charged and paid for parking adjacent to the Hotel. When we went to leave the gate would not open. We had to find the parking garage office and the Manager had to call several times over to the Hotel until finally someone picked up. They confirmed my payment and then we were allowed to leave the structure. The Hotel itself is beautiful!!! The bell hops and doormen were just wonderful. They were more than helpful and gracious but the internal staff were rude and not helpful at all!!!!

This hotel is trading on the Hilton name and although adequate the decor is dated and depressing. Although classed as a three star the prices do not reflect this. It was more expensive than other four star hotels in the neighbourhood, The breakfast is poor quality and the room very crowded. All in all the worst hotel we stayed at in a 14 day tour of Canada and the USA. Would not stay there again.
The room was wonderfully quiet, and our two-night stay felt far too short. The bathroom was spotless with a strong shower, while the city view made mornings especially enjoyable.

Booked a poolside room for the anniversary, but the thumping bass from the bar made sleep impossible. Staff shrugged off the noise complaints, and our 'city view' was a brick wall. Location's convenient, sure, but I'd rather stay anywhere else next time.

I am not much of a complainer, as you can see when reviewing my other posts on this site, but the Talbott provided such bad service that I feel the need to warn future travelers to Chicago: My girlfriend and I stayed at the Talbott for 2 nights in late July 2006. The first sign that something was wrong come during the initial booking of the room over the phone. The receptionist was outright rude, but took the reservation without a mistake. During our stay the hotel and restaurant staff was extraordinary incompetent, the waiters, the managers, nobody was friendly, nor tied to accommodate us. [------------------------] We and many others who stayed at the hotel attended a wedding reception close by and had arranged the hotel bar to remain open from 12-2 to have an after hour's party. The hotel manager had assured us that this was secured and done in the past upon such occasions. When we returned from the reception at 11:50pm the bar was closing and the night manager and hotel staff were very rude to me and my friends. 'Nobody told us, we can't do anything for you.' 'Are you sure that you arranged this?' Two quotes so typical for this hotel's staff that I know that I will never stay at this hotel again. I understand that mistakes are made and that communication can be difficult across different shifts in a hotel, but blaming the customer so being confused and failing to arrange what I know had been arranged for and was later confirmed by the day staff is too rude even for my taste.[-----]

Fairmont Hotels are generally my preferred choice, but this was a true disappointment. Check-in was quite slow and problematic (glitches with their reservation system locally). Room was very small and oddly arranged. Felt quite cramped in room and was hard to work at very small desk. Hotel overall felt quite cold and isolating...lobby is not at all inviting, and it didn't feel terribly safe walking around outside. Gift shop was overpriced, even for a downtown hotel. Food was disappointing. Overall this seems greatly overpriced and does not meet usual standards of A Fairmont i've come to count on. Bill was completely messed up and required 3 separate calls after i left to straighten out.

We stayed at the Knickerbocker for a long weekend and honestly expected much more for the price. Check-in took nearly forty minutes because they were 'short-staffed,' and the room wasn't ready until after 4pm even though we arrived at 2. The room itself was small and the street noise was relentless -- garbage trucks, sirens, everything -- despite requesting a quiet floor. Housekeeping skipped us entirely one day and we had to call twice for fresh towels. The rooftop bar looked appealing in photos but was so packed and overpriced ($22 for a mediocre cocktail) that we gave up after one round. Breakfast at the restaurant cost a fortune for cold eggs. Location is truly great, near Times Square but that's about the only upside. For $700 a night, I expected luxury, not excuses. Won't be back.

The staff were indifferent at best and the room felt tired, with a broken hairdryer and stained carpet. For these prices, I expected far more polish--definitely left feeling underwhelmed and overcharged.

I checked in at the Affinia Hotel in Chicago shortly after dinner on Tuesday, I was greeted by very frendly staff from the valet service to front desk. You can tell people were happy at the hotel. I was pleasantly surprised when I got to my room. The room was very well decorated and well thought out. The furniture was in the right location and there was lots of space. Plus it was convenient with lots of power outlets The bedroom and washroom was very clean and I had a great sleep in their very comfortable bed. I was told by front desk i could choose from 6 different pillows, although i did not take advantage of this offer i thought what a great idea. Once in a while you come across hotels with great service, well thought out rooms in a perfect location (right off Magnificent Mile). When visiting Chicago again I will definitely try and stay at Affinia again

This is a stunning hotel in an excellent location in the greatest of US cities. The entrance and lobby of the hotel indicates its class. The bedrooms are large and comfortable and the customer service is second to none. It is located on South Michigan directly across the road from Grant and Millenium Park. It also has a free shuttle to the Water Tower in the heart of the Magnificent Mile. For Blues fans, Buddy Guy's Legends Club is situated immediately behind the Hotel. Highly recommended.

The bathroom was spotless with excellent water pressure, and breakfast had plenty of hot and cold options. Staff were genuinely welcoming, and our room stayed tidy throughout. A very comfortable, hassle-free stay overall.

I expected much more from the Conrad given the rate and reputation. My room faced the street, and traffic, sirens, and late-night voices carried through the windows well past midnight. The breakfast looked polished but was underwhelming: lukewarm eggs, stale pastries, and coffee that tasted as if it had been sitting for hours. The bathroom was attractive at first glance, yet the shower pressure was weak, the drain backed up, and there was very little counter space for toiletries. Wi-Fi was another irritation; it repeatedly disconnected during a video call and was too slow to reliably work from the room. Staff were courteous when asked, but no one followed up on the problems. Overall, it felt more like an expensive inconvenience than a relaxing stay.

I wasn't sure what to expect from a downtown Omni, but this one surprised me in the best way. I slept like a rock--the blackout curtains actually worked, and the bed had that perfect balance of firm and plush. Breakfast downstairs was a cut above the usual hotel buffet; the omelet station was fast, and the fresh pastries were still warm. Honestly, I could have stayed another day just to lounge in the lobby with a coffee, but our schedule was packed. When I checked the bill, I felt the rate was justified, especially given the room size and the quiet despite being near all the action. It wasn't a bargain, but it wasn't a rip-off either. If you're on the fence, book it--just give yourself more time than we did. I left wishing we'd planned an extra night.
Staff were warm and efficient, the updated decor felt fresh without being flashy, and our room overlooked the park. The bathroom was spotless, with a roomy shower and great water pressure.

Stay Away! After generations as an old-world, cozy and stately, if a bit tired oasis, the AE has been purchased by Ian Schrager and taken down so many notches it's almost not functional. Allowing for the fact that the hotel is under renovation, the entrance is not handicapped accessible, and I saw several hotel guests with canes, casts, etc (including myself, recovering from foot surgery and in a cast, with a cane) struggling with the up and down outside stairs one has to navigate just to get into and out of the hotel. With luggage, it's almost impossible. This is simply inexcusable. I've been a customer of the Ambassador East for decades--but no more. The hallways are so dark one can barely see. The rooms are stark white, which in and of itself, isn't a particular problem, but it is jarring and almost painful as one's eyes adjust from the dark hallways. The furniture--stark and scant--looks like something from an Ikea closeout. The bed is comfortable--what a relief--but only about 15 inches off of the floor, a real problem if you're at all physically challenged, or even elderly and less flexible than you were in your salad days. The problems don't end there. My room had a horribly uncomfortable wire/metal desk chair, and absolutely nowhere else to sit. No arm chair, no demi-sofa, no ottoman. With a foot in a cast, it would have been nice to be able to sit comfortably, perhaps even with my leg elevated, while in the room. No way. The bathroom has absolutely nowhere to put any of your toiletries. Not a shelf, a small table, a nook, or a medicine cabinet. If you want to put a razor, shaving cream, makeup (for women) or anything else down so that you can use them, you're sh*t out of luck. Repeated requests for a small table or some sort of chair went unmet. A borrowed umbrella from the front desk was broken and unusable, something I didn't discover until caught in an expected downpour. I was tempted to throw it out, but remembered that they would charge me for it if I didn't return it, in spite of its total lack of usefulness. Refrigerator--forget it. Shampoo? For two days in a row, the housekeeper left several bottles of lotion, and no shampoo. Room service--not available. If you want breakfast, the front desk will sell you a small, pre-wrapped, commercial grade muffin for $4.00--something you can buy in any gas station for $1.00. No added value whatsoever. The photos show a nice entrance, and a large lobby for which the AE has long been famous. Unfortunately, that lobby is closed off, under construction, and the temporary lobby is on the second floor, difficult, again, for handicapped access. Thermos-bottled coffee and water for tea were stone cold, at 8 in the morning. When confronted with these various misses, the front desk staff repeatedly shrugged their shoulders and said, 'Yeah, we know, you're not the first to tell us this stuff.' All this shows is that Schrager doesn't even care to make an effort to make his guests comfortable, and that the staff is either too indifferent or too amateur to know the difference and even make an effort to get it right. It's one thing to get a good price on a hotel room when it's under renovation. It's another thing altogether to get screwed in the bargain, particularly after booking a non-refundable pre-paid reservation. Again, avoid this hotel like the plague.

After Leaving some important documents in the room, I called and asked for the lost and found department... SEVEN TIMES over the course of a week. Eventually I had enough and asked for a manager and was put on hold then disconnected. Finally , a deceivingly friendly operator PROMISED me she would have someone call me back in a few minutes, It never happened. So Avoid this place because after they rip you off once they'll keep doing it later. They cannot be trusted at their word

Fairmont Chicago delivers a classic, refined stay rather than cutting-edge style--the lobby's marble and warm wood feel timeless, not tired, and our room's furnishings were well-kept even if the palette leaned traditional. The Wi-Fi was rock solid throughout, easily handling video calls from the desk by the window. Breakfast in the main restaurant was a highlight: the made-to-order omelet bar was quick, and the fresh pastries and strong coffee set us up for a long day of sightseeing. Being steps from Millennium Park and a short walk to the Riverwalk made mornings effortless, and the doormen's transit tips saved us time. Staff were consistently courteous, and the pool was a bonus after a hot afternoon. A dependable, polished choice--I'd book again if returning to the Loop.

This is a great find for downtown Chicago. The price is right and the staff are excellent. As noted, there is construction going on around the hotel, but I didn't notice any issues that disturbed sleeping. I asked for a quiet room on an upper floor, and was gladly given one. The lobby is small, the atmosphere is that of a small boutique hotel. The concierge, Stephanie did a super job in finding us a restaurant and booking us reservations (along with a complimentary appetizer). We had a standard room, and it was spacious, tastefully decorated--everything we needed. The bathroom had a nice whirlpool tub for soaking--and the MP3 compatible radio was a nice perk. Just can't say enough about how nice the staff are--every single person you meet. Would definitely stay here again.
The room was spotless, and the bathroom felt modern and well-maintained. Our stay was too short to enjoy everything, but the comfort and service made it feel worth the price.

The view was a dreary brick wall, and the constant hallway noise made rest impossible. Though central, the staff's indifference soured the convenience, leaving me feeling utterly let down by this Intercontinental stay.

My room at Hotel James was the perfect mix of style and comfort--loved the dark wood accents and the plush bed. Staff were friendly without hovering, and the location made exploring downtown a breeze.

We stayed at the Hilton for a long weekend to celebrate our anniversary and honestly couldn't have asked for a better experience. Check-in was quick and the front desk agent even sent a small plate of chocolates up to our room when she learned the occasion, which was a genuinely thoughtful touch. The room itself was spacious, spotless, and had a surprisingly comfortable bed, a real highlight since hotel beds usually leave us sore. Housekeeping was consistent without being intrusive. The executive lounge breakfast had a nice spread, and the omelet station was excellent. Location was convenient, a short walk to plenty of restaurants. Only minor gripe: the pool got crowded Saturday afternoon. Overall, wonderful stay, friendly staff, and we'd absolutely return for our next trip. Highly recommend this property.

The location of this hotel is excellent. The hotel itself is not a 4 star like they say - in my opinion. The room decor is horrible (probably more European than I am used to) and the room is small and furnished like an old apartment. On the upside, if you want to stay in a great location, feel safe, and can put up with some aesthetic issues and can get a great deal then this will work. I prefer Westin or Marriott...something that you can count on.

I was disappointed by my stay at the Ambassador. The lobby has some attractive old details, but the guest room looked tired, with worn carpet, scuffed furniture, and curtains that had clearly seen better days. My window faced a neighboring wall and a noisy alley, so there was barely any daylight and no worthwhile view. The staff were polite enough at check-in, though not especially welcoming, and my request for extra towels took two calls and nearly an hour. The bathroom was the biggest letdown: it was clean but cramped, with dated fixtures, weak water pressure, and grout that needed attention. The bed was reasonably comfortable, but that alone did not justify the price. I expected more care and upkeep from a hotel with this reputation.
Affinia looked tired, and our room smelled musty despite being 'upgraded.' The elevator was painfully slow, the Wi-Fi kept dropping, and the front desk barely acknowledged our complaints.

The view from our room was absolutely stunning, overlooking the city skyline, and the decor felt fresh and modern. Breakfast offered a great spread, and given the quality throughout, it felt well worth the price.
Our room at the Fairmont was spotless and the marble bathroom felt genuinely luxurious. Honestly, the weekend flew by too quickly. Pricey, yes, but for this level of comfort it was worth every penny.
The city view was disappointing, and although the Fairmont's location was convenient, loud hallway noise ruined the stay. Staff remained polite but seemed indifferent when we raised concerns.
InterContinental was a great choice for our weekend--quiet room, comfortable bed, and genuinely warm service. The concierge pointed us to an excellent nearby breakfast spot, too.

We booked the Knickerbocker for a quick anniversary getaway, and honestly, it was over far too soon. The room was spotless--crisp white linens, gleaming bathroom fixtures, and not a speck of dust on the windowsill overlooking the bustling street below. I slept like a log, thanks to the blackout curtains and the surprisingly plush mattress that cradled my back after a long day of walking. The bed was so comfortable I almost wanted to extend our stay, but the weekend flew by. Given the prime location and the attentive staff who remembered our name each morning, it felt worth every penny. My only regret is not booking a third night.
The James felt polished without being stuffy; our room was quiet, the bed was excellent, and the front desk pointed us to a great late-night spot nearby.

I wanted to like Hotel Palmer because the location was convenient, but the stay felt neglected from the moment we arrived. Check-in took nearly 25 minutes even though there was only one person ahead of us, and our room wasn't ready at the promised time. The carpet in the hallway smelled damp, and the room itself had scuffed furniture, a noisy air conditioner, and thin walls that made it impossible to sleep through the late-night conversations next door. The shower pressure was weak and the bathroom door wouldn't close properly. I mentioned the noise and maintenance issues to the front desk, but got a polite apology with no real solution. For the price, I expected a cleaner, more comfortable experience.

Disappointing stay--staff seemed indifferent, and for this price I expected far more attention. The constant hallway noise made it feel endless, yet somehow our short night passed without any real comfort. Not worth the splurge.

Over all, my trip was great; I got to spend time with my best friend. We did some shopping and site seeing. Trip was overall great. The only thing was our hotel stay was not up to speed with other luxury hotels I have stayed at. Some of the walls had wall paper missing, most of the faucets leaked, there was water stains on the ceiling in the bathrooms, some of the furniture had very visible stains, the fire alarm was coming off the wall in the main bedroom. we stayed in the corner suite on the 37 floor room 3711. Considering what ones pays for the room you would think the pool would be free and they would not charge for every single small amenity. I do not plan on staying there again. Apart from the trip was great![]

We stayed here because of all the great reviews, and it's all true. We were highly impressed with the high quality of everything, everyone, and the location. Walking distance to much of what Chicago has to offer. Gibson's steakhouse and the Hancock building to name a couple. This hotel should really be in the top ten or even top five hotels for Chicago. It should also have more than three stars. I mean three stars is for the hilton garden inn or marriott courtyard, and this place far exceeds chain hotels like those. Depending on the room you get, any price under $250 would be a good deal. Between 250 - 300 could still be worth it.

I had a very comfortable three-night stay at the Conrad. The check-in process was quick, and the front desk staff were welcoming without being overly formal. My room was spotless, quiet, and thoughtfully laid out, with a genuinely comfortable bed, plenty of outlets, and a large bathroom with excellent water pressure. I especially appreciated the small touches, like the good quality coffee and the evening housekeeping service. The hotel's central location made it easy to get around, and I could walk to several restaurants and shops. I also used the fitness center, which was bright and better equipped than expected. Breakfast was a little expensive, but the food was well prepared and the service was attentive. Overall, it felt polished but still relaxed, and I would happily stay here again.

IMO the Amalfi doesnt come close to justifying the glowing comments on TA. This is basically a Holiday Inn. Half of the rooms overlook an alley / loading dock. The hotel is not more than 6 or 7 flors high and the garbage pick up woke me up daily at 5 am. At 530, when you are just nodding off again, they begin setting up for the complimentary breakfast. This is a continental buffet on every floor next to the elevator bank. Any room within 100 feet of the elevators will hear the noise. Reception was a bit tacky and the 'staff' was a little rough around the edges. I didn't see a single business travellers while I was there. Valet parking was expensive (usual for Chicago) but was very slow. Just ok. Explore other options.

My family booked five nitghts at the Omni Chicago for our upcoming spring break. We took advantage of a pre-paid, non-cancellable offer. We subsequently received a 'Bed & Breakfast' offer via email and immediately called the hotel to inquire whether we could switch our reservation (same dates, different offer). We called the 800' number and the customer services representative was so obnoxiously condescending and ignorant, we simply hung up. We had been looking forward to our vacation, but now I am not sure I made the right choice with this hotel. I should have paid closer attention to the reviews - the Ritz, the Four Seasons, and the Peninsula would have never treated us this way. I will post again after our stay on April 17th.

I had a wonderful two-night stay at the Fairmont for a quick city break. The lobby felt elegant without being stuffy, and the front desk team had us checked in quickly despite a busy afternoon. Our room was bright, exceptionally clean, and had a comfortable chair by the window that became my favorite spot for morning coffee. Wi-Fi connected immediately and was reliable enough for a video call and streaming in the evening. I slept extremely well on the plush bed; even though we were near the elevators, the room stayed remarkably quiet overnight. Breakfast was fresh and service was attentive without hovering. My only complaint is that the trip felt far too short--I would happily return and give myself another day to enjoy the hotel.

We stayed at the Hotel Monaco for three nights and honestly wished it could have been a full week. The room was spotless when we checked in, and housekeeping kept it that way throughout our visit, which is not something we say often. The bed was genuinely comfortable, and between the quiet hallway and the blackout curtains, I slept better than I do at home. Breakfast was a highlight each morning: fresh pastries, good coffee, and eggs that were actually hot instead of sitting under a heat lamp. The staff greeted us by name by the second day. Location is walkable to plenty of restaurants and shops. We left feeling rested and well taken care of, and we will absolutely be back next time we're in town. Highly recommend.
Hyatt made our weekend easy: spotless room, friendly front desk, and a surprisingly quiet floor despite the busy lobby. Breakfast was fresh, and checkout took less than a minute.

This is a superb hotel. The rooms are huge, including a luxurious bathroom. It is clean and service is first rate. Breakfast was excellent (and complimentary for Hilton Honors members). Hotel is in a good location, and is connected to a mall, which I imagine would be a great asset in the Chicago winter. Next time I go to Chicago, I will stay here for sure.

Disappointing stay at Affinia: the Wi‐Fi kept dropping, the bathroom was dated and cramped, and breakfast was bland and overpriced. The location was convenient, but not enough to offset everything else.

I had a very pleasant stay at the Fairmont and would happily return. The location was incredibly convenient, with restaurants, shops, and public transportation all within an easy walk, while the hotel itself still felt calm and welcoming. My room overlooked the city skyline, and watching the lights come on in the evening was a real highlight. The decor has a few traditional touches, but it felt well maintained and elegant rather than outdated; the lobby in particular was fresh and beautifully presented. Wi-Fi connected quickly and remained reliable for video calls and streaming throughout my stay. Staff were courteous without being intrusive, and check-in was smooth. The bed was exceptionally comfortable, and the room was quiet despite the central location. Overall, it offered the polished service and relaxed atmosphere I was hoping for.

We had a really fun weekend at Hard Rock. The lobby has the music-and-memorabilia vibe you expect, but it never felt overdone, and the front desk team got us checked in quickly despite a busy Friday evening. Our room was spotless, comfortable, and surprisingly quiet once the door was closed. The bed was excellent, and I appreciated having enough outlets and counter space to actually unpack a little. We grabbed drinks at the bar one night and the bartender was friendly without rushing us. Location was also convenient for walking to restaurants and nearby attractions. The pool area got crowded in the afternoon, so go earlier if you want a lounger, but that was the only small downside. I'd happily stay here again.
My weekend at the Conrad went by far too quickly. I slept deeply in the quiet, plush bed, and the fresh decor and roomy marble bathroom made the stay feel especially polished.

Nestled just off the beaten path and about two blocks from the river the Fairmont Chicago offers an excellent location to operate as home base for your trip to Chicago. The staff were friendly and helpful, arranging many of the sightseeing events we enjoyed while in the city. There are many attractions withiin easy walking distance (The Art Institute is a must see and Millenium Park is a fun visit). The architectural tour by river departs a dock that is very close to the Fairmont and there are lots of restaurants nearby. The rooms were excellent and the club room is worth the extra expense. We would definitely stay here again.
Homewood was a great pick for our weekend--room was spacious, breakfast had plenty of options, and the staff handled our late check-in with a smile.

I have to admit, I was a little worried the Sheraton would feel dated, but my corner room was spotless and surprisingly modern. The carpet looked fresh, the bathroom grout was pristine, and the blackout curtains worked perfectly. My only real complaint is that I booked a two-night stay and it simply flew by--I could have easily used a third day just to lounge in that ridiculously comfortable bed. Breakfast downstairs was a pleasant surprise, with made-to-order omelets and proper barista coffee, far above the usual hotel buffet mush. Given the location, the lovely pool, and the overall polish, it genuinely felt worth every penny. I left already checking dates for my next visit.

I had a very comfortable stay at the InterContinental and would happily book it again. The lobby has an impressive old-world feel, but the service was warm rather than formal or stiff. Check-in was quick, and the front desk arranged a late checkout without making it complicated. My room was quiet, with a genuinely comfortable bed, plenty of storage, and a good desk for catching up on email. I especially liked the large windows and the well-maintained bathroom, although the shower took a minute to get to the right temperature. The location made it easy to walk to restaurants, shops, and nearby attractions, and the fitness center was better equipped than expected. A small coffee shop in the building was also convenient on busy mornings. Overall, polished, relaxing, and worth the rate.

I stayed in this hotel for 5 days in November together with my colleagues. Internet only wired available for 20 additional dollars a day. No fridge or microwave included in the price. Our room had two too soft full size beds. In the hall way the wallpaper had come off the wall. Who doesnt believe it, check out the 16th floor close to room 212. With discount we paid more than 300 dollars a night which is ridiculous. I stayed in the Hyatt Regency before for much cheaper and that was way better. The restaurant in the main hall is very nice and the food is tasty, but although being almost the only customer it took forever that the food got served. please stay away and take one of the plenty alternatives nearby.

I really wanted to like the Ambassador, but our stay was a letdown from start to finish. Check-in took nearly half an hour because the front desk was staffed by one visibly overwhelmed clerk. The room itself was dated, with a sagging mattress, a wobbly desk chair, and an air conditioning unit that rattled loudly every time it kicked on. We asked three times about the AC before anyone came up, and even then the fix lasted a day. Housekeeping skipped our floor one afternoon entirely. The location is decent, I'll grant that, and the morning coffee in the lobby was fine, but for this price I expected far more. The hallways smelled musty, and our window faced a brick wall. We won't be returning.

The Hard Rock didn't just meet expectations--it shattered them. The room was surprisingly quiet despite the lively lobby, the bed was heavenly, and the staff remembered my name every single morning. Perfect spot for exploring downtown, and the pool scene was a vibe.

They allowed parties to go on all night and booked us in a room with no running water. We called security twice for them to do nothing about the party. When they finally came up about 30 people filed out of that room only to file right back in after about 10 minutes. When we called back nothing was done about it. My 2 year old son was awaken by all the loud music and cursing. THEN we get up the next morning at 7:30 to get ready only to find that we have no running water. After the maintenance man piddles around with it for a half hour we have no time to shower and have to ride the two hour train ride dirty and tired from no sleep. They did not resolve this issue. They just keep passing my complaint to 'managers' supposedly. It was the worst stay of my life and my poor two year old had to be there for it

Breakfast was a lovely spread of fresh pastries and made-to-order eggs, well worth every penny. The room felt so cozy that my one night here flew by, though the reliable Wi-Fi kept me connected for late work.
